components.name: End screen
components.job: The last 10-20 s of a long-form video: slots where YouTube places its end-screen elements, over a looping background.
components.summary:
The last 10-20 s of a long-form GTA video: a held card with slots where YouTube places its end-screen elements (two video
elements and the subscribe element), a big "WATCH THIS NEXT" and a hand-drawn arrow, over the video's last shot. Long-form
YouTube (16:9). Put it on the last 6-20 s of the edit and line up YouTube Studio's end-screen elements with the slots.

- `a/index.html`, **Two slots + subscribe:** blurred bed, two 16:9 slots + round subscribe slot, the arrow picks slot 2.
- `b/index.html`, **Watch this next:** darkened drifting last shot, one big slot, avatar in a subscribe ring with a pill, the
  arrow lands and the slot powers on.

The slots, ring and title are real Three.js geometry (`media/es3d.js`: chrome bezels, extruded bevelled Archivo letters,
PMREM studio light). Screens and avatar are DOM layers posed to match the 3D camera exactly.

- `slots[]`: screen rects `{cx, cy, w, h}` in px. Keep 16:9 and match the YouTube element you place there.

- `subscribe`: ring centre, avatar radius `r`, `ring` width, colour, pill `label` and `pillY`.

- `arrow`: Bezier points `p` (start, two controls, head base), width profile, head size, `fill`, `outline`.

components.name: Word captions
components.job: Burned-in captions, one word or short phrase at a time, keyword in colour. Top in both formats.
components.summary:
Burned-in commentary captions in the style of top GTA 5 / GTA Online creators: one word or a short phrase at a time, in heavy caps with one ink edge around the face and a graded extrusion, over a soft contact shadow. Every word is timed to the voice-over from CONFIG start times. It drops in with a squash, motion blur and a spring, and swaps with a hard cut (no fades).

- **Gold keywords** are bevelled: a top-edge highlight, a curved 3-stop face, a warm seam and an extrusion with a lit lip. In A they catch fire from white to gold behind a feathered hot-white light front when spoken.
- **The payoff word is real 3D** (Three.js): extruded, bevelled letters traced from the caption font. They land white, turn to polished gold as the light front crosses, take a raking key light, one wide specular sweep and bloom, and stay wrapped in the same ink edge. Then they snap out.

| Variant | File | Canvas | When a creator uses it |
|---|---|---|---|
| A, Long-form | `a/index.html` | 1920x1080, 6.5 s | YouTube commentary or gameplay videos. 1-3 word groups, bottom-centre (cap centre at y 885, 82%). Inter 900 caps at 100 px, payoff at 150 px. |
| B, Shorts | `b/index.html` | 1080x1920, 5.9 s | Shorts / TikTok / Reels. One word at a time in narrow heavy caps (Archivo 64% width, 900), cap centre at y 1240, auto-fitted inside the safe zone. Hit words land gold and bigger. |

Files: `index.html`, plus in `media/` the payoff renderer `payoff3d.js` (identical in a/ and b/), the font outlines `glyphs.js`, and `gen-glyphs.js`, which regenerates them.
components.configDocs:
Edit only the `const CONFIG` at the top of each file.

### Text and timing
- **`words`**: `[{ w, t, g, hot, pay, ignite }]`. Fields:
  - `w`: the word as displayed (punctuation included).
  - `t`: the second it is spoken.
  - `g: 1` (A only): starts a new caption group.
  - `hot: 1`: a keyword. In A it arrives white and catches fire to gold at `t`. In B it lands already gold.
  - `pay: 1`: the payoff word, rendered in 3D. It lands white at `t`.
  - `ignite`: the second the payoff turns gold. Put it on, or just before, the big moment in your clip, so the gold reads before any white-out.

  To time words, paste a transcript's word timestamps here (for example from `npx hyperframes transcribe voice.wav`).
- **`lastOut`**: when the payoff starts its 5-frame snap-out exit. **`end`**: the composition length. Keep this in step with `data-duration` on `#root`.

### Type
- **`type.family / weight / size`**: the face and its size in px.
- **`type.paySize`** (A, a multiplier) and **`type.hotSize / paySize`** (B, px).
- **`type.maxWidth`** (B): DOM words auto-fit to this width. 690 keeps the landing squash inside the 9:16 safe zone (x 72-936).
- **`type.payMaxInk`** (B): the ink-width cap for the 3D payoff. The payoff is optically centred, with any trailing period hanging outside the centre.
- **`type.capCentreY`**: the vertical position of the caption, as the y of its cap-height centre.
- **`type.edge`**: the visible outer ink edge in px. It wraps the face and the extrusion as one block, in DOM and 3D alike.
- **`type.rim`**: the thin line between face and side, in px. It is ink on white words and the warm seam on gold.
- **`type.depth`** (and **`type.hotDepth`** in B): the DOM extrusion in px.
- **`type.ink`**: the edge colour.
- **`type.tracking`** and **`type.wordGap`** (A): spacing in em.
- **`type.tilt`** (B): the entry tilt in degrees, which springs to 0.

### The 3D payoff
- **`payoff3d.depth`**: the extrusion in px.
- **`payoff3d.bevel`**: the bevel in px.
- **`payoff3d.tilt`**: how far the top leans back, in radians, which shows the extrusion below the face.
- **`payoff3d.shade`**: the opacity of the soft local shade behind the word.

### Colour and footage
- **`colors.face`**: the white face's stops: top, mid, pre-shade, baseline.
- **`colors.side`**: the white words' extrusion, from near to far.
- **`colors.goldFace`**: the gold face's top, middle and bottom.
- **`colors.goldLip`**: the lit 1 px lip at the top of the gold extrusion.
- **`colors.goldSide`**: the gold extrusion, from near to far.
- **`colors.seam`**: the warm seam on gold.
- **`colors.hot`**: the hot-white light front.
- **`colors.glow`**: the warm bloom.
- **`shots`**: the `<video>` ids that get a slow push.
- **`grade`** (A): a CSS filter for a shot's wrapper (the parachute plate is lifted with `contrast(1.15) saturate(1.25)`).

### Changing the payoff word or font
`media/glyphs.js` holds outlines for A–Z, 0–9 and `. , ' ! ? -`, so any payoff word made of those characters works with no rebuild. For a different font, run `gen-glyphs.js` (instructions at its top; it needs `fontkit`).

components.name: Hit transitions
components.job: Cuts with impact: flash, whip blur, shake hit, zoom-through, dip to black.
components.summary:
The cuts GTA editors throw between clips: whip pans, zoom punches, speed-line shake hits, VHS colour-bar tears, flash hits and dips to black. These are full-frame footage treatments, not overlays. Every top GTA channel (long-form and Shorts) cuts with some of these. This pack does them the way a motion designer would: the whip blur comes from the image's real velocity; from the zoom on, a WebGL pass draws each frame from the footage itself, with a true radial shutter blur (48 jittered taps, sharp centre, streaking edges), light added from the footage's own highlights (threshold bloom, highlight-only exposure) instead of a grey veil, a real VHS signal model, and a luma dip where the shadows go first.

- **Variant A, `a/index.html` (16:9, 1920x1080, 7.2 s, "Transition pack").** Long-form. Whip pan 1.40, zoom-through punch 2.80, speed-line shake hit 4.20 (the payoff: lines rush inward over the outgoing shot, converge on the cut over an explosion, burst outward; warm core, bloom, shake), luma dip to black 4.90 with a hold on black and a highlights-first rise into the yacht on the beat at 5.60.
- **Variant B, `b/index.html` (9:16, 1080x1920, 7.07 s, "Vertical pack").** Shorts / TikTok. Slide-split 1.40 (three slabs with motion blur, cast and contact shadows and lit edges, then a lock-in kick), VHS colour-bar tear 2.80, zoom-through punch 4.20 (the Deluxo rushes the lens, the glass tower lands out of it), flash hit 5.40 (the payoff: the tower's own sun glare blooms into the cut under a radial suck-in; on the bridge's first 3 frames a hard exposure punch: the skyline's tall tower goes white-hot with a tight bloom, the lit steel and sunlit concrete go near-white, the shadows go deeper and the sky is held (and deepened) by a skyline matte, under a 1.38 back.out punch and a 52 px shake; it releases in about 0.2 s, then a 1.37 s settled hold).

A's cuts sit on a 1.4 s beat grid; B's last cut comes 0.2 s early so the pack accelerates into the payoff. Retime by moving the `CONFIG` times and clip windows together.
components.configDocs:
All tuning is in `const CONFIG` at the top of each file's script.
- `end`: the comp length in seconds. `shots`: the shot names, for reference (the `<video>` tags hold the real `src`).
- A, `whip`: `at`, `dur`, `maxBlur`, `blurPerPx`, `swell`, `tilt`, `lift`, `streak`, `chroma`/`chromaMax`.
- A and B, `zoom`: `at`, `outDur`/`outTo` (outgoing accelerates to this scale), `inDur`/`inFrom` (incoming lands from this scale), `shutter`, `taps` (radial blur samples), `lens` (barrel warp at the cut), `lensIn`, `chroma` (edge chroma px), `contrast`, `edgeDark`, `bloom`.
- A, `hit`: `at`, `center` (where the lines converge, canvas px), `suck`/`suckTo`/`suckShutter`/`suckVig`/`inhale` (the pre-hit suck-in), `lines` (count), `rush` (pre-cut frames: inner radius, alpha), `burst` (post-cut frames: inner radius, alpha, width), `core`/`coreA`/`coreHold`/`coreDecay`, `punchFrom`/`rest`/`punchDur`/`punchShutter`, `shakeDur`/`ampX`/`ampY`/`rot`/`shakeBlur`, `lift`/`key`/`warm`/`hold`/`decay` (warm highlight-only exposure), `chroma`/`chromaDur`, `bloom`, `hitVig`.
- A, `dip`: `outAt`/`out` (luma crush), `riseAt`/`rise` (highlights-first rise; the gap is the hold on black), `settleFrom`/`settle`.
- B, `split`: `starts`, `dur`, `dirs`, `maxBlur`, `blurPerPx`, `shadow`, `drop`, `rim`/`rimH`, `lock` (lock-in time), `kick`, `tick`, `recede`, `pushEnd`.
- B, `vhs`: `start` and `frames`, one entry per frame: `a` main signal ("a" outgoing, "b" incoming, "bars"), `b` + `mix` rows ripped in from a second signal, `jit` line jitter, `sine` travelling tear, `tear` block tears, `noise`, `bleed`/`off` chroma bleed and offset, `trackY`/`trackA` tracking-noise bar, `scan` scanlines.
- B, `flash`: `at`, `build`/`buildGain`/`buildLift`/`buildBloom`/`buildTh`/`buildShutter`/`suckTo` (the build on the outgoing shot), `gain` (the peak exposure gain on the core), `hot` (the light core: source-px centre x, y and radii x, y on the end shot; aim it at your subject) / `hotFall`, `floor`/`floorR`/`floorV` (the share of the gain the rest of the frame takes, falling off from the core over the `floorR` source-px radii; `floorV` = [y0, y1, share]: above y0 only that share, so skyline buildings stay textured), `toe` (luma range below which no gain applies, so blacks stay black), `zone`/`archY`/`ownKey` (where the sky is keyed per pixel instead of by the matte: left of `zone` x, for a foreground that moves against the sky), `skyDim`/`sat` (the sky deepens slightly at the peak), `lift`/`key`/`warm`/`contrast` (highlight lift and warmth on the core, extra contrast), `hold`/`peak` (peak frames and their levels), `decay` (release), `bloom`/`bloomTh`/`skyRej`/`bloomStep` (threshold bloom off the lit core), `knee` (filmic shoulder), `centre` (the point the punch scales about, canvas px), `punchFrom`/`rest`/`punchDur`/`punchEase`/`punchShutter`/`push`, `shakeDur`/`ampX`/`ampY`/`rot`/`shakeBlur` (clamped inside the punch's overscan), `chroma`/`chromaDur`. `SKYLINE` (after CONFIG) is the end shot's skyline matte: run-lengths of [columns, skyline y] in source px. If you swap `s5`, re-roto it (or set `flash.hot` z to 0 to switch the keyed flash off).

variants.kindEvidence: Full-kind component: the transitions are treatments of the footage, so bg "none" keeps the footage

notes.zoom: zoom-through: true radial shutter blur (48 jittered taps between this frame's scale and the previous one), barrel lens, edge chroma
notes.hit: speed-line hit (payoff): lines rush inward over the outgoing bridge, converge on the cut, then burst outward over the explosion
notes.dip: luma dip: shadows go first and the fire dies last; hold on black; the yacht rises highlights-first on the beat

variants.label: Vertical pack
variants.kindEvidence: Full-kind component: the transitions are treatments of the footage, so bg "none" keeps the footage

notes.vhs: VHS colour-bar tear, one entry per frame from `start`: a = main signal ("a" yacht, "b" Deluxo, "bars"), b + mix = rows ripped in from a second signal, jit = line jitter px, sine = travelling wave tear px, tear = block tear px, noise, bleed/off = chroma bleed step and offset px, trackY/trackA = tracking-noise bar, scan = scanline depth. The Deluxo lands on the beat (2.80).
notes.flash: flash hit (payoff). Build (last `build` s of the tower): the sun's own glare sliding across the tower's lower glass blooms (threshold `buildTh`) and lifts under a radial suck-in, a fast attack that stays below the peak. Hit (the cut): a camera exposure punch keyed to the skyline's tall tower, in source px so it rides the punch and shake: `hot` (centre xy, radii xy, Gaussian `hotFall`) is the crown core, which takes the full `gain`, a highlight lift, warmth and a bloom keyed off it alone; the rest of the frame takes `floor` of the gain, falling off from the tower over `floorR`, capped to `floorV`[2] on the skyline buildings (above source y `floorV`[0..1]) and pinned at the `toe`, so blacks get none; the sky is held by the SKYLINE matte (and keyed per pixel left of `zone` x, where the bridge arch moves against the sky), deepened by `skyDim` at the peak. Peak on the cut frame (`peak` per frame for `hold` frames), then a clean `decay`, under a back.out punch about `centre` (so the crown stays in frame), a shake clamped inside the overscan and a 3 px chroma split. A bright core with a fast falloff, never a veil.

notes.lines: Title lines, top to bottom. Each line is justified to the same ink width (a poster lockup), so shorter lines set bigger.
notes.tracking: extra letter spacing in font units (cap height = 688)
notes.kicker: the credit line in the bottom letterbox bar ("" to hide)
notes.face: Material: the blue anodised face (top -> bottom gradient) and the polished gold bevel / walls.
notes.shots: Footage (assets/shots or your own clip). Cuts are mirrored on the <video> tags above. "glow" is the light behind the title (and its rim light) while that shot plays: pick it from the shot's own light so it never fights the plate.
notes.faceReflect: how strongly the playing shot reflects in the blue faces
notes.rake: the payoff light raked across the bevels on the landing
notes.bloom: HDR bloom on the hot metal (the bevel glint)

notes.lines: The stack, top to bottom. "window" lines show the footage through hollow letters, "solid" lines are the red slab. Every line is justified to the same ink width, so short words set huge (a poster lockup).
notes.width: ink width of every line, px. The hold grows it 5% and the payoff steps it up 7% (to about 840 px); the step's overshoot peaks near 850 px, so even the transient frames stay inside x 72-936.
notes.grow: slow scale-up while the lockup holds (sine.inOut, 0.5-2.9 s)
notes.frame: The window letters: hollow channel letters. "lip" is the hard chamfer (as a share of the line's cap height, clamped to px), "depth" the walls (share of cap height). "color" is the frame metal; "tint" on each shot lights the walls inside the letter.
notes.slab: The solid line: a chiselled red slab in clear-coated lacquer (it reflects a studio: an overhead softbox, a strip light in front, a vertical strip at the left). "front" is the paint; wallPx is how tall its lower wall shows, chamferPx its chamfer, tilt (degrees) leans it back so the top chamfer faces the key. top / low / wall are the 2D fallback's.
notes.light: One light rig for all the letters (strengths): a raking key from the upper left, a top light, a fill. The chrome lips get their own key, lower and further left, and a weak top light, so their top chamfers rest at a bright grey (headroom for the payoff band) while the left chamfers go white and the right / lower ones dark.
notes.shots: Footage: the native 16:9 shots at 1:1 behind the window words. "frame" is the source pixel at the centre of the window block (LOS + SANTOS together). "cover" is the source x the full-frame crop centres on after the open. "tint" is the shot's light on the walls inside the letters. "grade" overrides windowGrade for that shot; its "roll" (0-1) is a warm highlight roll-off: clipped white (a sun disc) rolls into the sky's own orange, so no letter goes white. It eases out as the letters open. Mirror cut times on the <video> tags.
notes.windowGrade: inside the letters; eases to neutral as they open
notes.beats: The beats on the cuts. punch: a transient kick that settles back; step: a state change, the lockup steps up and stays (back.out(2.6) over 0.28 s); rake: the strength of one soft specular band (bandPx wide, feathered) that runs left to right along the top chamfers in rakeDur s, peak held 3 frames; slabLag: STORIES lands that many seconds after the window words (with a 0.9 -> 1 squash); shake: px.
notes.band: the payoff band: px wide at half height, dur s to cross; slant: it leans so it crosses LOS, then SANTOS, then STORIES; peak: [from, to] s at full strength; bloom: the chrome lips' glow (radius px, thresholded on the facets)
notes.drift: the hold's light: a broad, soft specular drift across the chrome lips (start, seconds, strength, px wide)
notes.openOn: the letter the camera flies into when the title opens (first match in a window line)
notes.open: blurPx: the zoom-blur streak on the stem's edges in the push-through; liftEV: the 2-frame stem exposure lift; cover: the cut comes once the stem's opening covers this share of the frame width

components.name: Facecam frame
components.job: The webcam box over gameplay.
components.summary:
The webcam box over gameplay, the most common layout in GTA streams-turned-videos. Two variants, each its own HyperFrames
project:

- **a/ Corner cam (16:9, long-form).** The cam docked top-right, 48 px from the edges, in a bevelled gunmetal frame with a
  caption-yellow lip, a red LIVE plate and a yellow name plate. It scales out of the corner with a soft bounce, and on a
  reaction beat snaps up to the enlarged size (the "zoom on my face" moment creators cut to), the lip ignites and a light
  rakes across the rim, then it settles back to the dock.
- **b/ Stacked cam (9:16, Shorts / TikTok).** Facecam band across the top 42%, gameplay below, joined by a physical seam
  (gunmetal bar, yellow inlay) with a glossy yellow name pill and LIVE plate on it. On the beat the cam punches in on the
  face, the inlay lights up from the pill outward and the pill takes a press-and-spring hit.

The frame, lip, plates, seam and pill are real Three.js geometry (extruded, bevelled, PMREM-lit); all type is DOM, pinned
to the plates. Everything is seek-safe and renders from timeline time.

components.name: Punch-in zoom
components.job: A snap zoom onto a detail or face, with a shake.
components.summary:
The snap zoom creators put on a detail or a face to make a point: "look at this", "bro...", a reaction beat. It is used in long-form gameplay (onto the HUD, game text, a vehicle or a face) and in Shorts (stepped meme punch-ins on a character). It is a treatment of the footage itself (`kind: full`), so it always renders with footage.

- **A: Detail punch (16:9, 4.0 s).** One continuous gameplay shot with a sample wanted-level HUD. A focus frame springs onto the stars and locks (white to yellow). The camera punches 1.0 → 1.6 onto the HUD with a real zoom blur, a decaying shake and an exposure hit, while the 5th star ignites. It holds 1.67 s with a slow tracked push, then snaps back.
- **B: Face punch (9:16, 4.0 s).** The Shorts letterbox layout: the 16:9 clip in a band across the middle (1080×909) on true black bars. After a short setup (Franklin on the street), the edit cuts to the reaction shot in the band and holds 5 frames at 1.0. Three stepped punches land on the character's face (1.0 → 1.25 → 1.5 → 1.9), each opening the letterbox a notch (909 → 1000 → 1100 px); the third bursts it to 1728 px (black bars only 96 px), so the letterbox breaks. A payoff word, "BRO?!", slams in with it as real extruded, bevelled caption-yellow letters with an ink outline (Three.js). Each step is a 2-frame snap with zoom blur, a crisp 3-frame shake, an exposure kick and a tightening vignette. The face ends at about 1.6x of the source. The hold runs to the end of the shot, then the band snaps back on the cut to the next shot; the word docks onto the band edge and stomps out.
components.configDocs:
**A**
- `shot.start`, `shot.dur`: the punch shot's place on the timeline. Keep it in step with `<video id="s0">` and the `z1`–`z6` zoom-blur taps.
- `hud`: the sample wanted-level stars (`show`, position, size, `count`, `lit`, and `ignite`, when the last star lights). Set `show:false` to punch on your own clip's detail.
- `track`: the detail's centre in source pixels of the 1920×1080 clip, `[shotTime, x, y]`. The punch follows it.
- `box`: the focus frame size around the detail (source px).
- `punch`: `at` / `back` (times), `scale` (1.6), `drift` (slow push during the hold), `land` (where the detail lands on screen), and the snap timings and overshoot.
- `focus`: when the frame enters (`in`) and locks (`lock`), and the bracket `arm` length.
- `shake`, `light`, `vignette`, `blur` (zoom-blur strength), `sharpen`.

**B**
- `base`: the band scale at 1.0 (0.842 gives a 1080×909 band; 0.5625 would show the whole 16:9 frame). `bandY`: the band's centre line.
- `shots`: each shot's `start` (including a 1-frame pre-roll under the previous shot), `cut` (when it shows), `media` in-point, `ax` (horizontal anchor at 1.0: 0 left, 0.5 centre, 1 right) and face `track` (source px).
- `creep` / `tailCreep`: slow pushes on the setup and tail shots.
- `steps`: `[{at, zoom, band}]`, three by default. `band` is the letterbox height factor after that step (1.10, 1.21, then 1.9 for the burst; capped at the image's full height).
- `push`: the continued push across the hold.
- `snap`: the punch speed and overshoot.
- `out`: the snap-out (lands in the band on the cut to the tail).
- `faceX`: where the face is re-centred.
- `shake` / `vignette` / `light`: one value per step (shake is a crisp 3-frame kick; light is a band-local exposure kick).
- `word`: the payoff word (`text`, `size`, `cx`/`cy` cap centre, extrusion `depth`/`bevel`/`tilt`/`yaw`, `ink` outline, colours), `dock` (where it settles on the snap-out) and `out` (when it stomps out). Glyphs A-Z, 0-9 and `.,'!?-*` are in `media/glyphs.js`.
- `sharpen`: the unsharp pass on the band, from step `from` until the snap-out.
- `blur`: zoom-blur strength.

components.name: Circle and arrow
components.job: The red circle and arrow that point at something in the shot.
components.summary:
The red "look at this" annotation that GTA creators put on a player, car or detail: a hand-drawn circle with a curved arrow (long-form), or a thick block arrow with a short label (Shorts). Both variants are tracked to the subject in the sample clip.

- **A, `a/index.html` (16:9, 5.0 s), "Draw-on circle":** a chisel-tip red paint circle draws round the player in a crowded party, a curled brush arrow flicks in from the right and its two-flick brush head pops. Marker-ink material with dry-brush bristles, dark ink edge, tight contact shadow; on the payoff a white-hot bloom on the head and a glint that runs once round the ring.
- **B, `b/index.html` (9:16, 4.5 s), "Arrow + label":** a real 3D clear-coated red block arrow (Three.js) swoops in, lands with an overshoot and squash, bobs toward the target; "THAT'S ME" slams out of its tail; a quick brush circle loops his head.

- `clip.src`, `clip.in` (in-point, s); B also `clip.crop` (object-position x % for the 9:16 reframe).
- `target` {x, y}: fixed annotation position, used when `track` is `null`.
- `track` {t0, fps, x[], y[]} (+ B `map` {scale, dx, dy}): per-frame subject position measured from the sample clip. **For your own clip set `track: null` and put `target` on your subject** (or paste your own per-frame track).
- A: `offset`, `circle` {rx, ry, tilt, start, sweep, width}, `arrow` {from, ctrl, aim, gap, width, barb, barbAngle, barbWidth}: the shaft curls from `from` round `ctrl` and its tip lands `gap` px off the ring at ring angle `aim` (degrees, -90 = top), so it follows any ring size.
- B: `label` {text, key}, `arrow` {dir, gap, length, headLen, headHalf, neck, tail, depth, color, side}, `circle`, `labelOffset`.

components.name: Callout label
components.job: A short label pinned to a thing in the shot with a leader line.
components.summary:
A short label pinned to a thing in the shot with a bead pin and an elbow leader, tracking it as it moves. Creators use it to name, price or roast whatever is on screen: the car, the player, the NPC, the spot on the map. Long-form (A, 16:9) and Shorts / TikTok (B, 9:16).

- **A "Leader callout"** (`a/index.html`, 1920x1080, 4.0 s): a price callout on a car that re-targets on the cut, rolls the price on a 3D drum and ignites to gold with a RARE CAR stamp.
- **B "Stacked callouts"** (`b/index.html`, 1080x1920, 4.03 s): three staggered callouts on different people in a gameplay shot (one hangs under its pin); two retract, and on the cut to a close shot of Franklin his callout re-pins on his hair and locks in: the leader charges green, a bevelled lacquer plaque hinges up behind the word and locks, the type ignites to green metal, and the locked label holds at hero size while its leader follows him.

The labels are real Three.js geometry (extruded, bevelled Inter 900 from `media/glyphs.js`), lit and bloomed, with the creator ink outline + shadow done in post (`media/callout3d.js`). Pins, leaders and pings are SVG; A's tags are DOM.

components.job: A huge outlined reaction word (NOOO!!!, BRUH, W) on a beat.
components.summary:
A huge outlined reaction word that lands on the beat: the "NOOOOOO!!!", "BRUH", "W" moment that GTA creators burn in when something goes wrong (or very right). Built as real 3D type: each letter is an extruded, bevelled Three.js mesh with an enamel face, metal walls, a thick ink outline and a drop shadow.

- **A, `a/index.html` (16:9 long-form, 1920x1080, 4.0 s):** "NOOOOOOO!!!" in the bottom-centre caption band. Letters slam in one after another and the word stretches out from the centre; the "!!!" slam squashes the word, punches it to full depth and ripples a hop back through the letters. Use it in long-form gameplay commentary on a fail, a death or a loss.
- **B, `b/index.html` (9:16 Shorts, 1080x1920, 4.0 s):** a stacked "BR / UH" block in the middle of the safe zone. Letters pop in white, a yellow liquid fills them from the bottom, and the block locks in with a pop and a quick shake. Use it on the punchline beat of a Short.

components.name: Emoji pop
components.job: A 3D emoji or skull that pops on a beat.
components.summary:
A real 3D emoji sticker that pops on the beat over a GTA clip: the "I'm dead" skull or the tears-of-joy face that creators drop
next to the subject when something funny happens. Long-form (A, 16:9) and Shorts / TikTok (B, 9:16). Overlay: renders
transparent with `bg:none`.

- **A, Skull pop (1920x1080):** our own glossy 3D skull (Three.js: shaped cranium with real eye-socket and nose dents,
  capsule teeth, hinged jaw) pops in beside the subject with stretch and squash, snaps its jaw open and winks as the light
  rakes across it, laughs for ~1.5 s, then hops and tumbles out of frame.
- **B, Emoji burst (1080x1920):** our own 3D tears-of-joy face, about 56% of the frame wide, pops in grinning, then bursts
  into the laugh: the mouth snaps open, the glossy 3D tears squirt out and fling glass droplets, one shockwave of light rolls
  out from behind it and dissipates, and the arcade-magenta rim flares. Two smaller faces land together as the echo; all
  three laugh in bounce, then fall out.
components.configDocs:
A (`a/index.html`): `at` (cranium centre, px), `size` (px per skull unit), `wink` (`right` / `left` / `none`), `bone`,
`socket`, `rim` (rim-light colour, match your shot), `shadow` (drop-shadow opacity), `timing` (`pop`, `laugh` = payoff,
`out`, `end`), `shots` (keep in sync with the `<video>` tags).

B (`b/index.html`): `faces[]` (`x`, `y`, `size` = radius px, `pop`, `out`, `tilt`, `spin`; `faces[0]` also has `burst`, the
payoff second; give the echo faces the same `pop`), `face` colours, `tear`, `shockwave` (`on`, `from` / `to` radius in face
radii, `life`, `front` / `body` / `wake` colours), `splash` (droplet count), `rim` (rim light from screen-left, match your
shot), `key`, `shadow`, `laughBeat`, `timing.end`, `shots`.

notes.at: where the skull sits (canvas px, the cranium centre) and how big (px per skull unit: the cranium is 2 units wide)
notes.rim: rim light, matched to the shot (warm sun)
notes.shadow: drop shadow opacity on the shot
notes.timing: pop -> laugh (payoff: jaw snaps open + wink + light rake) -> tumble out pop on the cut, payoff (jaw snap + wink + light sweep), a second laugh snap on the next cut, then out
notes.shots: the footage (plate only); keep these in sync with the <video> tags above

components.name: Name tag
components.job: Player or character names floating over them, coloured per person.
components.summary:
Who is this, in their colour, sitting on them. Two variants:

- **A, Player tags (16:9, long-form):** floating 3D name tags pinned over each player in a gameplay clip (GTA Online crews, RP, story recaps). They drop in as pins, unfold into nameplates and light up in each player's colour, then ride the players' heads.
- **B, Character intro (9:16, Shorts / TikTok):** the freeze-frame character intro. The shot freezes, the world drops into a duotone in the character's colour while he stays natural (a head-and-shoulders matte with a rim behind his head), a big 3D name slams in above him and locks in green, with a role plate and a pointer to his head; then the frame whips out to the next shot.
components.configDocs:
**A (`a/index.html`)**
- `tags[]`: `name`, `rank` (the number in the puck), `track` (a head track in `media/tracks.js`), `tip` (pointer tip offset above the head centre at clip start / end, px), `scale` (start / end), `in` (pop time), `bx` (0 = plate centred on the pointer, 0.5 = puck over the pointer), `face` (enamel top / bottom colours), `hot` (front edge), `halo`.
- `look`: capsule height, tail, puck inset, name / rank sizes, the pre-payoff enamel `pre`, `tilt`, `depth`, `bevel`.
- `timing`: `unfold`, `ignite` + `igniteDur` + `frontFrom` / `frontTo` (the light front's screen x), `out[]` per tag, `end`.

**B (`b/index.html`)**
- `name`, `role`; `head` (face centre and head top on the frozen frame; the tail points at the top).
- `freeze`: `at` (media time of the frozen frame), `release` (the whip starts), `cut` (lands on the next shot).
- `name3d`: size, max ink width, centre, depth, bevel, tilt, ink outline px. `chip` (y, height, text size, tracking, padding), `tail` (width, ink px), `colors`, `timing` (`slam`, `ignite`, `frontDur`, `lock`, `chip`, `tail`, `out`, `end`).

notes.tags: One tag per player. track = a head track in media/tracks.js (made for the sample clip; for your own clip, re-run media/track_heads.py or key x/y by hand). tip = how far above the tracked head centre the pointer tip floats, px, at the clip's start and end. scale = tag size at start and end (far players smaller). bx = where the plate sits over its pointer: 0 = centred, 0.5 = the rank puck sits right over the pointer and the name flag unfolds to the right (keeps the plate clear of a nearer player's face). A number, or [[t, v], [t, v]] keys.

notes.head: the character's head on the frozen frame (px): media/freeze-v31-cut.png is his head-and-shoulders matte (natural colour over the duotone), media/freeze-v31-rim.png the green rim behind his head; the tail points at `top`
notes.freeze: the frozen frame is media/freeze-v31.png = shotA media time `at`; `release` starts the whip, `cut` lands on shotB
notes.timing: slam: the name lands white; ignite: the light front starts; lock: the fill completes (punch + bloom); out: the tag exits

components.name: Chapter card
components.job: ATTEMPT 2, 10 SECONDS LATER, DAY 3: the marker between sections.
components.summary:
The section marker between parts of a GTA video: "ATTEMPT 2:", "10 SECONDS LATER", "DAY 3". Creators drop it between attempts of a challenge or stunt (long-form and Shorts) and as the time skip in a Short.

- **A (`a/`, 16:9, 4.25 s): Full card.** Gameplay dims, blurs and pushes in; "ATTEMPT 1:" slams on in big white 3D enamel caps; the number is a counter drum that rolls 1 -> 2, locks and floods yellow; a slanted wipe hands back to gameplay.
- **B (`b/`, 9:16, 4.06 s): Time skip.** The clip freezes, dims and blurs; "00 / SECONDS LATER" slams on, the counter fast-forwards to 10 and locks in yellow, and the card rushes at the lens into the next clip. In and out in 1.44 s.

The lettering is real Three.js geometry (`media/card3d.js`, extruded Archivo outlines from `media/glyphs.js`).
components.configDocs:
A (`a/index.html`):
- `text`: the line; `#` is the counter drum (e.g. `"ATTEMPT #:"`, `"DAY #"`, `"ROUND #"`).
- `from`, `to`: the drum shows `from`, rolls to `to` (single digit, 0-9) and locks.
- `type`: glyph set (`wide` / `narrow`), size, `maxInk` (auto-fit width), tracking, centre `cx`/`cy`, extrusion `depth`, `bevel`, `tilt`.
- `colors`: `white` (face, walls), `state` (the locked yellow metal: face stops + `facePos`, lip, walls, hot band), `glow` (the warm bounce, rgb).
- `bed`: brightness, contrast, saturate, blur, shade, push of the footage under the card.
- `timing`: dim, letter `in` / `stagger` / `inDur`, `tick` / `rollDur`, `out` / `wipeDur`, `end`.

B (`b/index.html`):
- `number`: `"##"` (two drums), `from`, `to` (0 -> 10: the units spin a full turn, the tens carry).
- `caption`: the line under the number (`"SECONDS LATER"`, `"MINUTES LATER"`, `"HOURS LATER"`).
- `type.num`, `type.cap`: glyph set, size, max ink width, tracking, depth, bevel, tilt; `blockCY`, `gap`.
- `freeze`: the freeze time `at` and its grade (brightness, contrast, saturate, blur), `punch`, `push`, `shade`.
- `timing`: `in`, `stagger`, `inDur`, `spin`, `spinDur`, `out`, `outDur`, `end`.

components.name: Game title card
components.job: Names the game or series over intro footage. Our own lettering, no Rockstar marks.
components.summary:
The game-logo sticker creators stamp over the first seconds of a video or a segment: stacked heavy white caps with a black edge and one coloured accent bar, no box. Ours is real 3D (Three.js): white enamel faces, polished bevel lips, black lacquer walls, a candy-enamel bar with raised letters, one ink outline and a soft contact shadow, and a light sweep on the lock-in. Our own lettering (Archivo), no game logos.

- **A, "Series title" (16:9, long-form):** a series lock-up ("LOS SANTOS STORIES") centred over intro footage.
- **B, "Corner title" (9:16, Shorts / TikTok):** a compact game title ("GTA 5" / "ROLEPLAY") docked top-left over gameplay.

- `lines`: the stacked title lines (A–Z, 0–9, `& . , ' ! ? - : #`).
- `tag`: the word on the accent bar.
- `layout`: A uses `cx`/`cy` (lock-up centre); B uses `x`/`y` (top-left of the lock-up). `cap` (title cap height px), `lead`, `tracking`, `align`, `barH`, `barGap`, `tagCap`, `tagTracking`.
- `colors`: `face` (top, foot), `lip`, `wall` (near, far), `ink`, `bar` (left, right), `barWall`, `barLip`, `tagWall`.
- `timing`: letter stand-up (`lineIn`, `stagger`, `upDur`), bar (`barIn`, `barDur`), tag (`tagIn`, `tagStagger`, `tagDur`), lock-in punch (`lock`), light sweep (`sweep`, `sweepDur`, `bloomAt`), exit (`exit`, `exitStagger`, `exitDur`, `barOut`, `barOutDur`), `end`.

components.name: Speed lines
components.job: Anime speed streaks from the frame edges on fast or hype beats.
components.summary:
Anime speed streaks from the frame edges for the fast or hype beats of a GTA video: a climb, a skydive, a flight, a chase or a big jump. Top long-form GTA 5 creators lay a white speed-line overlay over these moments. Shorts use the same overlay, often tinted. This version is drawn live: vector spikes in three depth layers converge on the subject. They slam in on the beat, re-hit on each cut and retract off the edges at the end.

- **A, `a/index.html` (16:9, 1920x1080, 5.65 s): radial streaks.** White, with a soft fade to a sharp tip and an ice-blue bloom. Cruise state, a wind-up, then the slam on the cut at 1.70 s with a punch-zoom, an edge zoom blur and a hot bloom.
- **B, `b/index.html` (9:16, 1080x1920, 5.55 s): vertical streaks for Shorts.** Weighted to the top and bottom edges. Two-tone caption-yellow streaks with white cores, a quick ramp-up on the beat at 1.60 s, and white-hot for 3 frames.

notes.shots: One entry per <video> pair above (s# and z#). focus = the subject the streaks converge on, as a fraction of the frame; "to" (optional) tracks it across the shot.
notes.timing: in: streaks shoot in; beat: the payoff slam (cut on it); kicks: smaller re-hits on later cuts; out: retract off the edges.

notes.shots: One entry per <video> pair above (s# and z#). focus = the subject the streaks converge on, as a fraction of the frame; "to" (optional) tracks it across the shot.
notes.timing: in: streaks shoot in; beat: the quick ramp-up slam (cut on it); kicks: smaller re-hits on later cuts; out: retract off the edges.

components.name: Celebration FX
components.job: Money rain, confetti or a power-up aura on a milestone.
components.summary:
The milestone hit GTA creators drop over gameplay: money raining over the screen when the cash lands, or a power-up ring and a confetti
burst on the subject when something levels up. Overlay kind: both variants render transparent with `bg:none`.

- **A, `a/index.html` (16:9, long-form):** 3D money rain. Fictional "Los Santos 100" bills as real bent, fluttering paper with a satin
  clearcoat and a foil ribbon; a money-gun burst from the bottom edge, a hero bill that flips to the lens, then rain from above.
  Depth of field and real motion blur.
- **B, `b/index.html` (9:16, Shorts):** a cyan power-up aura round the subject's shoulders, built as a real lit 3D object: a thick
  glass torus full of plasma with a white-hot braided filament twisting inside it, a key-light specular band and a glass rim, crowned by
  faceted crystal barbs. It draws on, then locks in on the cut (the tube inflates, runs white-hot, the barbs erupt, a light rakes round
  the glass, a shockwave, wing slashes and a few embers), with two foil confetti cannons (gold, pearl iridescent, cyan).
components.configDocs:
A (`a/index.html`):
- `notes`: the front/back colour PNGs and their ORM maps (R bump, G roughness, B metalness). Rebuild with `/usr/bin/python3 a/media/make_notes.py`.
- `burst.at` / `burst.count`: when the money gun fires and how many bills; `burst2`: the smaller burst on the cut.
- `rain.from` / `rain.count`: rain start and bills; spawn times are solved so every bill is gone by `timing.clear`.
- `hero.apex`, `hero.x`, `hero.y`: when and where the hero bill faces the lens.
- `dof.nearBlur` / `dof.farBlur` (px), `motionBlur.samples` / `motionBlur.shutter` (frames), `light.exposure`.
- `light.shots`: one entry per shot (`until` = cut time): key colour `key`, strength `ki`, direction `from`, `rim`, fill `sky` / `ground` / `fill`,
  reflection environment `env` (`day`, `sunset`, `sea`). Match these to your own shots.
- `timing.clear`, `timing.end`.

B (`b/index.html`):
- `aura.color`, `aura.center` (px), `aura.radius` / `aura.tube` (px), `aura.tilt`.
- `aura.barbs`: one `[angle deg, out 1 / in 0, length px]` per crystal barb; `aura.barbBase` (root half-width, px); `aura.braid` (strands, twists).
- `aura.track`: the subject's head per 0.1 s as `[s, centre x, top y, width]` in footage px. It drives the head matte (the far arc passes
  behind the head), the light wrap and the ring follow (`aura.follow`). Re-measure it for your own clip.
- `subject.matte` / `subject.lightWrap`: the head matte and the cyan light on the subject are fitted to the sample clip. `"plate"` (default)
  uses them only over the sample footage, so the transparent render has neither; `true` keeps them on `bg:none` too, `false` turns them off.
- `aura.slash` (wing-slash half-span / tip height, px), `aura.wrap` (peak, hold, shoulder and hair ellipses), `aura.embers`.
- `confetti.count`, `confetti.streamers`, `confetti.colors`.
- `timing`: `drawOn`, `payoff` (the lock-in, put it on your cut), `collapse`, `gone`, `clear`, `end`; `camera.push` / `camera.kick`.
- `dof`, `motionBlur` as in A.

notes.notes: the note artwork (our own design; swap in your own PNGs at 1536x654, back pre-mirrored)
notes.burst: money-gun burst from the bottom edge (seconds, bills)
notes.burst2: a second, smaller burst on the cut (behind the hero)
notes.rain: rain from above, spawned so the last bill is gone by timing.clear
notes.hero: the one bill that flips to face the lens (x, y as fractions of the frame)
notes.motionBlur: sub-frame samples, shutter in frames (0.5 = 180 degrees)

notes.subject: fitted to the sample subject: "plate" = only over the sample footage (off in the transparent render), true = always, false = never
notes.camera: slow push on each shot (scale), shake amplitude on the lock-in (px)

components.summary:
Animated letterbox bars for story and character edits: the bars close on a cut, the picture takes a film grade,

- **A, `a/index.html` (16:9, 1920x1080, 5.3 s):** 2.39:1 bars for long-form cold opens, story beats and title

- **B, `b/index.html` (9:16, 1080x1920, 5.2 s):** vertical-edit bars for Shorts / TikTok story edits. Thin always-on

components.name: Blur-fill reframe
components.job: Puts a 16:9 clip on a vertical canvas.
components.summary:
The Shorts reframe: a horizontal 16:9 clip placed on a vertical 9:16 canvas, with the empty space filled by a blurred,
enlarged, darkened copy of the same clip instead of black bars. Creators use it on almost every gameplay Short and
TikTok cut down from long-form footage. Both variants are 1080x1920, 30 fps, kind `full` (they always show footage).

- **A, Blur fill** (`a/index.html`, 5.7 s): the clip plays on the face of a real 3D slab (Three.js: machined graphite
  bezel, polished rounded chamfers, 60 px thick, reflections of a studio and of the shot itself), a 1:1 crop of the 16:9
  clip by default (4:3 and 16:9 in CONFIG), floating over a dark, graded blur of the same clip. It opens tilted in 3D,
  swings flat and seats on the first cut, and a light rakes along the top chamfer with bloom on the metal. Every later
  cut jolts the slab and defocuses the bed; it tips back to its opening pose on the last frame, so it loops.
- **B, Split stack** (`b/index.html`, 5.93 s): gameplay on top, the creator's cam underneath, both on one 3D slab
  (1040x1274, a slim lit edge: 3 px ring + 5 px polished chamfers) split by one seam, over a blur of each clip, with a
  tab notched into each pane's top-left corner ("IN GAME", "@everestchris6"). The slab swings in tilted and lands flat on
  the lock cut; a polished rod grows out of the seam's slot from the centre and hits the bezel on that frame (squash,
  overshoot), the rod flares and light runs out along the side rails. It stays seated to the end; the tabs retract.
components.configDocs:
A:
- `shots` `[{id, cut, focusX}]`: each shot's <video> id, the time it takes over, and where the crop centres.
- `slab` `{width, aspect, centerY, radius, bevel, ring, depth}`: size, crop of the 16:9 clip ("16:9", "4:3", "1:1"),
  centre line, corner radius, chamfer size, flat bezel width and thickness. `metal` `{ring, chamfer}`: the two metal colours.
- `bed` `{blur, brightness, contrast, saturate, grain}`: the bed grade (keep contrast >= 1.1 and brightness <= .7).
- `open` `{x, y, z, rx, ry, rz}`: the tilted opening pose; `settle`, `kick`: the seat spring and the per-cut jolt.
- `rake` `{dur, power, bloom}`: the light rake after the seat. `timing` `{land, close, end}`.

B:
- `topLabel`, `bottomLabel`: the tab words (bottom defaults to the creator handle).
- `shots` `[{id, cut}]`: the gameplay shots; `cam` `{id, scale, focusX, top}`: the face crop (focusX is the source x at
  the pane centre; 700 puts the face right so the tab sits on the background).
- `slab` `{width, top, bottom, seamY, radius, bevel, ring, depth}`; `divider` `{height, bevel, proud}`; `metal`.
- `open`, `settle`, `kick`: the tilted opening pose, the landing spring, the per-cut jolt.
- `rake` `{dur, power, bloom}`; `timing` `{grow, lock, tabTop, tabBot, tabsOut, end}`: put `lock` on a cut or a hit in
  your gameplay; `grow` is how long the rod takes to reach the bezel.

notes.shots: cut: the frame the shot takes over; focusX: where the 1:1 crop centres (0..1)
notes.rake: the light rake across the chamfers after the seat

notes.cam: face crop: source scale, source x at the pane centre (face sits right), source y at the top
notes.divider: the polished rod over the seam
notes.open: the tilted opening pose (px, radians); y is an offset

components.name: Sponsor card
components.job: The sponsor or merch read card.
components.summary:
The sponsor / merch read graphic. Long-form GTA creators put it up during the ad read (often 10+ s): the product, the deal, and a QR code or discount code. Two variants, both 16:9 overlays (they also work in a 9:16 edit if you scale the overlay down).

- **A: Tiers + QR** (`a/index.html`, 6.3 s). A glossy 3D sponsor card swings in from the right with the product can standing proud of its corner. Three price-tier tiles drop into their wells; the best tier locks in (lifts, turns gold, price rolls down, BEST VALUE tab). Scannable QR + "SCAN FOR 30% OFF". Use it for the main ad-read segment.
- **B: Code lower third** (`b/index.html`, 6.25 s). A compact plug bottom-left, sitting above the GTA radar: the can pops in, a 3D plate hinges out from behind it, the discount code types into a coupon tile, the can whips a turn and lands face-on as the tile is pressed and locks in (gold fill, tick, bloom on the can), and a gold-foil 30% OFF tab slams onto the tile's corner. Use it to keep gameplay running while you read, or as the recurring reminder.

Everything 3D is Three.js r160 (`media/sponsor3d.js`, identical copies in a/ and b/), rendered from timeline time (seek-safe).
components.configDocs:

components.name: Transformation meter
components.job: The meter in 'Upgrading to X' videos: a portrait badge plus a fill that climbs as the character evolves.
components.summary:
The progress meter from "Upgrading X to Y" / evolution GTA videos: a portrait badge plus a fill that climbs as the character evolves, with a state change at every stage and a MAX payoff. It's a persistent overlay: it makes a big entrance, docks at the edge where creators put it, steps up between beats, and exits piece by piece.

| Variant | File | Use |
|---|---|---|
| A, Badge + fill (16:9) | `a/index.html` | Long-form. Top-left hexagon portrait badge joined to a wavy glass tube. A lime → red liquid surges stage by stage in milky glass. On each stage the badge punches, the next form irises open over the last one, the rim flashes and the LV chip rolls and slams. At MAX the meter pops, turns gold, a specular band sweeps the tube, embers lift off and a bloom lights the badge. Evidence: yt-EP_LdrobwPg, yt-E1Eu2_RUdEo. |
| B, Power tube (9:16) | `b/index.html` | Shorts. A gold-rimmed glass power tube at the left edge with an amber chevron power orb at its base. The liquid rises with bubbles while a true odometer counter beside the orb rolls up to 2,500. At MAX the padlock flies off, the final form wipes up out of its silhouette with gold light behind the head, and the counter slams gold. Evidence: yt-J2ed1YF71ZU. |

Both run 7.0 s at 30 fps.
components.configDocs:
### A (`a/index.html`)
- `forms`: one entry per form, as `{label, portrait}`. The meter starts on `forms[0]`, swaps on each stage, and the last entry is the MAX form. The portraits are square stills (480×480 is plenty) in `a/media/`.
- `liquid`: the gradient stops along the tube.
- `rim` / `gold`: the badge and tube rim colours, before and at MAX.
- `start`: the LV 1 level after the first pour, as a fraction of the tube. The default is `0.2`.
- `surges`: each entry is `[start time, level reached]`, where the level is a fraction of the tube and `1` is MAX. A stage ring is drawn at each level below 1. The defaults are 0.46 / 0.73 / 1. `surgeDur` sets how long each surge takes.
- `timing`:
  - `in` is the entrance;
  - `dock` is when it shrinks to its dock;
  - `pour` is the first pour;
  - `settle` is when it returns from the MAX pop;
  - `out` is when the exit starts. It needs about 0.6 s before `end`; the collapse is chip → tube → collar → badge.
  - `end` is the duration.

### B (`b/index.html`)
- `label` / `maxLabel`: the counter's eyebrow before and at MAX.
- `max`: the value at the top of the tube. `tickEvery` is the tick spacing.
- `steps`: each entry is `[start time, value reached]`; the last must reach `max`. `stepDur` sets how long each step takes. Values are multiples of 100: the odometer turns a hundreds wheel and carries into the thousands wheel, while the tens and ones stay at 0.
- `crest.unlocked` / `crest.locked`: the final form as a cut-out portrait PNG (transparent background, face about 65 % of the frame) and its silhouette. `crest.halo` is the gold light behind the head once it's unlocked.
  - To key a portrait shot against sky: `ffmpeg -i p.png -vf "colorkey=color=0xDFC898:similarity=0.15:blend=0.07,format=rgba" cut.png`. Set `color` to the sky colour.
  - To make the silhouette: `ffmpeg -i cut.png -vf "format=rgba,lutrgb=r=5:g=8:b=26" silhouette.png`.
- `liquid`: the four colour stops of the gold liquid.
- `orb.mark`: the emblem engraved in the orb. It is `"chevron"` by default (our own double up-chevron, which charges white-hot with the level), or `"star"` for an anime-style star. `orb.glass` holds the five amber stops of the orb glass, from centre to rim.
- `timing`: `in`, `out` (when the exit starts: counter wipe → crest fold → drain → tube retract → orb pop, about 0.6 s) and `end`.

notes.forms: one entry per form; the meter starts on forms[0] and swaps on each stage it reaches. The last form is the MAX form.
notes.liquid: liquid gradient along the tube (evidence: lime -> yellow -> orange -> red)
notes.start: LV 1 level after the first pour (fraction of the tube), so the first form already reads as "charged a bit"
notes.surges: the fill steps: [start of surge, level reached]. Levels are fractions of the tube; 1 = MAX. Stage rings sit at each level below 1.

notes.max: the value at the top of the tube
notes.steps: [start time, value reached]; the last step reaches max and fires the transformation
notes.crest: final form: a cut-out portrait (transparent background) and its silhouette; halo = the gold light behind the head once unlocked
notes.orb: the power orb at the base: amber glass with an engraved mark. mark: "chevron" (default, our own) | "star" (anime-style option)

components.name: Upgrade ladder

components.summary:
The tier-token track from "upgrading every …" / transformation-challenge videos: a column (long-form) or row (Shorts) of round tokens where locked tiers show a red "?", milestone tiers carry a gold crown, and the current tier wears a green ring that climbs one step each time the creator unlocks the next form. The tokens are real 3D coins (Three.js): metal rims, glass-domed portrait faces, a glossy 3D "?" and an extruded gold crown.

- **A (`a/`, 16:9 long-form):** 8-tier vertical ladder docked on the right edge. Use it at each upgrade beat, then let it hide.
- **B (`b/`, 9:16 Shorts):** 5-tier horizontal row at the top of the Short with check badges on completed tiers and a "TIER n · MILESTONE / NAME UNLOCKED" label under it.

components.name: Level counter
components.job: LVL 1 to LVL 1,000,000: a counter that rolls up.
components.summary:
The "LVL 1 to LVL 1,000,000" counter from GTA challenge videos (climb a tower, train a character, level up every jump): a heavy white outlined level number that rolls up through the video and lands on a milestone. Built as real 3D geometry (extruded, bevelled Inter Black glyphs in Three.js) with the creators' thick ink outline and drop shadow, and mechanical digits that flip over on short drums as they count.

- **A, "Level roll" (16:9 long-form, `a/index.html`).** Docked top-left. Rolls LVL 1 to 999,999 with a pulse on each new column, then carries over into LVL 1,000,000 and fills with gold. Use it as the persistent challenge tracker in a long-form video.
- **B, "Level slam" (9:16 Shorts, `b/index.html`).** A big centred level number that rolls to 99, trembles, and slams to 100 with a shake, a gold fill and a green "LEVEL UP!" kicker. Use it as the beat of a Short.
components.configDocs:
A (`a/index.html`):
- `label`: the label text ("LVL"; letters available: L V E U P M A X !).
- `climbTo`, `ticks`, `max`: the climb target, the levels that tick in one by one, and the max the payoff carries into.
- `place`: `align` ("left" docks top-left, "center" docks top-centre), `x` (ink left of the label, for "left") and `capTop` (top of the digit caps), in px.
- `font`: `size` (digit em, px), `label` (label scale), `gap` (label to number, em).
- `depth`, `bevel`, `tilt`, `yaw`: the extrusion and which way it recedes.
- `ink`, `shadow`: outline width (px) and drop-shadow strength.
- `colors`: white enamel (face / side / lip), gold (4 stops: a hard horizon makes it read as metal), the hot meniscus, the ink.
- `timing`: `enter`, `climb` [start, end], `ticks`, `pay` (the max lands), `out`, `end` (s).

B (`b/index.html`): the same, plus `kicker` ("LEVEL UP!"), `climbTo` / `tick` / `max` (98 / 99 / 100), `place.cx`, `font.gap` (px), `font.space` (extra word space in the kicker, em), the green kicker colours, and `timing.tick`, `timing.land` (the slam).

Digits use tabular figures, so columns never shift while rolling. Glyph outlines live in `media/glyphs.js`; regenerate with `media/gen-glyphs.js` (fontkit) to add letters.

notes.label: the label in front of the number
notes.climbTo: the climb rolls 1 -> climbTo (log scale: a new column every ~0.25 s)
notes.ticks: then the last levels tick in one by one (set timing.ticks to match)
notes.max: ...and the payoff carries over into the max
notes.place: "left": docked top-left, x = ink left of the label; "center": top-centre (x ignored); capTop = cap top of the digits (px)
notes.font: Inter Black em for the digits (cap 68 px), label scale, label-number gap (em)
notes.depth: extrusion (px) and its direction: down and to the right

notes.label: the small label above the number
notes.kicker: what the label turns over into on the slam
notes.tick: ticks to this, holds and trembles...
notes.max: ...then slams to this (one more digit column)
notes.place: number: centre x (middle of the Shorts safe zone x 72-936), cap top (px)
notes.font: Inter Black em for the digits (cap 250 px), label scale (cap 96), label-number gap (px), extra word space (em)

components.name: Cash counter
components.job: Cash with rolling digits and a glowing +amount on each gain ($1 to $1,000,000,000 videos).
components.summary:
The cash HUD from "$1 to $1,000,000,000" challenge videos: a cash pill with rolling digits, where each gain pops in as a neon green "+$" and rolls the total up.

- **A: Cash HUD (16:9, long-form).** A smoked-glass pill with a white enamel bezel docks top-right. Lime odometer digits; gains float up into it. The big gain switches it to the neon gain state, every column spins, and it locks in.
- **B: Cash pill (9:16, Shorts).** A chunky 3D money-green slab with a white enamel bezel and a reeded coin edge, sitting in the hook zone under an Archivo "BANK BALANCE" label. Gains pop in under it. Crossing $1,000,000 grows a new digit column, re-skins the slab to gold on the cut and rolls the label to "MILLIONAIRE".

The pill is real Three.js geometry (`media/gloss3d.js`). The digits are DOM, so they stay razor-sharp.
components.configDocs:
- `start`: the balance when the pill lands.
- `gains[]`: `{ amount, pop, merge, payoff }`.
  - `pop` is when the "+$" appears; `merge` is when it hits the pill (put merges on your cuts).
  - `payoff: true` marks the big one.
- B only:
  - `milestone`: 1,000,000. The payoff should cross it.
  - `label.idle` / `label.payoff`.
- `timing`: `in`, `dock` (A), `out`, `end`, and `lockAfter` (the spin length before lock-in).
- `pill`: box, radius and bezel width; B also has `depth` (the slab thickness) and `lip` (how far the bezel stands proud of the face).
- `view` (B only): camera distance `D`, eye point (`eyeX`, `eyeY`; a low eye shows the bottom wall) and the held tilt.
  - A docks it top-right; move `x` to 48 for top-left.
  - B is centred at `cx`.
- `type`: digit face (Archivo, stretch %, size), the chip sizes and, in B, the label size and stretch.
- `colors`: digit ramp, glass or lacquer ramps, bezel, neon, gold, chip. B has separate `body` (the reeded wall) and `face` ramps.
- `shots`: the footage clips (plate renders only).

components.name: Goal checklist
components.job: Goals that tick off one by one across the video.
components.summary:
The challenge-video checklist: round goal tokens that turn green and get a tick as each goal is done ("GTA 5 but I have to…", collect-them-all and 100-days videos). Overlay.

- **A, side checklist (16:9 long-form):** a column of tokens down the left edge with the goal names; each goal ticks with a strike-through and a check pop, the counter rolls, and the header becomes COMPLETE.
- **B, top checklist (9:16 Shorts):** a row of tokens at the top with the current goal written underneath, highlighted by a gold selector ring and caret; each tick strikes the goal and rolls to the next, ending on CHALLENGE COMPLETE.

The tokens are real Three.js geometry (`media/token3d.js`): enamel rings swept green by a shader, a domed photo face under a glass lens, and a tick coin that spins in. The CHALLENGE COMPLETE payoff is extruded 3D type (`media/title3d.js` with the glyph outlines in `media/glyphs.js`) that lands white and is lit to gold.

components.job: The big #5 to #1 that opens each entry of a list video.
components.summary:
The big "#5" that opens each entry of a top-10 / ranking video. Creators use it in long-form list videos (a number + entry title card, then a small number kept in the corner for the whole entry) and in list Shorts (a giant number with the entry name at the top).

- **A (`a/`, 16:9, 6.0 s): Number card.** A giant 3D "#5" slams in on the right showing the previous entry's 6, the counter drum rolls 6 -> 5 and the lock floods it pink-violet; the entry card builds on the left (pill, title, subline, top-10 progress). Then the card folds away and the number flies into the top-left corner, where it stays.
- **B (`b/`, 9:16, 4.1 s): Number stack.** The same 3D number at the top of a Short with the two-line entry name and the progress row under it; the stack exits by folding the name away and collapsing the number into its centre.

The number is real Three.js geometry (`media/num3d.js`: extruded Archivo outlines from `media/glyphs.js`). Everything else is DOM type (Inter).

- `number`: `from` (the previous entry, shown first), `to` (this entry, 0-9: the drum rolls to it and locks), `prefix` (the superscript glyph before the number, `"#"`).
- `pill` (A): the small label, e.g. `"NUMBER 5"`.
- `title`: two lines; `accent`: which line takes the pink-violet gradient.
- `sub` (A): the italic subline.
- `progress`: `total` entries and how many are `done`; the next one is the lit dash.
- `type`: glyph set, numeral `cap` height in px, position (A: `right` ink edge and `cy`; B: block centre `cx` and `top`), `hashScale`, `gap`, extrusion `depth`, `bevel`, `tilt`.
- `dock` (A): docked corner `x`, `y`, `cap`, start `at` and flight `dur`.
- `colors`: `white` (the pre-lock enamel), `state` (the locked candy metal: face stops + `facePos`, `lip`, `side` walls, `hot` band), `glow` (rgb of the plate bounce), `shadow`.
- `timing`: `in` / `inDur` (slam), `tick` / `rollDur` (drum), `out` (title exit; B: whole exit), `end`.

components.name: Clip grid counter
components.job: A grid of clip tiles with a counter, ticked off as the list goes.
components.summary:
The list-video grid: a wall of clip tiles with a big counter over it, ticked off as the list goes ("15 hidden details in GTA 5").
Creators use it in long-form list videos as the intro (the count runs up while the clips land) and as the recap at the end (every
clip gets its green check), and in Shorts as the hook frame of a "6 things" video.

- `a/index.html`: **Tile grid (3D)**, 16:9 1920x1080, 7.3 s. 5x3 tiles; the camera flies the grid tile by tile.
- `b/index.html`: **Vertical grid**, 9:16 1080x1920, 6.6 s. 2x3 bigger tiles for a Short; the camera glides down the grid.

Each tile is real Three.js geometry (clearcoat slab, live footage screen, neon tube rim, contact shadow). The current tile lifts
toward the camera, lights up and gets a 3D check badge stamped on; the extruded counter rolls one up on its odometer drums. On the
last tick the counter locks in (punch, rake light, bloom), a light ripple runs back across the grid and the caption rises.
components.configDocs:
- `count`: items in the list (= tiles); the counter ends on it.
- `caption`: the line(s) under the grid; `{n}` is replaced by `count` (A); `key` is the word set in pink.
- `grid`: `cols`, `rows`, centre `cx`/`cy` (px), `tileW` (screen width; height is 16:9), `gap`, `border`, `radius`, `depth`.
- `counter`: centre, `cap` height, drum symbols per column (`" "` = blank), face gradient stops, wall colour, `punch`, `flash`,
  `rake` (glint strength), `flash`, `pop` (lock-in scale slam), bloom levels, `tilt`.
- `look`: `neon` colour, slab `body` colour, `pending` [brightness, saturation] of unticked tiles, `lift` (px toward camera),
  `badge` size, `glow`, motion blur `samples` / `shutter`.
- `camera`: FOV, start pose and the intro / fly / hold poses ([x, y, distance, yaw, pitch]), spring `omega` / `zeta`;
  `fly.follow` [x, y] is how far the fly follows each tile away from the grid centre (1 = all the way).
- `timing`: tile arrival, first tick `tick0`, tick intervals `iv` [first, last] (they ease between), `roll`, the settled `still`
  window (rendered without motion blur), `exit`, `end`.

components.name: Spin wheel
components.job: A random-pick wheel that spins and lands on a result.
components.summary:
The random-pick prize wheel from GTA challenge videos ("the wheel picks my car / my challenge"): it spins, ticks past the pegs, slows, lands on a result and shows it. This is not the radial weapon/character wheel (that is `47-selection-wheel`).

- **A, `a/index.html` (16:9, 1920x1080), long-form.** An 8-wedge 3D wheel, pointer at 3 o'clock so the winning label lands horizontal; the result plaque swings out of the wheel to the right of the pointer.
- **B, `b/index.html` (9:16, 1080x1920), Shorts.** A 6-wedge wheel inside the Shorts safe zone, pointer at 12 o'clock; the result plaque pops out of the hub and lands in front of the wheel's lower edge.

Both are real Three.js geometry (`media/wheel3d.js`): extruded lacquer wedges with printed labels, gold dividers, rim pegs and hub, a bulb ring, a sprung ticker, and a gold-framed plaque. The spin is a deterministic physics sim (`media/spinsim.js`): friction, air drag and every peg braking the ticker; the launch speed is solved so the wheel rests on your chosen winner. The fast spin is real motion blur (the wheel is rendered many times per frame across the shutter).
components.configDocs:
- `wedges`: `{ label, color, ink }` per wedge, clockwise. `ink: true` prints a dark label (for yellow, cyan, green).
- `winner`: the wedge index it lands on. `land`: how far past the last peg it stops (0-1). `turns`: minimum full turns.
- `kicker`, `result`: the plaque's small line and big line (the result can be longer than the wedge label).
- `wheel`, `card`: positions/sizes in canvas px. `pointerAngle`: 0 = 3 o'clock, -90 = 12 o'clock.
- `timing`: `in`, `wind` (wind-up), `launch`; the lock time comes from the physics; `exit`, `cut` (wheel gone, footage cut), `end`.
- Shots: the `<video>` tags (bed `v35-penthouse-dusk`, blurred and graded while the wheel is up; the result shot after the cut).

notes.timing: lock = launch + the physics settle time

components.name: Footage card
components.job: A reference clip or photo inset in a card with a credit line.
components.summary:
A reference clip (or photo) inset in a white-bordered card with a credit line: the "here's the reference / the
original / the trailer shot" inset top GTA creators drop over their gameplay or talking head, in long-form videos
(A, 16:9) and Shorts (B, 9:16).

The card is a physical object: an extruded white porcelain bezel (Three.js, perspective camera) slides in at a tilt
and swings flat on a spring. On landing, the hinged black credit tag drops, slaps onto the bezel and bounces. Its
yellow lamp chip switches on, and the clip goes from a standby grade to full colour. On the plate render, the gameplay
behind racks out of focus and dims under the card. At the end the card swings out to the left.

- `a/index.html`: Inset card, 16:9 1920x1080, 6.1 s. A 1152 x 648 window (60% of the frame width), centred.
- `b/index.html`: Inset for Shorts, 9:16 1080x1920, 6.1 s. A square 792 x 792 window centred on the Shorts safe area.

components.name: Evolution timeline
components.job: Year labels for evolution and history videos.
components.summary:
The release-year tag from evolution and history videos ("GTA V 2013 vs 2022", "evolution of police cars"): a big white outlined year in the top-right corner that changes when the clip changes. Built as real 3D (Three.js): extruded, bevelled enamel numerals with the creators' thin black stroke and soft shadow, and a gold lock-in on the last year.

- **A (16:9 long-form, `a/index.html`), "3D timeline":** every stop year is a card on a spine that recedes into depth. The camera travels along it: each new year arcs in and drops onto the top-right slot on its cut (squash, bounce, lock-in); older years slide back into depth, joined by a flat white enamel bar with one engraved groove per year between them. Fast moves carry real motion blur. The last year fills with gold on the impact and ignites on the lock-in.
- **B (9:16 Shorts, `b/index.html`), "Year stack":** one big year at the top-right of the Short whose digits are mechanical drums; it rolls from one year to the next on each cut and slams into the last year in gold.
components.configDocs:
- `stops`: the years the edit holds on (one clip each). The last is the payoff. A puts a collar on the rod for every year between; B rolls through every year between.
- `place`: A `{x, base}` front-slot ink centre and base line; B `{inkR, capTop}` right ink edge and cap top.
- `font.size`: Inter Black em in px (A 176 = cap 128; B 262 = cap 190).
- A `scene`: `pcx/pcy` principal point, `fov`, `elev` (camera height over the spine, rad), `yaw` (how steeply the past recedes), `step` (spine distance between stops), `gaps` (spine distance per gap), `recede` (older cards shrink), `cardYaw`, `lean` (0: passed years face the camera).
- `depth`, `bevel`, `ink`, `shadow`; B `tilt`, `yaw` (extrusion direction).
- `colors`: white enamel, dim (A, years not in the slot: white enamel a touch less lit), gold (payoff), rail (A's spine bar), hot (meniscus/bloom), ink.
- `timing`: A `enter` ([start, landed]), `travel` (one `[start, arrive]` per stop change; arrive on your cuts), `land` (`h` drop height per stop, `fall` time, `sq` contact squash per stop), `out`, `end`. B `enter`, `ticks` (one flip per year), `run` (the eased run of years), `land` (the last year, on the cut), `out`, `end`.

components.name: Selection wheel
components.job: A radial wheel (character, weapon or radio) that highlights and picks a slice.
components.summary:
The game wheel that top GTA essays and Shorts rebuild: the GTA V character-switch wheel and the radio station wheel. The plate blurs and desaturates while the wheel is open (as it does in the game; the radio wheel also drops it to slow motion), the highlight ticks from slot to slot, lands, is pressed and locks in, then the wheel folds away and the footage snaps back to full colour on that frame.

- **Long-form (16:9), `a/index.html`, "Character wheel":** use it when the video talks about switching characters, picking a protagonist or "who would you play as". Sits on the right of frame like the essay rebuilds, with a HUD name label under it. The four slices are real lit 3D wedges (Three.js, `a/media/wheel3d.js`): glass bevels, a gunmetal bezel, and a picked slice that is physically pressed and pops out.
- **Shorts (9:16), `b/index.html`, "Radio wheel":** use it for a "best station / what's playing" beat. A ring of 8 station badges (our own invented stations, no real station marks) round a centre label. The locked badge turns into a real lit 3D coin (Three.js: chrome rim, clear-coated face) that is pressed, springs and then flies, spinning, into the socket of a NOW PLAYING strip. The coin is a duplicate: the badge stays seated in the wheel, lit with a pink rim and bloom, until the wheel closes. The strip wipes open from it and stays on screen after the wheel closes.

Both are overlays: render with `bg:"none"` for a transparent wheel you can drop on your own clip (the blur/desaturate of the footage is only part of the sample plate; on your own edit, blur your clip under the wheel or use the plate render).
components.configDocs:
### A: Character wheel
| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| `kicker` | small HUD line above the name ("Switch character") |
| `slots[]` | the four quadrant slices: `name`, `angle` (-90 top, 0 right, 90 bottom, 180 left), `color` (GTA V HUD colours by default; it fills the slice behind the head, never the face), `img` (square transparent PNG cutout, head and shoulders, in `a/media/`), `face` (`[x, y, h]`: head centre and head height as fractions of the image, so every head lands at the same size and spot) |
| `current` | slot lit when the wheel opens (the character you are playing) |
| `path` | slots the selector ticks through; the last one is picked and locked in |
| `wheel` | `cx`, `cy`, `radius` of the wheel on the 1920x1080 canvas; `head` = on-screen head height in px; `depth`, `bevel` = slice thickness and bevel in px |
| `bloom` | colour of the warm light behind the picked head at the lock |
| `plate` | how the footage looks while the wheel is open (`blur`, `saturate`, `brightness`, `contrast`); keep contrast >= 1.1, brightness <= 0.7, saturate >= 0.4 so the bed keeps its blacks |
| `timing` | `open`, `ticks[]` (one per `path` entry), `press` (the slice squashes to .96 and sinks in; keep it 0.06 s before `lock`), `lock` (22 px radial pop with overshoot; on the overshoot frame two white-hot arcs run the bezel; a specular band and a warm bloom light the pick), `collapse` (label rolls out, slices fold into the hub; keep about 1.4 s after `lock`), `snap` (= collapse + 0.4: the picked slice hits zero, the plate is back to colour; also the cut), `end` (keep the tail after `snap` at about 0.75 s) |

Portraits are cutouts (macOS Vision foreground mask, matte choked 1 px with a 0.6 px feather, light unsharp) of stills from the GTA V shot library (`v22` Michael, `v06` Franklin and Lamar, `v33` Trevor), never Rockstar key art. Each PNG is the shot's native-resolution crop, shown at or below 1.0× (head 138 px). Swap one by dropping a square transparent PNG in `a/media/`, pointing `img` at it and setting `face` to where the head sits in it. Keep `head / face[2]` at or below the PNG's pixel size, or the face goes soft.

### B: Radio wheel
| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| `kicker` | small line at the top of the hub ("Radio") |
| `stations[]` | 8 stations clockwise from the top: `name` (72 px, wraps to two lines in the hub), `genre` (one short sub-line, e.g. "Synthwave"), `art` (one of `palms`, `soul`, `block`, `talk`, `rock`, `night`, `bahia`, `deep`; the landed one is also painted onto the 3D coin) |
| `current` / `land` | station lit when it opens / station it ticks to and locks in (clockwise; `timing.ticks` needs one entry per step) |
| `nowPlaying` | `kicker`, `title`, `artist` for the strip under the wheel |
| `wheel` | `cx`, `cy` of the wheel on the 1080x1920 canvas |
| `strip` | `left`, `top` of the 720x188 NOW PLAYING strip (default x 180-900, inside the 9:16 safe column) |
| `coin` | the landed badge as a 3D coin: `thick` (edge thickness in px), `rim` (chrome tint), `hot` (rim flash colour at the lock) |
| `plate` | open-wheel footage look (`blur`, `saturate`, `brightness`, `contrast`) |
| `timing` | `open`, `ticks[]`, `lock` (press; springs out 0.06 s later while a white-hot arc runs the rim), `fly` + `flyDur` (the coin duplicate leaves for the strip, uncovering the lit badge still seated in its slot, and lands `flyDur` later, then the strip wipes open), `collapse` (badges fold into the hub), `snap` (= collapse + 0.32: disc cut, plate back to colour, cut to the next shot), `stripOut` (strip wipes shut into its socket, the coin pops out), `end` |

The coin is drawn by `b/media/coin3d.js` (Three.js r160 from jsDelivr), always from the timeline time, so scrubbing and rendering are exact. A's wheel works the same way (`a/media/wheel3d.js`); its face textures are painted from the PNGs and colours in CONFIG when the page loads.

notes.slots: Four quadrant slices. angle: 0 = right, 90 = bottom, 180 = left, -90 = top. Colours are the GTA V HUD character colours. img: a transparent PNG cutout (head and shoulders) at the shot's native resolution. face: [x, y, h] = head centre and head height as fractions of the image, so every head lands at the same size and spot in its slice whatever the crop.
notes.current: slot highlighted when the wheel opens (the character you are playing)
notes.path: slots the selector ticks through; the last one is pressed and locked in
notes.wheel: head = on-screen head height in px; keep head / face[2] at or below each PNG's size so no face is upscaled
notes.bloom: the warm light behind the picked head at the lock
notes.plate: how the footage looks while the wheel is open
notes.timing: press = the pick squashes (0.06 s before lock); lock = the radial pop (the arcs fire on its overshoot frame); snap = the frame the footage comes back; keep it at collapse + 0.4 (the fold-out takes 0.4 s) and start the next shot there

notes.stations: 8 stations clockwise from the top. art: palms | soul | block | talk | rock | night | bahia | deep (our own marks).
notes.current: station playing when the wheel opens
notes.land: station the selector lands on and locks in (it ticks clockwise to it, one tick per entry in timing.ticks)
notes.strip: 720 x 188; right edge stays inside the 9:16 safe column (x <= 900)
notes.coin: the landed badge as a real coin: edge thickness (px) and chrome tint
notes.timing: lock = press; fly = the coin leaves for the strip (it lands flyDur later and the strip wipes open); snap = the frame the plate comes back (keep it at collapse + 0.32 and start the next shot there)

components.name: Mission HUD
components.job: An objective line, targets-left count and gauge over footage.
components.summary:
A recreated mission HUD for GTA 5 / GTA Online challenge videos: a targets-left counter, a battery gauge, a plus-crosshair
and a GTA-style objective line. The lock-on brackets ride the target, the target blows up in the footage, a comet flies
to the counter and the 3D drum rolls the count down (3 -> 2). Our own lettering (Barlow Condensed) and marks; no game logos.

- **A (`a/`, 16:9 long-form):** counter docked top-right, battery bottom-left, crosshair centre, objective bottom-centre.
  Use it on any mission / challenge segment of a long video ("RC heli mission", "destroy every cop car", "100 days").
- **B (`b/`, 9:16 Shorts):** phone-first: one centred column, a big 3D counter at the top, the crosshair at frame centre,
  the objective, then the battery gauge with its % readout, above the platform UI. After the payoff the HUD docks out of
  the way (counter shrinks to the top, objective clears, gauge shrinks). All inside the Shorts safe zone.
components.configDocs:
- `label`: counter label ("Targets left"). `count`: the count before the hit (single digit); the hit makes it `count - 1`.
- `objective`: the objective line as parts; a part starting with `*` is the red keyword, `|` breaks the line (B).
- `battery`: `from` / `to` lit cells (of `cells`), readout = cells x 20%.
- `colors`: crosshair idle / lock colours, comet colour.
- `counter`, `crosshair`, `batteryBox`, `objectiveTop`, `scrims`: layout in canvas px. B also has `counter.punch` /
  `counter.anchor` (payoff punch size and the fixed point, as a fraction down from the cap line), `counter.dock` /
  `batteryBox.dock` (docked scales) and `batteryBox.gap` / `yaw` (the gauge + readout row is centred on `cx`).
- `target`: the target's on-screen track (shot time -> source px, `map` = offset/scale onto the canvas). Re-measure it
  for your own clip, or set every point to the crosshair to lock dead centre.
- `timing`: boot (`cross`, `ctr`, `bat`, `obj`), lock-on (`acq`, `lock`, `fire`), `hit` (the explosion in the footage),
  `comet`, `flip` (the count rolls), `drain` (battery loses a cell; in B it is the shot's cost, right after `fire`),
  `dock` (B: the HUD shrinks out of the way), `out` (exit), `end`.

components.name: Status banner
components.job: A full-width result banner (passed, failed, busted) with a desaturate. Our type, no Pricedown.
components.summary:
The full-width result banner GTA creators drop on a moment: **CHALLENGE PASSED** for a win (long-form, 16:9) and **WASTED** for a fail (Shorts, 9:16). The footage drains of colour, a smoked-glass band splits open, and the status line lands as real 3D lettering (our own Archivo type, not Pricedown).

- `a/` Passed banner, 1920x1080, 5.8 s. The letters flip up into the band, then a gold light sweep rakes the metal and paints the colour back into the shot.
- `b/` Wasted banner, 1080x1920, 4.16 s. A hit, a speed ramp into slow motion, a hard black-and-white drain, then WASTED slams out of the lens, stops dead on its mark (squash, band flex, rule flare, hot lacquer cooling), takes a raking light and collapses into its line.
components.configDocs:
- `title`: the status line, e.g. `MISSION PASSED`, `BUSTED`, `HEIST FAILED`. Letters A-Z, digits, space and `. , ' ! ? - & : # $ +`.
- `sub` (A): the white line under it (`<b>` = gold); `""` hides it.
- `tracking`: extra letter spacing in font units.
- `face` / `lip` / `wall` (`wallMid` in B): the face gradient, the bevel lip and the walls behind it (B: deep red, then black chrome at the back).
- `band`: `{y, h}` in px. `word`: `{x, y, width}` (centre x, cap-centre y, ink width).
- `bloom`: `{strength, threshold}`. `grade` (B): the death grade. `slamFrom` / `squash` / `tilt` (B): the apparent scale the word slams in from, how flat it goes on the contact frame, and the settled tilt that shows its undersides.
- `timing`: every beat in seconds (hit, band, flip or slam, sweep or rake, exit, end).

components.summary:

- **B (`b/`, 9:16 Shorts):** the same card, phone-first, in the upper frame with a label per star. The payoff word ("PERFECT RUN") slams in under it.
