components.name: Drama grade
components.job: A grade change that marks a dramatic beat: the frame drains to black and white or a hard silhouette, then colour returns. Seen in 14 top videos.
components.summary:
The colour-grade beat creators drop on GTA footage for a dramatic moment: the shot drains to a real black-and-white (or silhouette / bleach / teal-orange) grade on a hit, holds, then colour comes back on the next beat. Long-form uses it for sad or shocking turns ("he never came back"); Shorts use the hard silhouette look across a few beat cuts.

- `a/` 16:9 long-form: noir drain with a lit seam, letterbox, swatch look label, title line, colour floods back from the subject through a feathered mask with light blooms.
- `b/` 9:16 Short: a hard cut on the beat into a silhouette grade (punch, contrast slam), held across beat cuts with one slow push, one colour kept (tail lights as glowing crimson lamps, carried across a match cut), then the red surges and the frame snaps to full colour on that wide sunset shot, lit from the tail lights, held 1.2 s (v01 colour -> v14 silhouette -> v24 silhouette -> v16 tail light kept -> v17 tail lights kept -> v17 colour).
components.configDocs:
- `look`: which baked grade plays. A: `noir` | `bleach` | `tealorange`. B: `silhouette-red` | `noir`.
- `looks`: per-look label, number, seam colour, grain, vignette and the six greyed `swatches` the label drains to (B: `keep` = index of the swatch that stays coloured, -1 for none).
- `palette`: the six colours sampled from the clip (the label strip's colour state).
- `label`: show the look label (true/false; B defaults to false, creators don't name the grade). A also has `bloom` (lamp, sky) for the return flashes.
- A: `title`, `letterbox` (true/false), `iris` (x, y where colour floods back from), `timing` (hit, drain, label, title, back, flood, titleOut, barsOut, end).
- B: `push` (one slow push through the grade's hold; the colour shot plays at 1.0x), `cuts` (hit = the cut into the grade, beat = a beat cut inside the hold, red = the cut to the kept red), `timing` (snap, end). `timing.snap` must equal the last shot's `data-start` plus its bake's `--snapcol` / `--kick` time, and its `--surge` must be the frame before.

The follow ask, built from real 3D social marks. We use our own simple marks (play, camera, bird, music note), never platform logos.

- **A, `a/index.html` (16:9, 1920x1080, 6.6 s): THE END + socials.** The end tag for long-form. A red lacquer THE END slab swings in, then a row of 3D candy-lacquer mark tiles pops on with @everestchris6 under it. A press wave and a raking light run across the row.

Their white enamel plates slide out; on the cut each tile is pressed and its colour floods the plate, the handle flips to white and the tag locks in with a bevel bloom; then both spring back into their corners at a smaller size and hold quietly.

components.name: Freeze-frame intro
components.job: The shot freezes on a character and their name and role slam in, then the action resumes.
components.summary:
The character intro creators cut into GTA videos: the action **freezes on a beat**, the character is called out with a big
metallic name and a role line, and the footage plays on from the same frame. Full kind: it is a treatment of your footage.

- **A, Character freeze (16:9, long-form):** letterbox bars slam in, the frame snaps into them, the world drops into a cool steel
  grade while the character stays warm with a gold light-wrap and keyline, a real 3D gold name slams in across the top band
  **behind his head**, locks in with a raking light, and a role plate wipes in. Then it all releases and the shot resumes.
- **B, Freeze for Shorts (9:16):** the same freeze phone-first. On the beat the shot stops and visibly holds full-frame (exposure
  hit, shake) while the world snaps into the steel grade from his face out; then the frozen frame settles into a **full-width
  frozen band**: a print on a real 3D slab (Three.js: rounded, a 19 px rounded gold lip, polished gold sides, a clearcoat face)
  wider than the Short, so its gold lips come in from the top and bottom like letterbox bars while the sides bleed off the frame,
  with the same frozen frame racked out above and below it. **His head breaks up out of the band's top edge**, his 3D gold name
  slams into the top hook band **behind his head** (his head covers the letters' bottoms) with the role plate above it as a kicker,
  and on the last landing the band settles while one light sweep crosses the name's bevel. The band pushes 1.15x in on him through
  the hold (mapped from the landscape frame at 0.92x -> 1.0x, never upscaled). Release: plate shuts, letters fly up and away, the
  camera **dives back into the frame**, the colour floods back from his face and **the shot plays on** from the frozen frame, then
  the edit cuts to the next shot.
components.configDocs:
- `name`: the 3D title (A–Z, 0–9 and `. , ' ! ? - & : #`); `roleKicker` (gold) + `role` (white): the plate.
- `freeze.at` / `freeze.release` / `freeze.end` (A): the freeze window and the end (s). B: `freeze.at`, `pull`, `unfreeze`, `cut`, `end`.
- `face` (A): the face position on the still (the grade wave origin).
- A `cam` (letterbox snap: scale, drop, creep). B `freeze` also has `pull` (when the frame lifts off), `unfreeze` (the dive back)
  and `cut` (the next shot). B `slab`: `K` (how much the 9:16 shot is scaled from the 16:9 one), `size`, `radius`, `depth`,
  `bevel` (slab px), `F` (his face in the 16:9 frame), `FL` (where it sits on the slab at rest: its y sets how far his head breaks

components.name: Earth zoom
components.job: A dive from a globe down into the game's map and then into the shot.
components.summary:
The "zoom from space down to the location" establishing move. A real Three.js globe on NASA Blue Marble imagery (day side,
city lights on the night side, ocean glint, atmosphere, a turning cloud layer) dives in one continuous log-altitude zoom onto
southern California and down onto the Los Angeles basin (30 m Landsat, sharp all the way), where small in-game style
district labels sit on the real city. The dive falls into a cumulus cluster over downtown, the cloud breaks open at the
landing spot onto real Los Santos footage (the hills over downtown, 1.0x): a glossy 3D map pin drops onto the skyline and
the place name springs out under it.

- **Long-form (a/, 16:9 1920x1080):** opening a video or a new location chapter ("we're going to Los Santos").
- **Shorts (b/, 9:16 1080x1920):** same dive, phone-first: the globe fills ~85% of the width, labels and title sit in the
  9:16 safe zone, the pin is ~40% of the frame width, and the landing is the wide vertical v36 skyline shot, full-bleed.

Kind: full (it is a treatment of footage; it always shows footage). Duration 6.47 s, 30 fps.

Imagery: NASA Blue Marble Next Generation (Reto Stöckli, NASA Earth Observatory), Black Marble 2016, the Blue Marble
cloud composite and Landsat WELD 2000 (USGS/NASA, via NASA GIBS), all public domain; files in `media/`, sources in
DECISIONS.md.
components.configDocs:
- `place.name`, `place.kicker`: the landing label (default "Los Santos" / "San Andreas").
- `target`: `[lat, lon]` the dive lands on (default downtown LA, which Los Santos stands in for). The close-in textures
  cover lon -140..-92 / lat 12..52 (`wna_mid`), lon -123..-113 / lat 29.5..38.5 (`socal_detail`) and lon -118.95..-117.75 /
  lat 33.55..34.45 (`la_city`, 30 m); a target outside them still works but goes soft in the last second.
- `city`: the closest texture level (`src`, `water` mask, `box` = `[lon0, lon1, lat0, lat1]`). Default: 30 m Landsat of the
  LA basin. Drop in your own top-down map capture (an in-game map screenshot works) with its box to land on that instead.
- `start`: `[lat, lon]` the camera looks at on frame 0. `sun`: `[lat, lon]` of the sub-solar point (sets the terminator).
  `spin`: degrees the planet turns over the opening.
- `pin`: `screen` (where the pin's tip stands, px: put it on the place in your landing shot), `height` (px), `color`.
- `cam.fov`, `cam.alt` (log-altitude keys `[t, altitude in planet radii, slope]`), `cam.swing` (seconds over which the view
  swings from `start` to straight down over `target`), `cam.aim` (seconds over which the dive's vanishing point slides
  from frame centre onto `pin.screen`).
- `deck`: the cumulus field `base`/`top` heights and cell `size`, and the `tower` we fall into (`r` radius, `top`,
  `off` offset from the target, `skirt` height), in 1/1000 planet radius.
- `labels`: `px` (size), `safe` (title-safe box, px), `list` of `{ t, ll: [lat, lon], at: s, water }`. Each label is pinned to
  its place on the globe, rises in at `at` and leaves by itself before it would cross `safe` or be swallowed by the tower
  (a label that would get under 0.45 s is skipped). `water` gives the italic sea style.
- `timing`: `swap` (full cloud cover; the globe goes off and the landing shot is under the cloud), `part`..`partEnd` (the
  cloud breaks open from the pin), `land` (pin impact + title), `out` (exit), `end`.

components.name: Holo scan
components.job: A holographic point-cloud scan with HUD labels locking onto parts.
components.summary:
A holographic lidar scan of a car: a thin laser contour sweeps the vehicle nose to tail, a point cloud condenses onto the body
and its crease lines light up, HUD tags lock onto parts, then a lock wave prints the car as a thin dark clearcoat shell, a specular band
rakes it, the lamps switch on and the result counts up and lands on a spring. Creators use it for a
"scanning the car" / "let's analyse it" beat: car showcases, "fastest car in GTA" lists, comparisons.

- `a/` 16:9 long-form: tags in left/right HUD columns with leaders, readout under the car.
- `b/` 9:16 Shorts: car centred at ~75% width on a holographic projector pad (rim, turning ticks, radar sweep, contact glow), readout as the headline, numbered bracketed data boxes in a 2x2 grid under it. Everything stays inside the Shorts safe zone x 72-936 across the orbit; if you raise `dist` less or move `shift`, re-check the tail and the wing pin against x 936.

The car is real Three.js geometry (`media/holo3d.js`: a wedge supercar lofted smoothly from 8 rails with sharp
creases, round wheel arches, glass, louvres, intake, lamps, wing; procedural, no external models), rendered from timeline time.
components.configDocs:
- `kicker`, `done`: the mono line while scanning and after the lock.
- `result`: `{ value, unit }`, the payoff readout (e.g. `"213"`, `"MPH"`).
- `tags`: `{ k, v, anchor }` per part (A also `side`, `y`). Anchors: tyre/brakes (front wheel), roof, intake (engine), wing.
- A: `columns`, `colW` (tag columns). B: `rows` (`top`, `pitch`, `x` column lefts of the 2x2 data boxes).
- `car`: `yaw` [start, end] orbit in degrees, `pitch`, `dist`, `target`, `shift` (px, moves the car on screen).
- `colors.body`: shell tint (dark clearcoat). `points`: surface point count (the crease lines are sampled on top of it).
- `timing`: ignite, scan0/scan1 (sweep), wave0/lock (payoff: shell prints, lamps on, reticles tick), rake0/rake1 (hold light), exit, erase0/erase1, end.

components.name: Disclaimer card
components.job: The disclaimer before a mod or story video: a full-screen card or a small persistent line.
components.summary:
The tongue-in-cheek disclaimer creators put before a mod or story video ("No NPCs were harmed...", "*mods used, not real gameplay"). Two HyperFrames projects:

- **A, `a/index.html`: Full-screen disclaimer** (16:9 long-form, 1920x1080, 5.6 s). A hard cut from gameplay to a black card: a red enamel warning plate (real 3D: steel bevel, chrome screws, cut-through warning triangle, raised "DISCLAIMER" letters) slams on, a red rule draws, the first line rises in, the red bracketed punchline stamps down with a raking light, a 3 s hold, then a rush at the lens and a hard cut back to gameplay. Use it in the first seconds of a long-form mod / story video.
- **B, `b/index.html`: Corner disclaimer** (9:16 Shorts, 1080x1920, 6 s). The same plate as a one-row "MODS USED" sign with the line "*not real gameplay (sadly)" hung under it slams in big at 0.5 s, then whips into the top-right corner on the first cut (the payoff: overshoot, hot rim, raking light) and stays there as a small chip for the whole Short (legible at 360x640).

The copy is a joke, not a legal notice, and never claims to come from Rockstar or any company. Keep it that way when you edit it.

components.name: Bond meter

A relationship meter between two characters that fills or drains with the story: two portrait medallions joined by a glass tube on a lacquered pink-neon pill, with a real 3D candy heart in the middle. The bond pours from both portraits toward the heart; when it drains the heart cracks open, and when it hits max the heart slams shut, ignites and spins (MAX BOND).

- **A, Heart meter (16:9, 1920×1080):** long-form. Sits bottom centre like the creators' version (x ≈ 28–72 %, y ≈ 82–94 %). Use it for "will they stay friends" / duo challenge / story-mode commentary beats.
- **B, Bond for Shorts (9:16, 1080×1920):** phone-first. A's meter stacked: portrait, a fully visible glass capsule, portrait (≈ 80 % of the width, inside the Shorts safe zone), with a 480 px 3D glass heart perched on the capsule's centre as the payoff gauge, under a heavy "62 % TIGHT" line. The liquid pours along the capsule from both faces toward the centre and fills the heart in sync. It cracks on BEEF (both fills retreat to the faces); on MAX BOND the two fronts collide under the heart's tip, the weld blazes and the heart heals on the same frame. The sample plate is a Shorts split layout (the clip sharp in a window over a blurred bed).

The meter, heart, medallions and liquid are Three.js (rendered from timeline time, seek-safe); the status word and the % are DOM type.

components.job: A clock whose hands spin forward to show time passing.
components.summary:
A big analog clock over your footage whose hands race forward through the hours, then lock onto the new time. Use it when a challenge, RP shift or grind skips ahead: "6 hours later", "by sunset", "all day grinding". Long-form (A, 16:9) and Shorts / TikTok (B, 9:16).

- **B, Clock for Shorts (1080x1920, 6.1 s):** the same clock at 69% of the width in the upper area. 2:00 PM to 9:00 PM.

The light on the clock moves with the time of day. At the lock-in the face lamp switches on.

components.summary:
RDR2's honor slider flips into GTA VI's Criminal Profile and slides to IRREDEEMABLE: a meter that changes identity, the comparison object for a system that crossed games.

**When a creator uses it.** Long-form (A, 16:9): a thesis or comparison beat ("the honor system became the criminal profile") over official footage; the meter enters, shows the RDR2 state, flips identity, then slides to the hero end on a cut. Shorts (B, 9:16): the same beat phone-first at 72 % of the frame width over a 1.0x footage band with a blurred fill.

**What it is.** A Three.js instrument: a brushed-metal bezel with a real recess, a key-lit navy panel sunk into it, a title tab that widens with the title, a lit slot (metal lip, dark channel with an inner shadow and a lit bottom edge, a liquid fill with a specular band and a hot core), a bevelled ceramic puck in a metal collar with an identity LED and a contact shadow. Labels are DOM Oswald pinned to the panel face. Beats: enter 0-0.4 s, knob lands on HIGH HONOR 0.42 s, flip 2.3 s (light sweep, colour swap, labels roll through windows, knob returns to PROFESSIONAL), slide 3.6-4.2 s to IRREDEEMABLE with a slam (payoff 4.2 s), hold, exit 5.85-6.3 s.

components.name: Clip counter
components.job: Persistent top tracker for a compilation: which clip you're on ('3 / 10') with a segmented progress bar that advances on each cut. Keeps viewers watching to the end.
components.summary:
The tracker for a numbered GTA 6 compilation ("10 details you missed", "wildest trailer moments", top-10 lists). It shows which clip you're on and how many are left, so viewers keep watching to the end.

It works in two beats on every cut:
- **Slam.** The clip number lands as a 400–430 px wide-type numeral. Only the digit that changes rolls, with motion blur, and it's clipped to the numeral's own line box. The counting numbers are a pearl fill lit from above, with a soft white bloom that flares on the cut and a quick sheen. This is the chapter beat.
- **Dock.** After a hold (0.65 s in variant 0, 1.0 s in variant 1) the numeral gets out of the way so the clip plays clean under a small persistent top tracker. In variant 0 it retracts into the fixed bar as a 150 px lockup (only the numeral moves; the title and bar never relocate). In variant 1 it flies into its own numbered station in the top tracker and becomes that station's label.

The cut to the last clip is the payoff:
- the "10" rolls in already lit in the Leonida sunset gradient;
- one crisp 0.35 flash frame and a short exposure push hit the footage (under the type), with a short shake and punch;
- it slams with a 6 px RGB hit; its sunset bloom peaks, settles, then swells again as one specular sheen crosses it;
- the title becomes "FINAL CLIP" (variant 0 also grades the sky to dusk).

It holds for 1.2 s and then docks like every other clip. Then comes the **completion beat**: as the tenth slot finishes filling (6.8 s), all ten segments or stations turn sunset left to right with a 40 ms stagger and a glint runs along them, and the tracker blurs out.

Run it for the full length of any numbered compilation. With real 6–10 s clips the docked state fills most of each clip, and the slam marks each new entry.
components.configDocs:
Per variant (`CONFIG.variants["0"|"1"]`):
- `style`: `"bar"` or `"dots"`.
- `title`: the compilation title (wide-tracked caps: 28 px in the bar variant, 30 px in the dots variant).
- `finalTitle`: replaces the title on the cut to the last clip. Use `""` to keep the title.
- `total`: the number of clips. It sets the segment or station count (and v0's "/10"). Numbers are zero-padded to two digits ("07").
- `startClip`: the clip on screen when the overlay starts. Use `1` for a full-length overlay.
- `startFill`: how far into that first clip you already are (0–1).
- `cuts`: the time in seconds of each cut in your edit; the counter steps and slams on each one. Put each one half a millisecond before the cut frame's time: at 30 fps, frame 39 is 1.3 s, so write `1.2995`. Use the same value as the next shot's `data-start`. If the cuts reach the last clip, that cut plays the payoff.
- `numSize`: the slam size in px (430 in the bar variant, 400 in the dots variant).
- `hold`: the slam hold after a cut before the numeral docks (0.65 s bar, 1.0 s dots).
- `entranceDock`: when the first clip docks, counted from `timing.in` (0.9 s bar, 1.2 s dots).
- `dockSize` (bar only): the docked size in px (150).
- `totSize` (bar only): the "/10" size at slam size (72 px). It sits on the numeral's baseline, 16 px right of the ink.
- `totDock` (bar only): the "/10" size when docked (48 px).
- `barGap`, `numGap` (bar only): px from the title's box to the bar (18) and from the bar to the numeral's cap line (26).
- `labelSize` (dots only): the station numbers' size (30 px). The numeral docks into the current one at this size.
- `titleY`, `railY`, `railW`, `capY` (dots only): the title's cap line (240), the stations' centre line (306), the station row's width (720, centred; keep the end labels inside x 936) and the slam numeral's cap line (404).
- `scrim`: `"plate"` (default) shows the grads only over footage, `true` always shows them, and `false` never does.
- `sampleShots`: a note on which sample shots are used.

Global settings:
- `sunset`: the gradient on the current segment or station number and on the final numeral.
- `bloom`: the payoff bloom on the numeral (`color` #FE8E4E, `peak` 1 on the slam, `settle` 0.5, `sheen` 0.95 while the sheen crosses).
- `sheen`: the payoff sheen across the "10" (`delay` 0.25 s after the cut, `dur` 0.5 s, power2.inOut).
- `pearl`: the fill of the counting numerals (white, lit from above).
- `flash`: the hits on the footage, plate renders only (`peak` 0.35 on the payoff with `decay` 0.2 s expo.out, `cut` 0.18 on regular cuts, `expose` 1.5 for the payoff exposure push).
- `dock.dur`: the dock move (0.5 s, expo.inOut).
- `dock.finalHold`: the hold on the payoff before it docks (1.2 s).
  - A clip too short to finish its dock 0.05 s before the next cut simply stays big until that cut.
- `sweep.stagger`: the completion beat's per-slot delay (0.04 s).
- `timing.in`: the entrance start.
- `timing.complete`: when the last slot finishes filling and the completion beat starts (6.8 s). It's skipped if it doesn't fit between the last cut + 0.6 s and `timing.out` − 0.3 s.
- `timing.out`: when the exit starts (a 0.35 s staggered blur-out, fully gone about 0.45 s later).
- `timing.end`: the composition end.

notes.pearl: the counting numerals: lit from above
notes.bloom: payoff bloom: peaks on the slam, settles, swells as the sheen crosses
notes.sheen: the payoff sheen across the "10": PAY + delay, power2.inOut
notes.flash: crisp hits on the footage: payoff flash · cut flash · payoff exposure push
notes.sweep: completion beat: each slot turns sunset 40 ms after the previous one
notes.timing: entrance · the last slot fills (completion beat) · exit (blur-out) · end

components.job: Top-N ranking moment: a big '#3' numeral with the item's title lands, then docks into a small corner badge that stays while the clip plays.
components.summary:
A Top-N ranking moment for GTA 6 countdown shorts, such as "Top 5 trailer moments" or "Top 5 police chases". A giant sunset-gradient rank ("#3") slams in on a cut, holds as a poster title over the action, then flies into the top-left corner and lives on as a clean, type-only rank badge while the clip plays. A 5-segment progress rule fills across the clip. There are no cards and no boxes.

Use one render per ranked clip, laid over the start of that clip. The rank lands in the first 0.75 s and stays until about 6.3 s (v0) or 6.15 s (v1). It clears by about 6.7 s, so the next item can cut in clean.

components.name: Hook title
components.job: The opening hook in the top third of the frame ('GTA 6 details nobody noticed'), one keyword accented.
components.summary:
The opening hook of a GTA 6 short: the line that tells the viewer the payoff before they swipe ("GTA 6 details nobody noticed", "What you missed"). Put it on the first 1–3 clips of a compilation, breakdown or listicle.
- It lands with the first cut, and its keyword hits as the payoff on that cut.
- It reads within about 0.5 s.
- It holds while your footage keeps cutting underneath, then clears with a designed mask-out at `timing.out`.

| Variant | Look | Use it when |
|---|---|---|
| `0` Boxed lines | The TikTok text box, made an object. Warm paper slabs with room around each line (40 / 24 px), TikTok's merged corners, a 1 px lit top edge and a soft plum-black contact shadow under the whole stack: a 72 px lead-in tab over two ~196 px lines of Inter 800 display. Each slab wipes in on a straight edge with motion blur, carrying its line up inside it. On the first cut the keyword's slab slams 1.12 → 1 as it fills with the Leonida sunset (pink → amber) behind a hot light edge. There's an RGB split, a flash, a punch-zoom and a light leak on the footage. Then its light falls outside it: pink off its left end and amber off its right, screened onto the image, plus a bounce on the paper next to it. A sheen crosses it, and it re-hits on every later cut while the stack pushes in. | Casual or reactive compilations, "details nobody noticed", listicles. |
| `1` Official caps | Rockstar's own card language set in the image. A white tracked kicker with the magenta offset sits above wide Archivo caps: "WHAT YOU" (about 104 px, white) and "MISSED" (about 153 px, sunset), locked to one measure. The lockup is set left at x 96 in the sky of full-bleed footage, over a soft plum sky grade. The hook reads by 0.5 s. MISSED slams in on the first cut (flash, shake, RGB split) while an anamorphic light streak travels across just above its caps, then its light comes up on the footage: the bloom is screened onto the image, each letter in its own fill colour. A source stamp bottom-left ("— FEATURES TRAILER · 0:43") names the trailer and time of the shot on screen and rolls on every cut. | "Trailer breakdown", "what you missed", news and premium shorts. |

As a transparent overlay (`bg: "none"`) you get the type only. There is no footage, grain, vignette, flash, leak, light streak, night paper, stamp, stamp spot, bottom smoke or top smoke. The slabs and caps keep their own shadows, glow, RGB split and sheen; Boxed lines' bloom runs at half strength (`bloom.none`). Official caps also bakes in a soft top smoke (`scrimNone` 0.45), so the white caps hold up on pale clips; set it to 0 for none.
components.configDocs:
- `duration`: composition length (7 s). If you change it, also change `data-duration` on `#root` and `#ov`.
- `accent`: the sunset gradient used on the keyword only.
- `variants["0"]` (Boxed lines)
  - `lines`: one entry per slab, `{ text, size, padX?, padY? }`. Each line is set at its own `size` (sample: 72 / 200 / 200) and only shrinks if its slab would pass `maxWidth`. `padX` / `padY` override the padding for that line (the sample tab uses 26 / 14).
  - `keyword`: the line whose text equals it gets the slam, sunset ignite, light edge, bloom, sheen and re-hits. `""` means no accent.
  - `maxWidth`: the widest a slab may get (772 px, so the stack stays inside x 936 through the hold push).
  - `top`: y of the first slab (232; keep it at 230 or more). With the sample text the stack ends at y 740; keep faces below it.
  - `centerX`: horizontal centre (540).
  - `padX`, `padY`: padding from the glyph ink to the slab edge (40 / 24 px).
  - `radius`: corner radius (14).
  - `snap`: neighbours whose widths differ by less than `snap × radius` become one width (4). A real step gets square inner corners on the wider slab and concave fillets on the narrower one (TikTok's merged text background).
  - `inkText`: the type colour on every slab (#0B0B0E).
  - `shadow`: `[x, y, blur, alpha]`, the soft plum-black lift under the merged stack (`[0, 24, 48, 0.38]`).
  - `contact`: the tight contact shadow (`[0, 2, 4, 0.18]`).
  - `edge`: alpha of the 1 px lit top edge on every slab (.6).
  - `slam`, `slamDur`: the keyword slab lands from this scale on the hit (1.12, 0.32 s expo.out).
  - `impact`: `{ flash, zoom, amp, color }` on the footage at the hit (plate only).
  - `bloom`: the lit slab's light around it.
    - `colors`: pink left, amber right.
    - `strength`: 1.3. On plate it's screened onto the footage.
    - `hold`: .55, the level it settles to after the hit.
    - `rehit`: .95, where each later cut lifts it.
    - `none`: .5, its strength in a transparent export.
    - `tint`: `{ color, strength, until }`, a plain pink bloom for the payoff shot only (it leaves at `until`). Remove it for none.
  - `bounce`: the lit slab's light on the paper slabs above and below it (.2; 0 = off).
  - `holdPush`: the scale the whole stack reaches by the exit, linear from 0.95 s (1.02).
  - `grain`: Look grain on plate renders (.14).
  - `night`: `{ at, shadowAlpha }`. From `at` (put it on your night cut) the paper dims to street light and the lift deepens to `shadowAlpha`. Plate only. `null` turns it off (the sample has no night shot).
  - `timing`:
    - `in`, `stagger`: entrance start and per-slab offset.
    - `hit`: the payoff (slam, RGB split, flash, leak). Put it on a cut.
    - `ignite`: the start of the sunset fill wipe and its light edge (just before `hit`).
    - `sheen`: when the sheen crosses the lit slab.
    - `rehits`: your later cuts (3.4, 5.5). On each, the lit slab pulses 1 → 1.03 → 1, its light lifts and a sheen crosses it.
    - `leak`, `leakDur`: the one light leak (plate only; on the hit by default).
    - `out`: exit start.
- `variants["1"]` (Official caps)
  - `kicker`: the small tracked line, rendered in caps. Only name a trailer if every clip under it comes from that trailer.
  - `kickerSize`, `kickerTrack`: 30 px, 0.34em.
  - `lines`: `[line 1, keyword line]`. Both lines' glyph ink is fitted to `width` (784 px), so they end on the same right edge. Each is capped at `maxSize` (160).
  - `left`: the x where every line's ink starts (96). Each line is shifted by its measured side bearing, so the G, W and M line up.
  - `top`: y of the kicker (262). The lockup ends at about y 551; keep faces below it.
  - `gapKick`, `gapLines`: 24 / 4 px.
  - `slam`: MISSED's scale as it lands, from its left edge (1.06).
  - `bloom`: `{ color, strength, matchFill }`. MISSED's light, screened onto the footage (1.15). With `matchFill`, each letter's light takes its own colour from the sunset fill; otherwise it uses `color`.
  - `flare`: `{ peak, length, colors, above, travel, travelDur, gone }`. The anamorphic streak on the hit (plate only). It rides `above` px (18) over MISSED's cap line and travels from `travel[0]` to `travel[1]` px (−260 → 200) in `travelDur` (0.22 s). It is gone by `gone` (0.95 s). Set it to `null` for none.
  - `scrim`: opacity of the plum sky grade over footage (1).
  - `scrimNone`: the top smoke baked into a transparent export (0.45; 0 = none).
  - `topScrim`: `{ alpha, to, until }`. An extra `.lk-scrim-top` (.35, down to y 640) over the palest skies, switched off on the `until` cut (1.9). Plate only; `null` for none.
  - `grain`: Look grain on plate renders (.12).
  - `stamps`: `{ size, track, top, smoke, spot, showNone, lead, items: [[trailer, time, at], …] }`.
    - One stamp per shot, bottom-left at `top` (1384).
    - The row enters at the first `at`; each later roll fires `lead` (0.07 s) before its `at`, so the new source is in on the cut's first frame.
    - `smoke` is the bottom smoke (0.62). `spot` is a soft dark ellipse right behind the row (0.5), so it reads over white water.
    - `items: []` hides the row. Stamps are hidden in `bg:none` unless `showNone` is true.
  - `timing`:
    - `kick` (0.0: the kicker is already half-lit on frame 0).
    - `l1`, `l2`: when WHAT YOU and MISSED start rising.
    - `hit`: put it on a cut.
    - `sheen`, `sheenDur`.
    - `leak`.
    - `out`.

The layout is measured only after the exact Inter and Archivo weights have loaded. That way the slab widths, paddings and fits match the type the renderer actually paints.

components.name: Word captions
components.job: Spoken-word captions for voiceover compilations: 1–3 words at a time, the active word in the sunset accent, inside the caption safe zone.
components.summary:
Spoken-word captions for GTA 6 voiceover shorts. They show 1–3 words at a time, and the word being spoken wears the Leonida sunset (pink → orange → amber). Every other word is white.

The captions are built to be cut with the edit, not floated on top of it. In the sample, every caption card or lyric line gets its own 4K trailer shot that cuts on its first word. The type is title-scale, and the number or date that matters lands with a payoff hit.

**When to use it.** Any GTA 6 short with a voiceover: "details nobody noticed", news recaps, character explainers, ranking narration, countdowns. It replaces burned-in auto-captions with one clean type system.
components.configDocs:
- **`duration`**: composition length in seconds (7.0). If you change it, also change `data-duration` on `#root` and `#ov`.
- **`sunset`**: the accent gradient (Leonida core).
- **`flash`**: the payoff light on footage: `color` (#FFE2B8, a warm screen flash), `peak` (.16) and `exposure` (1.8, a brightness kick on the footage that keeps the blacks). A variant's `flashPeak` overrides `peak`. Off with `bg: "none"`.
- **`variants["0"]`** (Word pop):
  - `shots`: the ids of the `<video>` tags this variant shows (`a1`–`a5`).
  - `cards`: each card is `{ lines: [ [[text, seconds], ...], ... ], payoff? }`.
    - `seconds` is when that word is spoken.
    - A third item, `"em"`, makes the word a display numeral on its own line.
    - `payoff: true` on a card gives its `"em"` word the exposure kick, shake, RGB split, sheen and bloom. Use it on one card only.
    - A card stays up until the next card's first word.
    - `emSize` on a card caps its `"em"` word's size (e.g. `emSize: 240` for "TODAY?"). The word is also fitted to `pop.maxLine`.
    - `drift: { from, to, y }` floats the card's text by `y` px, linearly, between those times (used on the payoff card).
  - `bloom`: the warm light on the payoff numeral (`color` #FEB747, `strength` .6).
  - `exitAt`: when the last card blurs out (0.4 s).
- **`variants["1"]`** (Karaoke line):
  - `shots`: `b1`–`b7`.
  - `lines`: each line is `[[text, seconds], ...]`. A line rises in just before its first word and leaves just before the next line's first word. Keep each line to about 10 characters ("Meet Jason") so it holds 160 px.
    - A line whose word carries `"em"` (e.g. `[["19.", 5.25, "em"]]`) is the payoff numeral. It doesn't replace the line above it: it slams in underneath, fully sunset on its own frame.
  - `payoff`: the time of the word that gets the hit (it must equal one word's time; normally the `"em"` word).
  - `flashPeak`: this variant's warm flash peak (.12, so the leak does the work).
  - `leak`: the one light leak on the payoff (`dur` .6, `colors`, `opacity` .5, `y` .36 of the frame height). Off with `bg: "none"`.
  - `drift`: the last line and the numeral float by `y` px (−14) from `from` to `to`.
  - `exitAt`: when the last line blurs out.
- **`pop`**:
  - `maxSize`: the caption px ceiling (170). Each card is sized on its own: the largest size at which that card's widest line fits `maxLine`, down to `minSize` (96).
  - `emSize`: numeral px (340).
  - `maxLine`: the widest a line may be (780 px, which keeps a centred line inside x 150–930). Keep lines to about 9 caps.
- **`kara`**:
  - `maxSize`: line px (160). It steps down, to a 120 px minimum, only if a line is wider than `maxLine` (864 px).
  - `emSize`: the payoff numeral px (360).
  - `capTop`: the y of the line's cap-top (1040). `emGap`: the px from the line's baseline to the numeral's cap-top (50). Both are placed from real font metrics, and they keep the numeral's baseline at about 1468, inside the safe zone.
  - `dim`: the opacity of unsung words (.38, crisp white).
  - `feather`: the sweep's soft edge (18 px).
  - `maxSweep`: the longest fill across one word (0.45 s).
  - `rise`: how early a line starts rising before its first word (0.13 s). `out` / `outDur`: the old line leaves from `out` s before the next line's first word, over `outDur` s (0.24 / 0.14).

notes.flash: the payoff light: warm screen flash + exposure kick on the footage (a variant's flashPeak overrides peak)
notes.pop: word pop: caption px ceiling per card (shrinks so that card's widest line fits maxLine), numeral px, floor
notes.kara: karaoke: line px (shrinks so the widest line fits 864), payoff numeral px, cap-top of the line row (y), gap baseline→numeral cap, unsung-word opacity

components.name: GTA 5 vs GTA 6 split
components.job: A 9:16-native stacked comparison: GTA V clip on top, GTA VI below, era chips with year, a clean divider. Uses plates g01/g02 (GTA V) and a GTA VI plate.
components.configDocs:
- `duration`: seconds (also change `data-duration` on `#root`).
- `sunset`: the GTA 6 name's gradient.
- `type`: the size hierarchy.
  - `bWidth`: the GTA 6 name is fitted to this width (744 = 86% of the 864 px safe width; clamped 110–200 px).
  - `aRatio`: the GTA V name's size as a fraction of GTA 6's (0.7).
  - `aMin`: GTA V's size floor in px (112). GTA V is also capped at 70% of the safe width, for long names.
- `light`: the seam's light moment.
  - `color`: the bloom colour.
  - `peak` / `rest`: bloom strength at the hit and when settled (rest 0.08 keeps the settled seam a crisp line; a variant can override it with `lightRest`).
  - `alpha`: the settled line's white alpha.
  - `sweep`: the glint's run time.
  - `decay`: the bloom's fall-off time.
- `cutLight`: `peak` / `decay` of the smaller glint on every later paired cut.
- `swap`: seconds for the place-label swap on a cut (the old place lifts out with blur, the new one rises in sharp).
- `a` / `b`: `name` ("GTA V"), `year` ("2013"); `b.countFrom` is the year the GTA 6 label rolls up from (`null` = no roll), in `b.roll` seconds.
- `variants["0"]` (stacked):
  - `seam`: y of the line of light.
  - `payoff`: the cut GTA 6 lands on.
  - `flashCuts`, `flash`: extra small flashes on these cuts (plate renders only).
  - `exit`: when the names sink back into the seam (default `duration - 0.75`).
  - `pairs`: the edit.
- `variants["1"]` (diagonal):
  - `seamLeftY`, `seamRightY`: where the parked blade meets the frame edges.
  - `reveal`: blade-in time, which is also when GTA 6's first shot starts.
  - `takeover`: when the blade sweeps on through and the GTA 6 title rises to the end card. Give each pair at least ~1.6 s before it.
  - `endY`: the end card's vertical centre in px.
  - `aEnd`: when the GTA V side stops (after it is covered). The wedge is fully wiped about 0.4 s after `takeover`, so the last GTA V shot must run at least that long.
  - `lightRest`: the blade's settled bloom (0.2, a little warmer than the stacked seam).
  - `R`: the right edge of the GTA 6 lockup in px (918). `lblInset` pulls the tracked label in so its ink ends under the "I" (measured ink edge x=894, inside the 936 safe line).
  - `cardOut`: when the end card blurs out (`null` = hold to the last frame).
  - `payoffDecay`: the payoff bloom's fall-off (ends before the next cut's glint).
  - `pairs`.
- `pairs`: one entry per cut, `{ at, places, a: { clip, start, focus }, b: { clip, start, focus } }`.
  - Diagonal only: a pair with just `b` (no `a`) is a GTA 6-only cut after the takeover, e.g. the end card's own shot (`at: 4.6` in the demo). The GTA V side's last shot then runs to `aEnd`.
  - `at`: when this pair starts. Both sides cut here on the same frame.
  - `places`: `[GTA V place, GTA 6 place]` shown in the labels while this pair is on screen. When a pair's place differs from the pair before, the label swaps on that cut. Use real places only.
  - `start`: the clip's in-point in seconds (skip slates, ratings and your clip's own cuts).
  - `focus`: CSS object-position, e.g. `"62% 50%"`, to frame the subject.
  - Optional `rate`: playback rate (e.g. `0.68`) to stretch a short shot. It repeats frames, so keep it at 0.6 or above (lower judders; pre-slow instead). The shot uses `duration × rate` seconds of source.
  - Optional `y`: px offset for that one shot.
  - Optional `rise` (diagonal, GTA 6 side): seconds for a shot framed low with `y` to climb back to 0 as the takeover starts. Its empty top strip stays hidden behind the parked blade (keep `y` under `seamRightY`, 220), and a `rise` of about 0.25 s stays ahead of the sweep. The demo's dock shot uses `y: 200, rise: 0.25` to put its string lights under the blade.
  - Optional `box: [top, height]`: size the shot to a band instead of the full frame. In the diagonal, the GTA V side only has to cover the wedge above the blade, so `box: [0, 1000]` shows a 16:9 shot at 0.93x (sharper, with the whole skyline above the blade) instead of a 1.78x full-height crop. Keep `top` at 0 and `height` past the blade's left end (860).
  - Optional `zoom` + `origin`: scale the shot from that point (default the top edge). Stacked halves fit their height exactly, so vertical `focus` does nothing there; zoom from `"50% 100%"` to lift a subject away from the seam.
  - Optional `grade`: a CSS filter for that shot, e.g. `"contrast(1.12) saturate(1.08)"` to lift a hazy shot.
  - Optional `scrim` (stacked, GTA V side): 0–1 extra bottom scrim under the label for that pair, for busy shots.

variants.label: Stacked / Diagonal reveal
variants.kindEvidence: Full-frame component: it always shows footage (the split IS the footage)

options.label: No finishing (footage still shows: full-frame split)

notes.type: The hierarchy is in the type: GTA 6 (b) is fitted to bWidth (86% of the 864 px safe width, clamped 110-200 px); GTA V (a) is aRatio x that size (never under aMin, never wider than 70% of the safe width), in 86% white.
notes.light: The seam is the light moment: at the payoff a specular glint runs its length (sweep s, expo.out), then it blooms warm at `peak` and decays to `rest` over `decay` s. Settled line alpha = `alpha`. rest 0.08 keeps the settled seam a crisp line of light, not a frosted band; a variant can override it (lightRest).
notes.cutLight: Every later paired cut gets its own smaller beat: the glint re-runs the seam at cutLight.peak, and the place names swap (old lifts out with blur, new rises in sharp, `swap` s) when a pair's `places` differ from the pair before.
notes.b: GTA 6 (bottom / lower-right). The label's year rolls countFrom -> year (null = no roll) in `roll` s, power2.out, and the digits stay blurred while they roll, so no wrong year is ever readable.

components.name: Blurred fill frame
components.job: A 16:9 clip framed in 9:16: the clip centred as a rounded card over a blurred, darkened, enlarged copy of itself, a title above and a source/handle line below.
components.summary:
Puts landscape (16:9) footage into a vertical 9:16 short as an **ambient screen**. The shot plays sharp in the frame. The same shot, blown up and blurred, glows around it, and the frame's own edges bleed light past it, like a lit screen in a dark room. Every cut re-colours the whole vertical frame. The type sits in that glow, never on the picture.

**When to use it in a GTA 6 short:** whenever the source is landscape: trailer moments, gameplay captures, a "things you missed in Trailer 2" breakdown or a compilation. It replaces a crop that loses the action, and it replaces dead black bars.
- **Variant 0 "Title + clip"** is for a hook title over a montage. An inset 900x506 screen (x 54-954, y 707, radius 6, lit top edge, contact shadow) sits in the middle of the frame, centred on the safe-zone axis (x 504) so its right edge stays clear of the action rail, and the lit room wraps all four sides. It opens from a 127 px slit of footage on frame 0 and closes back to it on the exit. Its light spills into the room and pools in a soft reflection on the floor. Above it sits the title in **Rockstar's own date-card style**: white wide Archivo caps with a hard `#EE08F2` offset and a soft white and magenta bloom ("Welcome to / LEONIDA", 134 px, about 825 px wide). A source line with a live trailer timecode sits below. **Payoff:** on the 2.1 s cut, LEONIDA becomes a window onto the jetski shot itself (video-in-type). The crop starts 2.3x close on the green hull and pulls back as the jetski arrives. It is graded darker and denser than the white title and has a 1.5 px inner white edge, so the knockout is the only colour event in the piece. A light hit and shake land with it. After 0.62 s, the white wipes back right to left, following the jetski out of frame, and the title gets a bloom swell. The sample montage is highway, jetski, sunset dock (a 0.9 s quick cut), sunset pier, then the Launch Trailer balcony sunset to close. It ends on its brightest, sharpest shot, never a hazy one.
- **Variant 1 "Clip + caption"** is for a clip with an opinion on it. An 864x486 inset frame (radius 8, lit edge) sits on the text grid (x 72-936, clear of the action rail). It resolves out of its own glow and throws light down into the caption hung tight beneath it. The caption has a real hierarchy: a 112 px setup line ("Every frame", Inter 700, 86 % white) and a 184 px payoff line ("is unreal.", Inter 800, sunset word). The payoff line slams in as one unit and is sharp by the 1.4 s cut. A 5 px RGB split then runs on that line only, for 0.15 s. The setup line never splits. One 27 px slate row above the frame carries the source and live timecode on the left and the handle on the right. The source label follows the shot (the sample opens on a Launch Trailer shot, then cuts to Trailer 2).

Both read within about 0.8 s. The hit on each is a 2-frame light hit (an exposure push that keeps blacks black, plus a faint warm veil) with shake (and, in v1, a small 5 px RGB split on the payoff line only).

The glow is graded, not left as raw blur. Below the clip, a soft-light ramp deepens the glow and raises its saturation (navy in v0, black in v1). v0 also has a bottom scrim (y 1350-1920 at .4), so the lower fill reads as falloff. A per-shot multiply `tint` gives white sky or spray in the glow the scene's colour (azure on the water, amber at the bar) instead of milky grey. v0 runs a lighter grain (.10) so it doesn't crawl on the flat blur.

- 1080x1920, 30 fps, 6.6 s. Footage always shows (full-frame component).
- Variables:
  - `variant`: `"0"` Title + clip, `"1"` Clip + caption.
  - `bg`: `"plate"` (default) adds the finishing stack: grain, vignette, light leak and the hit light. `"none"` keeps the footage but drops that stack.
components.configDocs:
| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| `handle` | Channel handle, set at the right end of the v1 slate row |
| `fill.blur`, `.brightness`, `.saturate` | The glow: blur in px (default 64), and its default grade (0.70 / 1.65). The room falloff (`#room`) darkens the far edges, and the floor grade (`#floorDeep`, `#floorTint`) deepens everything below the clip |
| `light.gain`, `.contrast`, `.veil`, `.hold`, `.decay` | The hit light (plate only). An exposure push on the footage (`gain`), with a `contrast` term that holds the blacks, plus a warm screen veil (`veil`). It peaks for `hold` s and decays over `decay` s. `variants[n].gain` overrides `gain`: lower it for bright shots so they flare instead of whiting out |
| `fill.zoom`, `fill.drift`, `fill.bleed` | How far the glow is enlarged, its slow push over the piece, and how far (px on the 1/4-size canvas) the glow copy runs past the frame edge, so a lighter blur never shows dark edges |
| `fill.spillBlur`, `.spillBright`, `.spillMax`, `.spillOpacity` | The edge spill: the shot's own edges stretched past the frame, blurred and screen-blended above the room falloff, so the screen throws light into the room. `spillMax` caps its brightness (v0 uses 0.95, so bright day shots glow instead of washing out). `spillOpacity` sets how much light it throws |
| `variants[n].fill` | Per-variant overrides of any `fill` field. v1 uses blur 36, zoom 1.0 and bleed 18, so the glow keeps the scene's structure |
| `variants[n].shots[]` | One entry per shot. `src`, `start`, `dur` and `in` must mirror the `<video>` tags. The rest are listed in the next rows |
| `shots[].tc`, `.focus`, `.glow` | `tc`: where the shot starts in its source video, in seconds (drives the live timecode). `focus`: which stripe of the frame the glow samples, 0 left to 1 right. `glow: [brightness, saturate]` (optional): that shot's glow. Give dark shots 1.0-1.2 so the room stays lit, and light shots 0.55-0.8 |
| `shots[].tint` | Optional `["#colour", strength]`: a multiply grade on the glow while the shot is up, so white sky or spray takes the scene's colour |
| `shots[].credit` (v0) | Optional. The source text before the timecode while this shot is up (defaults to `credit`). Use it when a shot comes from a different trailer. The sample's last shot reads "Rockstar · Launch Trailer", the short form, so the line stays inside the safe zone |
| `shots[].label`, `.scrim`, `.top` (v1) | Optional. `label`: which trailer the shot is from (defaults to `slate`). `scrim`: 0-1, a soft shadow behind the slate row. `top`: 0-1, a top-of-frame scrim. Use `scrim` and `top` on light shots |
| `variants[n].hit` | Time of the payoff: light hit and shake (v1 adds a 5 px split on the payoff line at hit + 0.12). Put it on a cut. In v0 the title takes the footage; in v1 the payoff line slams in |
| `variants["0"].typeFill` | The v0 video-in-type payoff. `shot`: which shot fills the title (it must match the `#t0b` `<video>`). `hold`: how long the footage fills the whole word, in s. `cross`: the length of the white wipe back. `dir`: `1` wipes in from the left, `-1` from the right (follow the subject's travel). `w`, `x`, `y`: the size and offset of the video behind the 864x240 title box; the glyphs sit at about y 81-177 in it. Aim the footage's most colourful band (here the green hull, frame x .54 / y .60) at the word's centre. `zoom: [from, dur]`: the crop starts that much closer and pulls back on the hit (use it when the subject is still small at the cut). `grade`: a CSS filter on the type's footage (darker and denser than the title). `edge: [px, alpha]`: the inner white edge stroke (half of it falls inside the glyph). End `hold + cross` before the subject leaves the frame |
| `variants[n].beat2` | A second, smaller light beat on a later cut (v0: a bloom swell on the title, on the cut into the last shot; v1: the sheen re-fires) |
| `variants["0"].grain` | v0's grain strength (.10). v1 uses the default .12 |
| `variants[n].leak` | Start of the single warm light leak (plate only) |
| `variants[n].out`, `.end` | Exit start and total length |
| `variants["0"].kicker`, `.title`, `.credit` | The small label, the wide hero title (Rockstar date-card style; keep it to about 7-8 characters at 134 px, or lower `#hero` font-size), and the source text before the timecode |
| `variants["1"].slate` | Default source label before the live timecode (a shot's `label` overrides it) |
| `variants["1"].caption`, `.setupSize`, `.payoffSize` | The caption. `\n` breaks the line. Wrap ONE word in `*...*` for the sunset word. The line holding it is the payoff line (`payoffSize`, 184 px: keep it to about 10 characters) and slams in as one unit on the hit. The other lines are setup lines (`setupSize`, 112 px: about 14 characters) and rise word by word at the start |

notes.handle: v1: right end of the slate row, above the frame
notes.fill: the glow behind/around the screen: blur in px, default grade, how far it is enlarged and how much it drifts in bleed = how far (px, on the 1/4-size canvas) the glow copy runs past the frame edge, so the blur never samples empty edges; spillOpacity = how much light the screen throws (variants[n].fill overrides any of these)

MUST mirror the <video> tags (screen copy s.., glow copy f.., spill copy g.. share src + timing). tc = where the shot starts in its source video (seconds): drives the live source timecode. label = which trailer the shot is from (v1 slate; defaults to the variant's slate). scrim = strength (0-1) of the soft shadow behind the v1 slate row while this shot is up (light shots only). top = strength (0-1) of a v1 top-of-frame scrim while this shot is up (light shots only). tint = [colour, strength 0-1]: a multiply grade on the glow while this shot is up, so white sky and spray in        the glow take the scene's colour (amber at the bar, azure on the water) instead of going milky grey. focus = which vertical stripe of the 16:9 frame the glow samples (0 left .. 0.5 centre .. 1 right). glow = [brightness, saturate] of the glow for this shot (optional; dark shots get more, so the room stays lit).

components.name: Release countdown
components.job: Countdown to the release on November 19, 2026: days, hours, minutes rolling, with the platforms line.
components.summary:
A countdown to GTA 6's release on **November 19, 2026**, in two variants. Each is 1080×1920, 30 fps and 7 s, rendered from one HyperFrames project. Use it over the included graded 4K trailer shots, or export it as a transparent overlay. | Variant | Name | What it shows | |---|---|---| | `0` | **Rolling digits** | **A full-bleed countdown where the digits own the frame and every clock tick is a cut.**
• Vertical shots run from day to sunset to night to midnight: a skydive over Vice City, a biplane trailing pink smoke over the beach, a sunset pier, a Vice City night drive under the skyline, then the sequin dancer under blue flares at midnight.
• The countdown fills the top half. A 460 px sunset **30** in Archivo Expanded 900 stands alone, centred (cap y 300–631). Under it is **DAYS LEFT** (Archivo Expanded 800, 64 px, tracked), then the live clock **00:00:03** in Inter 800 at 128 px (cap top y 820). Every digit is an odometer reel that drops in from above with vertical motion blur.
• "GTA 6 · November 19, 2026" in Rockstar's date style and the platforms sit low in the frame at 26 px.
• **Every roll lands on its cut:** each tick's reel starts 0.12 s early (expo.out), so the new digit has settled by the cut frame.
• **Payoff (4.2 s):** at midnight the day rolls 30 → **29** on the hard cut to the club, with a scale punch, and the clock cascades to **23:59:59**. A warm additive flash (screen blend, `#FFE2B8`, peak 0.28), a shake and an RGB split land with it. The numeral's bloom spikes in the warm light and settles into the club's blue, then a sheen crosses the new day count.
• The club shot holds to the end as one speed ramp: slow motion through the hair whip, the sequins and the flare, then back to real time as the type exits and the dancer turns into the neon. | | `1` | **One day left** | **A launch-eve poster title over full-bleed golden-hour footage.**
• The title block is left-aligned in the lower half, so faces stay clear above it. A big sunset numeral sits beside **DAYS / LEFT**, stacked to the numeral's cap height.
• The numeral counts **3 → 2 → 1** on the cuts: the sunset dock, the couple on the balcony, then Lucia at the gate.
• **Payoff (2.9 s):** the "1" slams in on the cut to Lucia and the "S" of DAYS drops out. A flash, shake, warm light leak across the top of the frame and RGB split land with it. The "1" blooms golden, DAY / LEFT catch the light, and a sheen crosses the "1".
• A big live clock, **23:59:01 TO GO**, drops in under the lockup at the words' size, with the platforms underneath. It ticks every second, and the minutes roll over to 23:58:59 at 5.8 s.
• Lucia holds to the end with a slow push. The clip is pre-slowed with motion interpolation, so it is smooth, with no repeated frames. | **Exits are designed:** - **v0:** from 6.2 s, on the ramp back to real time, the reels roll their last values away, the letters of DAYS LEFT fall and fade out of their line, the footer blurs out and the scrims lift. The first frame and the final frames (from about 6.75 s) are clean footage with no type. - **v1:** the "1" and the clock reels roll away, the words' letters fall and fade out of their lines, and the small lines blur out. **When to use it in a GTA 6 short** - **Variant 0:** the opener or closer of a "days until GTA 6" post, a hype compilation or a news recap. Set `from` to the moment you post; the days, hours, minutes and seconds follow. - **Variant 1:** launch-eve posts ("GTA 6 is out tomorrow"), reaction videos and "who's calling in sick" clips. Use it as the first 3 s over your best clip. **Safe zone.** All type stays inside the 9:16 safe zone (x 72–936, y 230–1480), clear of the like/comment rail and the caption area. - **v0:** numeral cap y 300–631 (ink about x 180–900, at most 792 px wide, centred). DAYS LEFT y 677–723, the clock y 820–913. Date and platforms y 1336–1405. - **v1:** block y 927–1405, x 84–913.

components.name: Wanted level
components.job: Wanted stars that fill one by one (1→5) as a clip escalates. Sparse and thin like Rockstar's real GTA VI HUD (our own star drawing).
components.configDocs:
| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `stars` | Five times in seconds, one per star. Default `[0.40, 1.30, 2.35, 3.20, 4.50]`. Move them to your clip's cuts and hits. |
| `reasons` | Five reason badges, in fill order. Glyphs: `witness` (eye), `call` (handset with call waves), `shots` (crosshair), `vehicle` (police car), `heli`. |
| `strobe` | The police light after the fifth star. It runs `from` (4.50) to `to` (5.50), then fades over `fade` (0.30). Red and blue alternate in `stepFrames` (4) frame steps; `shape` is a step's per-frame intensity, and `first` is the colour on the hit. It drives the corner washes (footage renders only) and the colour of the stars' bloom (both renders). |
| `starLight` | The lit stars' bloom: white at `rest` (0.5), police-coloured at `police` (0.6) while the strobe runs; both spike ×`spike` (1.6) on the hit and settle over 0.9 s. |
| `variants[*].strobePeak` | The red and blue corner-wash peak opacity (v0 `.95/.95`; v1 `.8/.8`). |
| `variants["0"].unfill` | The HUD corner exit: stars un-fill from `at` (5.50), one every `stagger` (0.04 s), each over `dur` (0.1 s), star 1 (rightmost) first. Each badge drops with its star. |
| `variants["0"].exit` | Then the empty row blurs out: `at` (5.68), `dur` (0.3), `blur` (6 px), `y` (−12 px), `stagger` (0.012). |
| `variants[*].hit` | The fifth-star exposure (footage renders only). `shot` is the video playing at the hit. `flash` is overlay-white on the hit frame (half on the next). `exposure` is a brightness kick that decays over 4 frames. `grade` is that shot's resting filter and must match the `#d0, #d1` CSS rule. |
| `variants["1"].label` | The small tracked label above the title (default "Wanted level"). |
| `variants["1"].names` | Two-line titles, e.g. `["Shots", "fired"]` (default three). |
| `variants["1"].titleAt` | Which star (index 0–4) each title lands on (default `[0, 2, 4]`). Keep at least 1.4 s between titles. |
| `variants["1"].slamLead` | How early the last title starts rising before the fifth-star hit (0.16 s), so it's up on the flash frame. |
| `variants["1"].titleMax` | The widest a title line may be, in px (default 780). The size steps down from 132 px if your longest line is wider. |
| `variants["1"].ghost` | WANTED's offset ghost on five stars: `px` (3), `frames` per step (2), for `dur` (0.6 s). |
| `variants[*].shots` | Documents the sample cut list. Edit the matching `<video>` tags to change it. |
| `newStarBlink` | HUD corner: the step length of the double blink on stars 1–4 (default 0.1 s, 3 frames). |
| `payoff` | The fifth-star hit: shake `amp` (12 px), punch `zoom` (1.045), `chromaPx` (12). |
| `pushes` | A slow push-in per shot, per variant: `[start, duration, fromScale, toScale]`. From the hit, `s119` pushes on to 1.08. |
| `pushOrigin` | Where the pushes aim (`42% 34%`, toward the flip). |
| `timing` | `out` (Centre hero exit start, 5.58 s), `outDur` (0.42 s), `end` (6.1 s). If you change `end`, also change `data-duration` on `#root` and `#ov`, and keep the exits finishing on or before the last frame. |

Star geometry (inner radius .40, keyline, facets, shade) is in the star block of the CSS and the star-path code (`const D` in the script). Sizes and gaps are in the `.v0` / `.v1` CSS rules.

notes.stars: Seconds at which each star lights (1→5). Each one sits on a cut; the fifth sits on the in-shot hit (s119 frame 68: the police SUV's nose lifts off the road), and the flip then plays at full speed under the maxed row.
notes.reasons: One dark-red reason badge joins under each new star. Glyphs: witness, call, shots, vehicle, heli.
notes.strobe: police light after the fifth star: hard red/blue alternation in `stepFrames` (4 frames ≈ 0.13 s) steps, `first` on the hit. `shape` is a step's per-frame intensity. It drives the top-corner washes (footage renders only) AND the stars' bloom colour (both renders): the star fills stay white, only their light turns red or blue. Runs `from`–`to`, then fades.
notes.starLight: the lit stars' bloom (Look.bloom recipe as SVG drop-shadows): white at `rest`; police-coloured at `police` while the strobe runs; both spike ×`spike` on the hit and settle over 0.9 s.
notes.newStarBlink: HUD corner: stars 1–4 blink on/off/on/off/on in 0.1 s (3-frame) steps
notes.payoff: fifth-star shake (px), punch zoom and RGB split; the flash is variants[*].hit
notes.pushes: per-shot push-in (footage only): [start, duration, fromScale, toScale]. From the hit, s119 pushes on to 1.08 toward the flip (origin `pushOrigin`), continuing the 1× shot's own push with no jump.
notes.timing: Centre hero exit; the HUD corner uses variants["0"].unfill / exit

components.name: Wasted stamp
components.job: The fail sting: footage desaturates and slows, a dark band slides in and the word lands. Our own type (no Pricedown).
components.summary:
The fail sting for GTA 6 compilation shorts, staged as a death-cam:
- The clip runs at real speed.
- On the hit, the world drops into smooth slow motion that keeps slowing, drains to hard black-and-white and snaps into a cinematic letterbox band (1080×820, closing in to 1080×680, about 1.6:1).
- A dark GTA-style ribbon (a flat .82 core with a short feather, edge to edge) slides in across it. The word slams onto it in wide Archivo caps, lit by its own bloom: a tracking slam, blur, a short RGB split, and an exposure flash and shake on the footage only.
- The top bar carries one line of meta: a time-coded kicker that belongs to the moment ("TIME OF DEATH · 14:32") over WASTED, or the five wanted stars over BUSTED.
- In Busted only the police lights keep their colour: the light bar burns blue and the tail lights red in a crushed black-and-white frame, pulsing with the word's bloom.
- A second beat lands in the hold: a glint sweeps across WASTED, or the wanted stars empty out.
- The type blurs out, the dark band slides away and the letterbox shuts like an eye. The comp ends as it shuts, so you can cut straight to the next clip.

It uses our own type (Archivo), not Pricedown, and no logos.

**When to use it:** at the payoff of a fail, crash, wipe-out or arrest in a "GTA 6 fails", "funniest GTA 6 moments" or "cops in GTA 6" compilation, or as a hard beat to end a clip. The win counterpart is #10 Mission passed.

| Variant | Word | Hit | Style |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0` Wasted | WASTED, lit red, centred in the band on the ribbon; time-of-death kicker in the top bar | Hard cut to the slowed 16:9 master in the band, bars cut in, white flash | Hard black-and-white with a highlight roll-off; a narrow warm glint crosses the word at about 3.7 s |
| `1` Busted | BUSTED, white-hot steel (the blue lives in the lights), on the ribbon in the band's lower third; five wanted stars in the top bar | Speed ramp on the same shot; the bars cut in wide and clamp down; blue flash | Crushed noir mono with only the police lights in colour; the lights and the bloom pulse together; the stars empty right to left |

Timeline (5.0 s, 30 fps):
- **0–1.2 s:** real speed.
- **1.12 s:** the dark band starts sliding in from the left, motion-blurred.
- **1.2 s, the hit (frame 36):** the cut or speed ramp, the letterbox (an 820 px band; Busted's cuts in at 880 and clamps to 820 over 0.3 s), the flash, the shake, and the word slam with an 8 px RGB split. The colour drains over 0.45 s; in Busted the police lights fade back in as colour.
- **1.5 s:** the kicker rises in char by char (Wasted) or the stars pop in (Busted), in the top bar.
- **1.8–4.5 s:** the band closes in 820 → 680 px (Wasted y 620–1300; Busted y 540–1220), with a slow push on the footage and a slow drift of the word's scale and tracking. Wasted's slow motion eases from 0.32x to 0.20x as the SUV goes over.
- **3.2–4.2 s:** the glint sweeps across WASTED (Wasted). **3.2–4.0 s:** the stars empty (Busted).
- **4.3 s:** the type blurs out, then the dark band slides off to the right.
- **4.5–5.0 s:** the letterbox shuts. The comp ends on the last sliver, with no black tail.
components.configDocs:
All content is in `const CONFIG` at the top of the script in `index.html`.

- `variants["0" | "1"]`
  - `word`: the stamp word. It is set in caps and auto-fits to `layout.wordWidth`, so "CLAPPED" or "FAILED" also fit.
  - `fill`: the word's gradient (CSS `linear-gradient`). Put the stops at about 24–82%, because the word box is 1.16em tall and the ramp has to span the cap height.
  - `glow`: the bloom colour (hex).
  - `bloom`: the bloom strength, as a number (steady) or `{base, swing, hz}` (a police light-bar pulse).
  - `kicker`: one tracked line in the top bar that belongs to the moment, e.g. `"Time of death · 14:32"` (26 px Archivo wide, 70% white; `null` hides it). Stars take this slot if `stars` is set.
  - `stars`: the number of wanted stars in the top bar, which empty out (0 = none).
  - `rule`: optional `{color, width}` for a short drawn rule under the word (`null` hides it; off by default).
  - `label`: an optional tracked line under the word; it replaces the rule (`null` hides it). The dark band grows to hold it.
  - `sheen`: `{color, peak, width}` sweeps one narrow glint across the word in the hold. `width` is a fraction of the word's width (0.09) and `peak` is its maximum opacity (0.45). `null` turns it off.
  - `flash`: `{color, amount}` for the exposure flash on the footage at the hit.
  - `grade`: the plate-mode grade after the drain:
    - `curve` is an optional tone curve: 11 output values for inputs 0, .1 … 1. Wasted's `[0,.06,.16,.28,.40,.52,.63,.73,.82,.89,.94]` is a highlight shoulder, so sunlit road paint and smoke keep their texture instead of clipping to flat white. Busted's `[0,.14,.33,.52,.66,.77,.86,.92,.96,.99,1]` crushes the shadows of a dark dusk plate to true black and lifts the upper mids;
    - then `contrast`, `brightness`, `tint` (hex or `null`) and `tintOpacity`.
  - `lights` (optional, Busted): `{id, src, amount, swing}`, a baked selective-colour layer (see `lights.py` below), multiplied over the mono slow clip. Its opacity is `amount ± swing`, pulsing with the bloom.
  - `leadGrade` (optional): `{brightness, contrast}` for the real-speed lead, e.g. to lift a dim clip. The drain starts from it. Keep contrast near 1 on dark plates, because contrast pulls their mids down.
  - `lockupY` (optional): the y the word is centred on (default: the band centre). The ribbon centres on the word. Busted uses 1070, the band's lower third, so the arrest plays above the ribbon.
  - `bandCenter` (optional): moves this variant's letterbox band off-centre to frame its footage. Busted uses 880, so the band's bottom edge lands on the bumper and the POV dashboard stays behind the bottom bar.
  - `bars`: `"cut"` (the letterbox arrives on the hit frame) or `"clamp"` (it cuts in at `layout.bandClamp` on the hit frame, then clamps to `bandOpen` over 0.3 s). `bg:none` always slams in over 0.34 s.
  - `lead`: the real-speed shot(s) before the hit. Each takes `{id, src, start, dur, in, y}`: `in` is the source in-point and `y` a vertical offset in px.
  - `slow`: the pre-baked slow-motion file played from the hit, `{id, src, rate, box:{x, y, w, h}}`. `box` places it on the canvas.
    - For a 16:9 source, use about `w: 1560, h: 878` and shift it so the action fills the 680–820 px band and any game HUD falls outside the visible columns.
    - For a speed ramp on a vertical clip, use the same framing as the lead (`x: 0, y: 0, w: 1080, h: 1920`) so the ramp is seamless.
  - `push`: `{lead:[from,to], slow:[from,to]}`, the slow camera pushes. For a speed ramp, start `slow` where `lead` ends.
- `layout`:
  - `bandCenter`, `bandOpen`, `bandHold`, `bandClamp`: the band centre and heights (960; 820 → 680 px; the clamp starts at 880).
  - `wordSize`, `wordWidth`: the start size and the fit width (keep the width ≤ 760).
  - `capRatio`: cap height ÷ font size, used for optical centring.
  - `tracking`, `trackingIn`, `trackingHold`: settled, slam-in and hold tracking, in em.
  - `metaGap`: the gap from the caps to an optional rule or label.
  - `stripH`, `stripPadMin`: the ribbon's height (210 px: a flat 82% black core, a short 10% feather, no hairlines) and the minimum space it leaves above and below the word.
  - `barMetaGap`: how far above the band's held top edge the kicker or stars are centred (76 px).
- `timing`: `hit`, `stripLead`, `drain`, `meta`, `rule`, `sheen`, `sheenDur`, `starsClear`, `out`, `close`, `closeDur`, `end` (seconds). Keep `end = close + closeDur`.

variants.kindEvidence: transparent overlay: bars, ground band, word, kicker / stars only — no footage, grade, flash, grain or vignette

components.name: Mission passed
components.job: The win sting: 'MISSION PASSED' lands with a sub-line and a rolling cash reward; the clean counterpart to the fail stamp.
components.summary:
The GTA result sting, built as a trailer title rather than a UI strip (craft v2). A real-speed action shot cuts on the beat into the result, and the grade tells you which result it was. Every shot plays at 1.0x.

- **Passed + payout** (variant `0`). Over the stunt (a biker riding beside a seaplane), **MISSION PASSED** rises in one wide white line in the sky. At 1.1 s the edit cuts to golden hour on the pier, and the payout **$25,000** (216 px, Leonida sunset gradient, the currency set small and raised) rises in with motion blur and counts up. It **lands at 1.55 s**: a 1.07 punch, an exposure pulse on the footage held for 2 frames, a warm anamorphic streak held for 0.2 s, a kick, and a sheen across the figure. The edit keeps cutting under it (the leap over Vice City at 2.6 s, the jetski at 4.2 s). The lockup blurs out at 4.5 s, before the riders rise into it.
- **Mission failed** (variant `1`). A Vice City police car slides through a sunny junction and `MISSION` tracks in. At 1.0 s **FAILED** slams in red on the cut to the drive-by past the police, and the world drains to cold mono: **only bright red survives** (the police lights, the tail lights and the word). An exposure pulse peaks on the hit frame and holds for 3 frames, with a shake and a punch-zoom. The reason, `The cops got there first.`, rises under it. At 2.6 s it cuts to the shootout (the police SUV charges and flips), still drained, and ends on the daylight street.

Use it in a GTA 6 compilation short:
- after a clean escape, a stunt landing or a lucky save (passed, with the payout as the punchline);
- after a crash, a bust or a cringe moment (failed, with the reason as the joke);
- as a sting between clips.

It reads in under a second and holds for about 3 s. Passed blurs out at 4.5 s (gone by about 5.0 s). Failed blurs out at 4.85 s (gone by about 5.35 s). Both are 5.4 s.

| Variant | Name | Look |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | Passed + payout | biker and seaplane, golden pier, leap over Vice City, jetski; one wide white line over a 216 px sunset-gradient payout that lands at 1.55 s with an exposure pulse and a warm streak |
| `1` | Mission failed | daylight police slide, then the drive-by and the shootout in cold mono with only bright red kept; red FAILED slams on the cut with an exposure pulse |

1080×1920, 30 fps. The lockup is set flush left on one optical column (the ink edge of every line sits at x = 96) in the top band, y about 234–494, inside the platform-safe box. There is no rule and no card; legibility comes from a soft top shade and lift shadows.
- Passed: `MISSION PASSED` (Archivo wide 900, about 66 px, sized to the payout's measure) over `$25,000` (Inter 800, 216 px, tabular figures). Both are about 760 px wide.
- Failed: `MISSION` (Archivo wide 700, 30 px, tracked) / `FAILED` (Archivo wide 900, 164 px, fitted to ≤ 780 px) / the reason (Inter 600, 40 px, sentence case).
components.configDocs:
- `variants["0" | "1"]`
  - `state`: `"passed"` (line + payout) or `"failed"` (kicker + red word + reason, cold mono grade with red kept).
  - `shots`: one entry per `<video>` this variant shows, in order: `{ id, at, dur, from, to, origin }`. `at`/`dur` must match the video's `data-start`/`data-duration`. `from`/`to` is the slow camera push on that shot; `origin` (optional) is its transform origin (`"50% 0%"` pushes from the top, so a head under the type sinks away from it).
  - Passed:
    - `line`: the result line (`"Mission passed"`). It is auto-sized (56–72 px) to the payout's width.
    - `reward`: `{ amount, prefix }`. `amount` is a whole number, comma-grouped, that counts up from 0. `prefix` (`"$"` or `"+$"`) is set at 0.42 of the digit size and raised to the digit tops.
    - `hit`: the cut where the payout rises in (1.1 s). `land`: when the count lands and the light hits (1.55 s).
  - Failed:
    - `kicker`: the small tracked word (`"Mission"`). `word`: the hero (`"Failed"`, fitted to ≤ 780 px).
    - `reason`: the creator line under the word, in sentence case (keep it to about 30 characters).
    - `hit`: the cut, the slam, the exposure pulse and the drain (1.0 s).
  - `out`: when the lockup blurs out (passed 4.5 s, failed 4.85 s).
- `colors`: `sunset` (payout gradient), `warmBloom` (glow on the passed line), `fail` (the red word's gradient, lit from above), `failBloom`.
- `grade`:
  - `pass`: a mild CSS contrast/saturation lift on the passed footage.
  - `fail`: one entry per drained shot, `{ at, lift, offset }` (the mono brightness and black level; the dusk drive-by gets more lift than the daylight shootout). `failCold` is the cold R/G/B cast. The red-keeping mask is `#isoMask` in the SVG filter at the top of `<body>` (`alpha = 6R − 6G − B − 2.4`: bright reds pass; shaded reds, skin, amber and sparks do not).
- `layout`:
  - `x`: the optical column. `ink`: per-line side-bearing offsets (px), measured from a render so each line's visible ink sits on `x`. Re-measure if you change the face or the first letter.
  - `lineTop`, `lineSize`, `cashTop`, `cashSize`, `cashMaxW`, `cashMin`, `curScale`: the passed lockup. The payout shrinks only if it is wider than `cashMaxW`, never below `cashMin` (200 px).
  - `kickTop`, `heroTop`, `heroSize`, `heroMaxW`, `reasonTop`: the failed lockup.
- `timing`: `line` (passed line reveal, 0.18 s), `kicker` (failed kicker, 0.62 s), `reason` (seconds after the hit, 0.3), `end` (5.4 s).

components.name: News chyron
components.job: In-world style breaking-news lower third with a LIVE tag and a ticker, for leak/news segments. Our own fictional network name, not Weazel.
components.summary:
A TV news break-in for leak, rumour and news segments in GTA 6 shorts. It comes from our own fictional station, **VCN · Vice City News**, not Weazel. It frames a clip as breaking or live news, the way top parody shorts use the Weazel chyron and Rockstar's own MEGA NOTICIAS segment, but built as a clean broadcast package. The bands are flat and hard-edged, bleed off the left edge of the frame, and use type at title scale.

Use it over the clip that carries the news beat: a release-date reminder, a leak, a record, or a "people are calling in sick" story.
components.configDocs:
| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| `network.mark` | Station mark ("VCN"), shown in the v0 logo box (the stinger and the chyron), the v0 tonal texture and the v1 ticker label |
| `variants[v].shots` | The `<video>` ids this variant shows. The cut points are the `data-start` / `data-duration` / `data-media-start` on those tags. |
| `variants[v].push` | `[from, to, endScale]` slow push for each shot |
| `["0"].stinger` | `lines` (e.g. `["Special", "Report"]`, auto-fit up to 108 px); `cut`, when the shots cut under the wipe (it must cover the whole frame then); `clear`, when its trailing edge leaves the frame |
| `["0"].hit` | The payoff: the paper slab locks and the last headline line slams in |
| `["0"].tag`, `clock` | Red band label, and the clock shown in the logo box's clock cell |
| `["0"].headline` | 1–2 lines at 120 px Archivo; auto-fits an 832 px measure, minimum 88 px. The last line slams on `hit`. |
| `["0"].subs`, `swaps`, `out` | Deck lines, the times they swap (put them on your cuts), and the exit start |
| `["1"].live`, `location`, `clock` | LIVE bug text, and the clock start `{h, m, s, suffix}`. The clock ticks every second. |
| `["1"].figure` | The hero figure ("1.5M"). Its digits spin on reels; other characters stay static. |
| `["1"].words` | Three short lines locked up beside the figure (auto-fit to the space left) |
| `["1"].sub` | Subline under the lock-up |
| `["1"].slam` | Time the last reel stops: flash, shake, scale punch and RGB split. Put it on a cut. |
| `["1"].ticker` | Short ticker items. The first one should fit the 670 px window (about 28 characters). |
| `["1"].tickerOpenAt`, `tickerReadAt`, `tickerSpeed` | The ticker lands with the last item whole at the left edge at `tickerOpenAt`, and reaches the first item at `tickerReadAt`. The speed is solved from those two times and clamped to `tickerSpeed` `[min, max]` px/s. |
| `look.grain`, `look.vignette` | Finishing strength (plate renders only) |
| `timing.out`, `end` | Exit start and composition end |

components.name: Location card
components.job: Location reveal for a new area of Leonida: name, region, small coordinates.
components.summary:
A place-name reveal for a GTA 6 short that cuts to a new part of Leonida, such as "now we're in Vice City" or "this is the Keys". Use it on the first clip of a new area in a map tour, an "every location in GTA 6" compilation or a "trailer locations explained" short. It runs 6 s, and the graphic clears on its own by about 5.9 s, so it loops or cuts cleanly.

| Variant | Look | Where it sits |
|---|---|---|
| `0` Official wide caps | Rockstar's date-card language at title scale. A small "NOW ENTERING" kicker sits over a big white Archivo wide-caps name, with a justified foot below: region, a light rule, and the coordinates in mono. The name resolves centre-out through blur while its tracking tightens. On the first cut it locks with a flash, a shake and an RGB split that decays into the #EE08F2 magenta edge and bloom. Sample: a 4-shot Vice City montage (highway → skyline skydive → biplane beach → sunset pier). | The sky band, y ≈ 318–620, over a soft top scrim |
| `1` Pin pill | A map pin dropped into the shot. The needle falls with motion blur and plants on a point in the footage: flash, shake, a ground shockwave and a chroma hit. A frosted-glass label then unfurls from the sunset-pink pin head: the name in Inter Display 800 (~97 px) and the coordinates rolling to a lock. Ground rings ping while it holds, and the pin rides the shot through a tracked path. Sample: a held, slowed aerial of a marina. | Floating above the planted point (sample: y ≈ 235–515, x ≈ 144–914) |
components.configDocs:
- **`variants["0" | "1"]`**
  - `name`: the place name. v0 sets it in caps and auto-fits it to `layout.heroWidth`; v1 auto-fits it to `layout.nameMaxWidth`.
  - `lat`, `lon`: decimal degrees, where negative means S or W. They roll in like a GPS lock. The demo uses the real-world places each area is modelled on (Miami, Florida Keys), so treat them as flavour.
  - `kicker` (v0 only): the line above the title ("Now entering").
  - `region` (v0 only): the word left of the rule ("Leonida").
- **`layout`**
  - **v0**
    - `lockTop`: y of the lockup.
    - `heroWidth`: the title's locked ink width (760 = 88% of the safe width).
    - `heroSize`: the title's minimum and maximum size in px.
    - `heroTrack`: the tracking in em at the start of the entrance and once locked.
    - `scrimOverlay`: `{height, peak}` for the top scrim on `bg:"none"` renders.
  - **v1**
    - `needle`: the needle length in px.
    - `nameSize`, `nameMaxWidth`: the name's size range and fit width.
    - `track`: `[t, x, y]` points the pin follows.
    - `anchorOffset`: from the tracked feature to the planted tip.
    - `trackZoom`: how much the sample shot zooms. It scales the offset.
- **`timing`**
  - `end`: the total length (6 s).
  - **v0**
    - `cuts`: the cut times. The hit lands on `cuts[0]`; keep these equal to the `data-start` values of the v0 videos.
    - `heroIn`: when the title starts to resolve.
    - `out0`: when the exit starts.
  - **v1**
    - `drop`: when the pin starts to fall.
    - `land`: the plant and the hit.
    - `out1`: when the exit starts.
