components.name: Source tag
components.job: Small credit tag for each clip: 'Footage: Rockstar Games · Trailer 2' or the creator's @handle, sits in a safe corner.
components.summary:
A per-clip credit for GTA 6 compilation shorts. On the first clip, the credit arrives at title scale, like a trailer end card. On the cut it collapses into a safe corner, where it holds as a quiet credit for the rest of the clip and changes on every cut. Use it on "every detail from the trailers" edits, "best GTA 6 clips" compilations, or any short that reuses someone else's footage. Viewers see where each clip came from, and the credit never fights the footage after its first moment.

| Variant | Name | Look | Docks to | Sample footage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0` | Footage chip | Rockstar end-card credit style: an outlined **FOOTAGE** chip and the source in tracked wide caps; the detail ("TRAILER 2") in wide Archivo caps with Rockstar's magenta offset; a running source timecode in mono. Re-credits on every cut. | top-left (x 72, y 252) | `s055` Trailer 2 night → `s011` Trailer 2 highway → `s135` PlayStation Features Trailer → `s074` Launch Trailer |
| `1` | Handle tag | Creator credit: "CLIP VIA" and the @handle in tight Inter display with a sunset "@"; it docks beside a monogram avatar whose ring draws in | bottom-left (bottom edge y 1460) | golden-hour cut: `s027` → `s084` → `s108` → `s026` → `s036` |

**Timeline (7 s, 30 fps):**
- **0.1 s:** the announce. The chip/label row blurs in, the hero rises out of its mask by character, and the timecode settles.
- **Dock on the cut into clip 2** (1.6 s in v0, 1.85 s in v1). This is the payoff: every row flies to its docked twin (0.5 s `expo.inOut`) with a travel smear. On plate renders there is an exposure flash, a shake and a punch-zoom, and an RGB split on the type. v1 adds a sunset light leak, and its avatar pops in with a drawn ring.
- **Every later cut (v0):** the source and detail hard-swap on the cut frame, settle out of a soft blur and take a decaying RGB split. The timecode jumps to the new clip's real source time.
- **6.35 s:** exit, blurring out row by row. Gone by about 6.85 s.

**Plate renders** use the 4K graded shots, a slow push on every shot, and the Look finishing layer (grain and vignette). **`bg:none`** is a clean transparent overlay: no footage, grain, vignette, flash or leak. Only the soft legibility scrims behind the type remain.
components.configDocs:
- `variants["0"]` (Footage chip)
  - `chip`: the outlined label, default `"Footage"`.
  - `timecode`, `tcLabel`: show the running source timecode row, and its label (`"TC"`).
  - `announce`: `{ align: "center", top: 392 }` sets the position of the title-scale credit on the first clip. Set `announce: null` for a corner tag only; it then rises in at `timing.in`.
  - `clips`: one entry per clip, in order: `{ video, source, detail, srcIn }`.
    - `video`: the id of the `<video>` that plays the clip. Its `data-start` is the cut time.
    - `source`: who owns the footage (`"Rockstar Games"`, `"PlayStation"`).
    - `detail`: which video (`"Trailer 2"`, `"Features Trailer"`, `"Launch Trailer"`).
    - `srcIn`: where the shot starts in that source video, in seconds. The TC row shows `srcIn + data-media-start + time into the clip`.
    - When source or detail changes between clips, the tag swaps on that cut. When neither changes, only the timecode jumps.
  - `corner`: `"tl"`, `"tr"`, `"bl"` or `"br"`. Right corners right-align the rows.
  - `size`: `bigRow`, `bigHeroMax`, `bigHeroWidth`, `bigTc`, `dockRow`, `dockHeroMax`, `dockHeroWidth`, `dockTc`. The heroes are measured and fitted, so long details stay inside the safe width.
- `variants["1"]` (Handle tag)
  - `label` (`"Clip via"`), `handle` (`"@everestchris6"`), `initials` (the avatar monogram, `"EC"`).
  - `clips`: the `<video>` ids of the creator's clip. `corner`, `announce` and `size` work as in v0 (`dockRow`, `dockHero`).
- `safe`: the docking insets (`left 72`, `right 936`, `top 252`, `bottom 1460`), inside the 9:16 safe zone.
- `timing`:
  - `in`: the announce start.
  - `dockClip`: the tag docks on the cut into this clip index; default 1.
  - `travel`: the flight time.
  - `out`: the exit start.
  - `end`: the total duration.
- `colors`: `magenta` (the Rockstar offset), `sunset` (the "@" fill), `leak` (the v1 light leak).

notes.safe: 9:16 safe zone (DESIGN.md): x 72–936, y 230–1480. The tag docks inside these insets.

components.name: Circle callout
components.job: Points out a detail: a clean ring draws around it, a leader line runs to a label pill ('Real-time reflections').
components.summary:
Points out one detail in a clip by drawing on the footage itself. A mark locks onto the detail and follows it, a fine leader line runs to a cinematic label set in the image's own negative space, and the moment the mark closes is the payoff hit.

Use it in "details you missed", "GTA 6 graphics are insane" and side-by-side detail shorts, whenever the voiceover says "look at the…" and the viewer needs to know *where* to look. One callout per shot works best. Number them (`Detail 01`, `Detail 02`…) across a list.

- **Variant 0, Ring + label.** A ring of light in the Leonida sunset gradient draws clockwise around the detail, led by a white-hot pen head. When it closes: a warm exposure bloom on the detail, a specular glint sweeps across the lens inside the ring, the footage punches in on the detail with a short shake, and the ring splits RGB. The leader leaves the ring at 9 o'clock, runs left and drops down the frame's dark edge to a pin, and the label rises out of masks below it: `— DETAIL 01` over **Real-time / reflections** in Inter display (about 150 px). Sample: Jason's mirrored sunglasses in `s008` (Jason driving), which reflect the street going by.
- **Variant 1, Bracket + label.** Four white focus-lock corners fly in from wide with motion blur and snap onto the detail. On the lock: the corners flare white-hot, a warm bloom lands on the detail, the footage punches in with a short shake, the corners split RGB, and the frame outside the brackets dims a touch, like a camera finding focus. A pin on the middle of the box's top edge sends a leader up to the label: `— DETAIL 02` over **CLOTH / PHYSICS** in Archivo wide caps (about 118 px), with PHYSICS in the sunset fill and a specular sheen. Sample: the palm-print sleeve in `s004`, which folds and swings as he gestures.

1080×1920, 30 fps, 5.0 s. The mark is on screen from frame 3, the payoff lands at about 0.6 s, the label reads by about 1.2 s and holds to 4.3 s, then the type drops back into its masks, the leader retracts and the mark un-draws (ring) or opens out (brackets). Everything is clear by about 4.95 s, so the clip loops.

On the sample footage the mark is **motion-tracked** (SSD template tracking, one sample every 0.1 s in `CONFIG`). The label never moves while it's being read; the leader re-aims every frame. The footage push and the punch-zoom both pivot on the detail, so the mark stays locked.

Circle something the viewer can verify at a glance, and make the label say exactly what is inside the mark. Keep the label off faces and hands.

components.name: Magnifier zoom
components.job: A lens that pulls a 2.5× zoom of one region of the footage into an inset, joined to the spot by a leader, with a label.
components.summary:
A detail lifts off the footage. A mark draws on one tracked spot of the clip. Then a loupe (v0) or a framed plate (v1) grows out of that spot as an exact copy of the footage under it and flies to its seat while the magnification climbs to 2.5×. It lands on a hit: flash, shake, RGB split and a glass sheen. While the inset is up, the rest of the frame racks out of focus (blurred and darkened, with a sharp hole at the spot), and the hero line rises in the bottom band. At the end the type drops away, the inset flies home and lands as a 1:1 copy of the footage, and the world refocuses. The zoom reads a **native-pixel master** of the same shot (cut from Rockstar's 2160p Trailer 2), so it shows real detail rather than an enlarged blur.

**When to use it in a GTA 6 short:** the "details you missed" beat. The clip keeps playing, with no freeze, while the lens pulls out the small thing worth talking about: a print, a sign, a plate, a tattoo, a reflection or a HUD icon. Use it once per reveal, on a steady shot, for 3–5 s while you say the line.

| Variant | Name | Look |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | Round lens | A 560 px optical loupe over the dark part of the frame: 3 px white rim with bloom, edge falloff, specular and a faint chromatic edge, plus a fine tick ring that turns into place as it lands. A drawn ring with N/E/S/W ticks marks the spot, joined by tangent lines and a faint light cone. The hero is Archivo wide caps, "TINY **BEACH**" (sunset on BEACH), with the kicker "HIS SHIRT · 2.5×". |
| `1` | Inset card | A framed detail plate (580×518) with square corners, a 2 px white frame and viewfinder brackets. The spot is a focus box (corner brackets closing in, plus a hairline), and projection lines carry the light up into the plate. The hero is Inter display, "A whole **beach**", with a JetBrains Mono kicker "TRAILER 2 · 0:14 · 2.5×". |

Both variants are 1080×1920, 30 fps and 5.0 s. Timeline: mark 0.15 s → lift 0.50 s → **hit 1.00 s** → hold → type out 3.90 s → inset home 4.10–4.42 s → mark gone 4.66 s → clean shot to 5.0 s (a handle for your next cut). Hero frame: 2.0 s.
components.configDocs:
- `clip`: the shot. **Also change the static `src` of `#plate`.**
- `zoomClip { src, x, y, w, h }`: the clip the zoom reads, and the rectangle of the 1080×1920 frame its picture covers. The sample is `assets/zoom/s004-shirt-zoom.mp4` at `x 240, y 800, w 640, h 600` (a 1600×1500 master, exactly 1:1 at 2.5×). With no sharper source, use the shot itself: `{ src: clip, x: 0, y: 0, w: 1080, h: 1920 }`. **Also change the static `src` of `#zoom`.**
- `zoom`: magnification (2.5). The mark is the inset size ÷ zoom.
- `push { from, to }`: the slow camera push on the held shot (1.00 → 1.05). The mark follows it automatically.
- `defocus { blur, dim, contrast, saturate }`: what happens to the world outside the spot while the inset is up (8 px, 0.4, 1.1, 1.06).
- `track { fps, pts }`: the spot centre in frame pixels, sampled `fps` times a second from t = 0, as `[x0,y0, x1,y1, ...]`. Give one point for a still subject.
- `typeTop`: the mark is softly held above this line (1296 px) so it never runs into the type band.
- `variants["0"]` (Round lens): `kicker`, `hero` (two words: the second gets the sunset fill), `lens { x, y, r }` (seat centre and radius; the sample is 378, 556, 280), `nudge [dx, dy]` (shifts the track to frame the detail).
- `variants["1"]` (Inset card): `kicker` (real context, such as the source and timestamp), `hero` (two parts: the second gets the sunset fill), `plate { x, y, w, h }` (the sample is 86, 272, 580, 518; keep the brackets, 14 px outside, inside x 72–936), `nudge`.
- `timing`: `spot`, `lift`, `land` (the hit), `settle`, `typeOut`, `back`, `backDur`, `clear` and `end`, in seconds.

The hero line auto-fits to the 864 px safe width (it steps the size down if a longer line would overflow). Keep it to one short line: two words in v0's wide face, about 13 characters in v1.

components.name: Arrow pointer
components.job: A clean drawn arrow that points at something in frame with a short label ('Look at the water').
components.summary:
A clean drawn pointer that sends the viewer's eye to one detail in the shot, with a short label. Use it in GTA 6 breakdown and compilation shorts at the reveal moment ("Look at her hair", "Look at the rust"), or to name a character the first time they appear. Use one pointer per reveal: the top-performing GTA shorts use a single arrow, only at the reveal.

- **Variant 0, Curved arrow:** the arrow leads. A white arc draws from just above the caption to the spot in 0.30 s (power3.out). The line tapers from 8 px at the tail to 12 px at the tip, like a brush stroke. As it arrives, a 64 px open chevron grows to 1.15 and settles to 1 over 2 frames, so the arrow is complete about 0.32 s into the beat. The caption words rise in from 0.15 s (expo.out). It is Inter 800 at 92 px with one key word in the Leonida sunset gradient. On exit the caption lifts out first, then the arc retracts into the target, so the label is never on screen without its arrow.
- **Variant 1, Pointer + dot:** a sunset dot with a white ring pops onto the spot. A 5 px vertical stem draws out into a smoked-glass card, which wipes open from the edge the stem enters. The card rides the dot sideways, so the stem always lands on the type's column: the left edge of left-aligned text, or the right edge of right-aligned text. The card holds a tracked caps tag (30 px) and a name (84 px, or set per beat). Use it as a detail callout ("DETAIL / Rusted arch") or a name tag ("PROTAGONIST / Lucia Caminos"). On exit the card fades as one layer (its type slightly ahead of the glass), then the stem retracts into the dot, then the dot shrinks away.

Both variants support several **beats**. The demo has two:
1. Lucia's hair, for 0.35–2.55 s.
2. After the hard cut at 2.57 s, the rusty teal car, for 2.7–4.95 s.

Delete a beat to get a single callout. Each beat clears before the next starts, so nothing straddles a cut. Each beat's target is a **track** of keyframes, so the arrow tip or dot follows the subject while the camera moves. Every tip and dot is clamped into the safe zone. With `bg: "none"` (the transparent overlay) there's no sample plate to follow, so each beat holds still on its `still` spot.
components.configDocs:
| Field | Meaning | |---|---| | `duration` | Composition length in seconds (5.0). Also update `data-duration` on `#root`, the video and `#ov`. | | `safe` | The safe-zone box. Tips, dots and cards are clamped into it (x 72–936, y 236–1480). | | `beats[].in` / `.out` | When the beat starts and when it has fully cleared, in seconds. | | `beats[].exit` | How long the clear-out takes, ending at `out` (default 0.37 s). v0: caption first, then the arc. v1: card, then stem, then dot. | | `tracks` | Named tracks of the sample plate (`hair`, `arch`), shared by both variants. | | `beats[].track` | The spot being pointed at, as a name from `tracks` or as its own `[[time, x, y], ...]` in 1080×1920 frame pixels, smoothed with a spline. One keyframe gives a fixed spot. Used with `bg: "plate"`. | | `beats[].still` | `[x, y]`: the fixed spot used for the transparent overlay (`bg: "none"`). Set it to where your detail sits. | | `variants["0"].strokeTail` / `.strokeHead` | Arrow line weight at the tail and at the tip (8 → 12 px taper). The arrowhead uses `strokeHead`. | | `variants["0"].head` / `.headAngle` | Arrowhead arm length (64 px) and chevron half-angle (degrees). | | `beats[].lines` / `.highlight` (v0) | Caption lines, and the one word painted with the sunset gradient. | | `beats[].label` (v0) | `{align, x, y, follow}`: the caption anchor. With `align: "right"`, `x` is the right edge. `follow` (0–1, default 0) makes the caption and the arrow's tail drift with that fraction of the target's x motion, so a panning shot doesn't slide scenery under the type. The rust beat uses 0.35. | | `beats[].tail` / `.bend` (v0) | Where the arrow starts (just above the caption), and how much it bows (a fraction of its length; a negative value bows it the other way). | | `variants["1"].angle` / `.leader` | The leader's diagonal in degrees from vertical (35, side cards only), and the leader line weight (5 px). | | `beats[].tag` / `.name` / `.nameSize` (v1) | The small tracked caps line ("Detail", "Protagonist"), the name lines (one array entry per line), and an optional name size in px (default 84; the rust beat uses 92). | | `beats[].card` (v1) | `edge` is the card edge the leader enters.
• `"top"` puts the card below the dot and `"bottom"` puts it above. Use `{y, edge, column}`. The leader is a vertical stem, and the card rides the dot sideways so the stem lands on `column`. `"left"` (the default) means left-aligned text with the stem on its left edge. `"right"` means right-aligned text with the stem on its right edge. `"center"` means centred text. `y` is the card's top. If the safe zone stops the card, the stem leans onto the column as the card opens.
• `"left"` puts a fixed card to the right of the dot, and `"right"` puts it to the left. Use `{x, y, edge, anchor}`. A 35° diagonal then runs into `anchor`: `"tag"` (the tag's centre line, the default), `"center"`, or a px offset from the card top. |

components.name: Freeze-frame detail
components.job: The clip freezes, the surround dims and desaturates, a spotlight isolates the detail and a label explains it, then playback resumes.
components.summary:
The "wait, look at that" beat in a GTA 6 detail breakdown. The trailer stops dead on one frame while the camera keeps pushing in. The world drains to a cold, dim mono, and only the detail keeps its colour. A big word names it, and a line explains it. Then the colour floods back and playback resumes from the exact frozen frame.

Use it in "details you missed in the trailer" shorts, Easter-egg and map-location breakdowns, or any time the viewer needs three seconds to notice something small in a busy shot.

- **Variant 0, "Spotlight":** the freeze hits with a shake, an exposure pulse and a camera punch-in. The grey surround closes in from the frame edges to a soft, feathered pool of warm light on the detail, like a practical light, with no ring or pointer. The hero word (Archivo wide 900, 200 px, white, with a warm bloom) and the line sit in the dark lower third.
  - Sample: Trailer 2 0:47, the Haitian coat of arms on the mural behind the police stop.
  - Best for a detail that is a region of the frame: a mural, a logo, a face, a poster.
- **Variant 1, "Scan reveal":** after the freeze, a light blade sweeps the frame top to bottom and drains it to mono as it passes. The detail is cut out along its real outline. As the blade clears it, the detail lifts toward camera with a contact shadow and an exposure pulse. The hero word (sunset gradient with a sheen) and the line sit in the open space next to it. On the exit, a reverse sweep wipes the colour back from the bottom up.
  - Sample: Trailer 2 0:37, the "VCI Airport / Ambrosia" exit sign on I-35 with a jet overhead.
  - Best for a detail with a hard outline: a road sign, a storefront sign, a licence plate, a billboard.

Format: 1080×1920, 30 fps, 5.0 s (freeze at 1.0 s; resume at 4.35 s for v0 and 4.3 s for v1). This is a full-frame component, so it always shows footage. `bg: "none"` only turns the finishing (grain and vignette) off.

The default is cold mono at brightness .44. On bright daylight footage, lower the brightness. On very dark footage, raise it so the shapes still read. components.name: Slow-mo replay
components.job: Replay moment: 'REPLAY 0.25×' badge, a scrub bar with playhead, footage slows down.
components.summary:
The "wait, watch that again" moment for GTA 6 compilation shorts. The clip plays at real speed, goes back to the moment and replays it in slow motion at 0.25×. A replay UI shows what is happening: a playhead that drags back and then crawls, a timecode that slows down, and a REPLAY 0.25× label. Every cut is a hard cut with a 3-frame sideways camera hit (no white flash), and no footage frame ever repeats.

Use it on the best beat of a clip: a crash, a flip, a tackle, a near miss, a stunt landing. It works as a mid-clip beat in a "Top 10" compilation or as the payoff of a single-moment short. 1080×1920, 30 fps, 6.0 s. The UI clears by 5.93 s, so it loops cleanly.
components.configDocs:
- `duration`: the composition length (6.0 s). If you change it, also change `data-duration` on `#root` and `#ov`.
- `exit`: `{ at, dur }`, when the UI starts to clear and how long it takes (5.60 s + 0.33 s).
- `hit.px`: the camera hit on the replay cut, as the x offset in px for each frame (default `[6, -4, 2]`, i.e. 3 frames). The footage is scaled just enough to hide the shifted edge. Use `[]` for a plain cut.
- `variants["0" | "1"]`:
  - `clip.src`: your clip, played at real speed from `clip.mediaIn` seconds.
  - `clip.scrubSrc`: the baked reverse segment (the drag-back for 0, the rewind for 1).
  - `clip.slowSrc`: the baked slow-motion segment.
  - `timing.real`: seconds of real speed.
  - `timing.back`: seconds of drag-back or rewind.
  - `timing.backEase`: `"linear"` for a `bake.sh reverse` file, `"inOut"` for a `bake.sh rewind` file.
  - `timing.curve` (rewind only): the length the rewind file was baked over (its `<outLen>`). Defaults to `back`.
  - `timing.trimIn` (rewind only): seconds skipped at the head of the rewind file. A rewind file's first frame repeats (the curve starts at zero speed), so use 0.034 (one frame), with `back = curve − 2 frames` (e.g. 1.0333 → 0.966).
  - `replayIn`: the source second the replay restarts from.
  - `rate`: the slow-mo speed the bake used (0.25 = quarter speed). The playhead, timecode and speed labels follow it.
  - `range`: `[start, end]` in source seconds, the window the scrub rail or tape shows.
  - Variant 0: `word` (the badge word) and `countIn` (how long the badge counts 1.00 → `rate` once the slow-mo starts, 0.4 s).
  - Variant 1: `labels` (`rewind` / `replay`, the hero words) and `grade` (`brightness` / `contrast` on the footage; set both to 1 for no lift).

The script writes `src`, `data-start`, `data-duration` and `data-media-start` onto the active variant's three `<video>` tags (`v0a/v0b/v0c` or `v1a/v1b/v1c`). Mirror the values in those attributes too, so `hyperframes check` and Studio see the same thing.

components.name: Name tag
components.job: Identifies a character on screen: 'JASON DUVAL · Protagonist' attached by a leader line, or as a lower third.
components.summary:
Shows who's on screen, set like a film credit and lit by the shot it labels. Use it the first time a character appears in a GTA 6 short: a trailer breakdown ("this is Lucia Caminos"), a character-reveal compilation, a "who is…" explainer, or a reaction where viewers need the name before the line lands.

- **Variant 0, Leader tag.** A lock-on pin is tracked to the character's collar. An elbow callout runs from the pin down a steep diagonal, then a horizontal leg runs left and ends at the name's left edge. The name hangs under the leg in 124 px wide caps: a white first name, a Leonida-sunset surname (about 770 px, 89% of the safe width), and PROTAGONIST at 28 px. The demo is LUCIA CAMINOS on Lucia at the gate (s018, golden hour), pre-slowed with a slow push.
  - **Payoff (0.98 s, when the last surname glyph seats):** a one-frame warm exposure flash from the sun (upper left, 0.9 peak), one warm gold-to-pink light leak from the sun side (under the tag), a 1.05 kick, a 0.4 s light pulse and ring snap on the pin, a sheen across the sunset, and a warm bloom on CAMINOS.
  - **Exit (3.95 s):** the role blurs out, the name rises out through its masks (each glyph fades as it goes), the callout retracts into the pin, and the pin collapses right behind it. Clean by 4.65 s.
- **Variant 1, Lower third.** The name is born in the blast. One speed-ramped shot: Jason on the rooftop at 0.4x, dropping into a 0.17x ultra-slow as the helicopter explodes behind him, held for the full 5 s. The lockup is a broadcast lower third with its own structure: a small first name (JASON, 64 px wide 600, tracked .22em) over a huge surname (DUVAL, wide 800, fit to 88% of the safe width, about 745 px), then a 2 px sunset hairline drawn under the surname that leads into PROTAGONIST. The role ends flush with the surname's right ink edge, so the block reads as one justified unit. The hairline is the frame's one accent.
  - **Payoff (0.60 s, on the fireball):** a warm additive exposure hit centred on the fireball, a shake and punch on the footage, a 6 px RGB split on the lockup, and the surname rising in it. The fire's measured light then glows on the name for the whole hold.
  - **Exit (4.1 s):** the role blurs out, the hairline retracts, and both name lines leave as whole masked lines (0.06 s apart) with a 6 px blur and a late fade. Clean by 4.7 s.

There are no cards and no boxes. Legibility comes from placement (v0: a dark shirt under the collar; v1: low-left over a bottom scrim) and light. Each variant runs 5 s and has fully left by about 4.7 s, so it loops. Plate renders run the Look finishing layer (grain .16; vignette .5 on v0, .38 on v1).
components.configDocs:
| Field | Variant | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `first`, `last` | both | The name. v0: both lines in Archivo wide 800 at `block.size` (124 px), with `last` in the sunset gradient. v1: `first` is the small tracked line (`first1.size`, 64 px, wide 600) and `last` is the hero (`size` 190, shrunk until it spans at most `maxWidth`). Both shrink only if a line would pass the max width. |
| `role` | both | The tracked label (Archivo wide 600, pure white), such as "Protagonist": 28 px under the name in v0, 26 px at the end of the hairline in v1 (flush with the surname's right ink edge). Use real facts only (see `research/gta6/FACTS.md`). |
| `shots` | both | Mirrors the `<video>` tags: `id`, `src`, `start`, `dur`, `mediaStart`. v1 shots also take `push: [from, to]` and `origin` (a per-shot push; add more shots for a montage), plus an optional CSS `grade`. Edit `shots` and the tags together. |
| `push {from,to,origin}` | 0 | The slow push on the held shot. `origin` is in frame px, and the pin is mapped through it. |
| `track [[t,x,y]…]` | 0 | The subject's path on the unpushed clip, in frame px. Keys are eased with Catmull-Rom. One key gives a static pin. |
| `pinDy` | 0 | How far below the tracked point the pin sits (12 puts it on the collar band in the demo). |
| `block {left, roleBaseline, gap, size, maxWidth}` | 0 | `left` is the name's left edge. The callout's leg ends on the first glyph's ink edge, measured per name, so it sits flush over the stem. The lockup is anchored by the role's baseline (1458) and builds upward. The leg sits `gap` px above the name. |
| `leader {angle, ringGap, minLeg, draw, blur}` | 0 | The callout: diagonal angle from horizontal (58°), gap from the pin's centre (27), the shortest leg allowed (90 px), draw time (0.28 s, expo.out) and the directional motion blur on the drawing head (6 px). |
| `reveal {stagger, dur, seat}` | both | The masked char rise. In v0, the payoff time is computed from it: `last + (chars−1)·stagger + seat·dur`. |
| `sunset` | 0 | The surname gradient. |
| `payoff.light {at, color, peak, decay, radius}` | both | The exposure hit: its centre as frame fractions (put it on your shot's light: the sun, a fire, a lamp), its colour, its peak for exactly one frame (v0 0.9, v1 0.6), decay (power3.out) and radius in px. Plate only. |
| `payoff.leak {lead, dur, colors, opacity, y, from, to, size}` | 0 | The one light leak: starts `lead` s before the hit, sweeps from `from` to `to` (frame-width fractions) at height `y`. Keep it on your shot's sun side. Plate only. |
| `payoff` (other fields) | both | v0: `zoom` (1.05), `amp`, `snap` (ring scale on the hit), `pinPulse` (s), `sheen` (s), `bloom`. v1: `amp`, `zoom`, `chroma` (px). Shake and punch only play with footage. |
| `left`, `baseline`, `size`, `maxWidth` | 1 | The lockup's ink left edge (80; first name, surname and hairline share it), the surname's baseline (1392), its starting size (190) and fit width (760, 88% of the safe width). |
| `first1 {size, gap, spread}` | 1 | The first name: size (64), the gap from its baseline to the surname's cap top (24), and the per-glyph spread of its tracking-in (10 px). |
| `rule {below, gap, draw, min}` | 1 | The sunset hairline: px under the surname's baseline (32), the gap before the role (24), draw time (0.45 s, expo.out) and minimum length. Its length is computed: it runs from the left edge to the role. |
| `exit {dur, lineStagger, blur}` | 1 | The whole-line masked exit: duration (0.42 s), the delay between the two lines (0.06 s) and the blur (6 px). |
| `scrim {top, opacity, spot}` | 1 | Where the bottom scrim starts (760), its strength (.9), and the strength of the soft spot behind the lockup (.85). |
| `fire {end, glow, luma[]}` | 1 | The scene light on the name: `luma` is one 0–1 value per frame from t = 0 (the demo's is the measured fire brightness of the ramped s098 clip). It drives a warm glow (`glow` = its strength) until `end`. Set `luma` to `[]` or `end` to 0 for a clip without a dominant light. |
| `timing` | both | v0: `pin`, `leader`, `first`, `last`, `roleAfterHit`, `pulse`, `out` (the callout retracts at out+0.25 and the pin collapses by out+0.7). v1: `scrim`, `hit` (put it on your hardest beat; the surname rises there), then relative to `hit`: `first` (the first name's tracking-in, −0.12), `rule` (+0.3) and `role` (+0.62); and `out`. |

components.name: Spec card
components.job: A spec block for a vehicle or era in an evolution/detail compilation: name plus 3 stats with bars.
components.summary:
A spec block for one item in a GTA 6 evolution or detail compilation: a name plus 3 stats with animated bars. Use it once per item, for example "every police car in GTA history", "GTA eras ranked" or "GTA 6 vehicles we've seen".

Drop it on the clip where that item is on screen, and cut it with that clip. A vehicle card should only ever sit over the vehicle it names.

1080×1920, 30 fps, 5 s. Everything sits inside the 9:16 safe zone (x 72–936, y 230–1480).

What it does over its 5 s:
- **Vehicle:** the card fades in over 0.10 s and lands at the height of its name block. It opens to full height as its three stat rows arrive. Each row (label, value and bar) arrives as one unit, then the bar fills and the number counts. It is done by about 0.86 s.
- **Era:** from 0.18 s the full card fades in over 0.10 s on the previous era: "2013 / GTA V", "Era 07 / 08 · Los Santos" and that year's numbers. It holds for 0.45 s. Then the year, the game name, the meta row, the numbers and the bars all roll together to "2026 / GTA 6", "Era 08 / 08 · Leonida · Vice City", 13 / 24 / 29. It is readable by about 0.83 s.
- **Hold:** one beat at 3.0 s. A soft sheen crosses the bars, and on the era card the year swells 1 → 1.04 → 1.
- **Exit:** a 0.36 s fade from 4.58 s, so the next item can cut in cleanly.
components.configDocs:
Per variant (`CONFIG.variants["0"]` / `["1"]`):
- `style`: `"vehicle"` (glass HUD card) or `"era"` (paper card with year).
- `place`: `"top"` or `"bottom"`.
- `plate`: the sample clip path shown when `bg` is `"plate"`. It must match the `src` of one of the `<video>` elements.
- `meta` / `metaRight`: the small, wide-tracked caps line at the top of the card, for example `"GTA 6 · 2026"` and `"Our rating"`, or `"Era 08 / 08"` and `"Leonida · Vice City"`. If the two are too long together, the row shrinks to fit, down to 24 px.
- `metaFrom` / `metaRightFrom` (era only): the previous era's meta row, for example `"Era 07 / 08"` and `"Los Santos"`. It is on the card from the start and rolls to `meta` / `metaRight` with the year. In lines of the same length, only the characters that differ roll. Leave both out, and the meta row instead fades in once the roll has landed.
- `name`: the item name. Long names shrink to fit automatically.
- `sub` (vehicle only): the second line under the name.
- `yearFrom`, `year` (era only): the digits that differ roll from `yearFrom` to `year`, while shared digits stay still. Only those two years are ever readable. Set `yearFrom` to `null` (or to `year`) for no roll.
- `nameFrom` (era only): the previous era's game, shown beside `yearFrom` and rolled to `name` together with the year, for example `"GTA V"`.
- `max`: the value that fills a bar completely. Use 10 for ratings and 29 for the series timeline.
- `decimals`, `suffix`: number format, for example `1` and `""` gives `8.6`, and `0` and `" yrs"` gives `13 YRS`. Values are set in caps.
- `unit` (vehicle): a small scale after each number, at the label size and 50% white, for example `"/10"` gives "8.6/10". Use `""` for none.
- `segments` (vehicle): `0` draws one continuous bar filled exactly to value/max (the default). `10` brings back HUD blocks, where the boundary block fills partially.
- `sheen`: `"all"` (the hold-beat sheen crosses every bar) or `"lead"` (only the highest).
- `pulse` (era): how far the year swells on the hold beat (`1.04`); remove it for none.
- `stats` (**creator fill**): exactly three `{ label, value, from }` rows. On the era card, `from` is the number shown while `yearFrom` is up (see the rule above). The vehicle card ignores `from` and counts from 0.
- `timing` (optional, per variant): overrides `CONFIG.timing` for that variant only. The era card uses `{ cardIn: 0.18 }`, so the full card is up by about 0.27 s.

`CONFIG.timing` (all in seconds):
- `cardIn`, `cardFade`: when the card appears, and its opacity ramp (0.10, power1.out);
- `textIn`: the vehicle type's delay after the card (0 means with it);
- `barsAt`, `barDur`, `barStagger` (vehicle: 0.24, 0.50 and 0.06): when the rows arrive and how long the bars take to fill;
- `growDur` (vehicle): how long the card takes to open from its name block to full height (0.4). It starts at `barsAt − 0.06`;
- `yearRollAt` (after `cardIn`) and `yearDur` (era): how long the previous era holds (0.45), and how long the year, name, meta row, numbers and bars take to roll (0.45, expo.out);
- `beats`, `beatDur`: start times and length of the hold accent (`[3.0]`, 0.5); use `[]` for none;
- `out`, `outDur`: exit start and length (4.58, 0.36);
- `end`: composition end (5.0).

components.name: Before/after slider
components.job: A slider wipes between GTA V and GTA VI footage of a similar shot, with era labels on each side.
components.summary:
A full-frame before/after slider for GTA 6 shorts. Two clips are stacked full frame, and a white seam with a smoked-glass handle wipes between them. Each side carries an era label: GTA 5 (2013) is the "before" and GTA 6 (2026) is the "after". Each side holds one shot for the whole loop, and the two shots are matched like for like (the same kind of subject, at the same scale and height), so the eye compares the same thing across the seam.

The motion is one real drag:
1. The seam wipes GTA 6 in to a 50/50 split and holds.
2. The handle is grabbed and dragged so GTA 5 nearly fills the frame, then across in one long drag so GTA 6 nearly fills it, then back to 50/50. Each era gets the frame to itself for 0.5 s.
3. The labels ride the seam, 40 px clear of it. When a label's side gets too narrow to hold it inside the safe zone, the label fades out over 0.15 s, and it fades back in as the room returns. The seam never cuts a label.
4. The seam retracts the way it came, so the clip loops cleanly on full-frame GTA 5.

Use it for "GTA 5 vs GTA 6" graphics comparisons, "same spot, 13 years later" beats inside a compilation, or any A/B shot (old trailer vs new trailer, leak vs final).

| Variant | Name | Look |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | Vertical slider | The handle travels up and down. GTA 5 is on top and GTA 6 below, with a horizontal seam. Two ink-navy era cards of matching width ride the seam on the left (GTA 5 above it, GTA 6 below it). Each card shows the name, year and place, left-aligned on a shared name column, and the sunset gradient on "GTA 6" is the only accent. The seam travels from y 1400 (GTA 5 fills 73%) to y 420 (GTA 6 fills 78%). Sample: the red GTA V convertible at the kerb vs a parked red sports car in GTA 6, at the same scale. |
| `1` | Horizontal slider | The handle travels left and right. GTA 5 is on the left and GTA 6 on the right, with a vertical seam. Two see-through tinted-glass chips (name over year) ride the seam near the top. The sky shows through them, blurred, so they read as glass rather than v0's solid card. The seam travels from x 870 (GTA 5 fills 81%, and the handle stays inside the x 936 safe edge) to x 180 (GTA 6 fills 83%). Sample: the green "5 · Los Puerta Fwy" overhead sign vs the GTA 6 "35 North · VCI Airport" signs with a jet passing over, at the same height. |

Duration: 5.0 s, 1080×1920, 30 fps. Timeline:
- 0.08–0.64 s: wipe-in to 50/50;
- 1.10–1.65 s: drag so GTA 5 fills the frame, then hold;
- 2.15–2.95 s: one long drag so GTA 6 fills the frame, then hold;
- 3.45–4.00 s: back to 50/50;
- 4.36 s: labels leave; 4.46–4.88 s: the seam retracts.

Hero frame: 4.2 s.

components.name: Evolution timeline
components.job: GTA evolution by year: GTA III 2001 → Vice City 2002 → San Andreas 2004 → GTA IV 2008 → GTA V 2013 → GTA VI 2026, advancing card by card.
components.summary:
A "GTA through the years" overlay for evolution and compilation shorts. It steps through the series one game at a time: GTA III 2001 → Vice City 2002 → San Andreas 2004 → GTA IV 2008 → GTA V 2013 → GTA VI 2026. Each entry shows its year, its name and an item counter, so the viewer always knows where the video is and how far it has to go.

Use it at the top of a "GTA evolution" compilation. Each step lands about every 0.9 s, so cut each game's clip to land on its step. It also works as a recap card before a GTA 6 reveal moment: the last step is the climax. The 13-year gap gets a duration of its own and a hard landing at about 5.6 s (rail) or 5.9 s (ticker). Cut your GTA 6 shot on that frame.
components.configDocs:
| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| `label` | Header text ("GTA Evolution"); shown as wide-tracked caps. |
| `items[]` | `{ year, name, highlight? }`, in order. 2–8 entries work. The rail keeps its stack above y 1102: up to 6 entries use 112 px cards, and more entries compress the cards and their type. The ticker's ruler and odometer adapt to the min/max year. `highlight: true` gives the payoff treatment. On the rail: the year count-up from the previous entry, the 4% row step, the impact, the inverted chip and the sunset hairline. On the ticker: the punch, the shake, the halo and the bubble pop, plus the sunset sweep onto the year when the highlighted entry is the last one. |
| `gap` | Chip/bubble text: `one` for a 1-year gap, `many` with `{n}`. |
| `variants["0"/"1"]` | `style` ("rail"/"ticker"), the sample `plate`, and the ticker `top` (the y of the card, default 250). |
| `timing` | `intro`, `steps[]` (the second each entry lands; one per item, or `[]` to spread them evenly from `first` to `last`), `out` (fade start), `end`. Ticker steps roll in 0.45 s; a `highlight` step rolls in 0.9 s. On the rail, a `highlight` step's count-up lasts 0.6 s (`RC` in the script). |

notes.label: the series, in order; years and names from research/gta6/FACTS.md
notes.gap: gap chip / bubble text ("+N YRS" since the previous entry)
notes.timing: steps: the second each entry lands (one per item). Leave [] to spread them from first to last.

components.name: Tier list
components.job: S/A/B/C tier list: items drop into tiers one by one (e.g. GTA games ranked). Ends with 'Comment yours'.
components.summary:
An S/A/B/C tier list for GTA 6 shorts. Items land in their tiers one at a time, then the board grows a "Comment yours" footer row to pull comments. The look borrows the GTA in-game menu: a dark board, hairline rows, and one solid white "selected" bar on the item that just landed. Empty slots show a quiet "?", and the final pick gets a punch and a lock-in ring. Use it in ranking shorts ("every GTA ranked", "GTA 6 cast ranked", "best trailer moments"), as the payoff of a compilation, or as the closing beat that turns a list into a comment fight.

1080×1920, 30 fps, 7.6 s. Overlay: it works over the sample plate or as a transparent overlay (`bg: "none"`).
components.configDocs:
- `tiers`: the row letters, top first, default `["S","A","B","C"]`. The first row's letter carries the sunset gradient. 4 rows fit comfortably. With more rows, or tiers that wrap, the rows shrink (to at most 70 %) so the board stays above y 1480.
- `dim`: how much the list darkens the clip behind it, from 0 to 1. This also applies to the transparent overlay.
- `cta`: the closing prompt. It appears as the board's footer row (Barlow caps), so keep it short.
- `variants["0"|"1"]`:
  - `plate`: the sample footage (preview only).
  - `kicker`: the small wide-tracked label.
  - `title`: the headline. It shrinks to fit automatically.
  - `items`: in reveal order, `{ name, sub, tier }`. `sub` is the small tracked second line (a year or a surname), and `tier` is one of the `tiers` letters. Any number per tier: the column count follows the fullest tier (2–4 columns), and a tier with more than 4 items wraps onto another line. Empty slots show a "?" ghost. The **last item gets the payoff** (punch, ring, row stays lit), so end on an S-tier pick. Names shrink to fit (down to 30 px, then wrap to 2 lines). Sublines tighten their tracking, then ellipsize.
  - `timing`:
    - `in`: entrance start.
    - `first`: when the first item lands.
    - `step`: seconds between items.
    - `cta`: when the prompt appears.
    - `out`: exit start.
    - `end`: end time.

  If you add items, move `cta` to 0.45 s after the last item lands: Tier rows `first + (count − 1) × step + 0.63`, Tier reveal `first + (count − 1) × step + 1.25`. With many items, lower `step` (Tier rows works down to about 0.36, Tier reveal to about 0.6) so everything lands before about 5.5 s.

components.name: Versus card
components.job: A head-to-head title: 'JASON vs LUCIA' or 'GTA V vs GTA VI'.
components.summary:
A head-to-head title for a GTA 6 short (craft v2). Use it to open a comparison segment: "LUCIA vs JASON" (who's the better protagonist), "GTA V vs GTA VI" (graphics or map comparison), car vs car, city vs city. It runs 6 s, and its first 2–3 s also work as a cold open.

1080×1920, 30 fps, 6 s. Full-frame: footage shows on every frame, and the Look finishing stack (film grain, vignette, flashes, one light leak) is always on.
components.configDocs:
- **`duration`**: the length in seconds (6). The root `data-duration` and the overlay's `data-duration` must match it.
- **`variants["0"]` (Split)**
  - `vs`: the emblem text.
  - `a` / `b`: the contenders. `a` is the top pane and the first intro; `b` is the bottom pane and the second intro.
    - `name`, `label`: the big name and the small surname kicker above it.
    - `intro.clip`, `intro.start`: the full-frame close-up for that contender's intro beat (a `-v` 1080×1920 shot works best) and its in-point. Intro A needs 1.1 s, intro B 1.5 s.
    - `pane.clip`, `pane.start`: the clip for that contender's half of the split and its in-point. The pane starts sliding in at 2.3 s, so it needs **3.7 s** from `start`.
    - `pane.box`: `{ x, y, w, h }` in canvas px, the box the clip is laid into (object-fit: cover). It must cover its half of the frame: pane A from y 0 down to the seam, pane B from the seam's high end (`seam.yRight`) to y 1920 and the full width.
    - `pane.origin`, `pane.push`: the transform origin and end scale of the slow push during the hold.
    - `b.pane.filter`: an optional CSS filter on pane B's clip.
    - `b.pane.track`, `eyeY`, `yMax`: vertical face tracking for a shot whose subject lifts or drops his head. `track` lists `[seconds into the clip, eye y in clip px]`; the box moves so the eye sits at canvas `eyeY`, clamped between `box.y` (the box's foot on the canvas floor) and `yMax` (its top on the seam's high end). Remove `track` for a locked-off shot.
  - `seam`: `{ yLeft, yRight }`, where the diagonal seam meets the left and right edges.
  - `introSize` / `introMaxW` / `introBaseline`: the intro name size, the width it is fitted to, and its baseline y.
  - `nameSize` / `nameMaxW`: the face-off names' size and fit width (both names share the smaller fitted size).
  - `vsSize`, `vsX`: the VS size and the x where its ink is centred on the seam.
  - `nameBBaseline`: name B's baseline (at the foot of B's portrait, inside the safe zone).
  - `gapVS`: name A's baseline above the VS ink. `seamClear`: name A's last letter stays this far above the seam. `gapLabel`: a kicker label's baseline above its name's cap top.
  - `bladeGap`: how far the blade stays clear of the VS.
  - `blade`: `{ width, fill, bloom, strength }`, the light edge along the seam. `vsBloom`: the VS's bloom colour and strength. `leak`: the light leak on the hit (`colors`, `opacity`, `dur`, `size`).
- **`variants["1"]` (Centre)**
  - `vs`, `a.name`, `a.label`, `b.name`, `b.label`: the lockup text.
  - `cuts`: the matched pairs, each `{ at, dur, a: { clip, start, fit }, b: { clip, start, fit } }`. Clips are 16:9 (`-h`) shots, cover-scaled into their 1080×960 pane (1707×960, so about 63% of the width shows). `fit` frames each shot: `x` / `y` are the object-position (0–1; `x: 0.72` shows the right side), and `s` is an extra zoom about that point (`1.125` is the `-h` file's native pixels, so it costs no sharpness). Each clip needs `dur` seconds from `start`.
  - `seamY`: where the seam runs (960 = a 50/50 split).
  - `nameSize` / `nameMaxW` / `vsSize`: the type sizes and the fit width.
  - `gapVS`: the gap between each name's ink and the VS ink. `gapLabel`: the gap between a label and its name (labels sit outside the lockup).
  - `bladeGap`: the blade's clearance around the VS. `blade`: `{ width, color, bloom, strength }`. `vsBloom`: the VS's bloom colour and strength.
  - `scrimH`, `scrim`: the soft dark lip on each side of the seam, under the lockup (its height, and its darkness at the seam and at 28 / 56 / 80% of `scrimH`).
  - `sunset`: the gradient on name B.
- **`vsFill`**: the Split VS gradient (Leonida sunset).
- **`inkEdge`**: `{ left: 96, right: 900 }`. Every flush-left and flush-right line is aligned on its glyph ink (measured), inset from the 72–936 safe limits.
- **`timing.split`**: `cutB` (intro B starts), `slide` (the portraits start sliding in), `cutSplit` (the payoff hit; the VS starts falling `vsFall` s earlier and the blade draws in the last 0.16 s), `nameA` / `nameB` / `labels` (the type lands), `sheen` (the light pass over the VS), `out` (the exit starts).
- **`timing.centre`**: `open` / `openDur` (the wipe out from the seam), `nameA` / `nameB` / `labels`, `slam` (the payoff, on the first matched cut), `vsFall`, `sheen` (the light pass over name B), `out` (the type exits), `close` / `closeDur` (the panes shut onto the seam).

components.name: Trailer views race
components.job: Bars race to real numbers: Trailer 1 305.4M, Trailer 2 189.6M, Launch Trailer 82.0M YouTube views.
components.summary: Category: Comparisons · Kind: overlay (works over the sample plate or as a transparent overlay)
components.configDocs:
| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `eyebrow` | `[bright, dim]` header parts, joined by " · " ("GTA 6 trailers", "YouTube views"). Shown in caps in both variants. |
| `source` | v0 footer, left side ("as of Nov 18, 2026") |
| `unit`, `decimals` | Number suffix ("M") and decimal places (1). The odometer builds one wheel per digit from these. |
| `items[]` | `{ label, date, value }` for each entry. v0 sorts them by value; the top one gets the gradient bar, the 128 px numeral and the margin pill. |
| `variants["0"].plate` | Sample plate under variant 0 |
| `variants["0"].gapWord` | Words in the margin pill ("ahead of" gives "+115.8M AHEAD OF TRAILER 2"; shown in caps) |
| `variants["1"].plate` | Sample plate under variant 1 |
| `variants["1"].a / .b` | Indexes into `items` for the head-to-head (default 0 vs 1). `a` must be the larger value: it takes the sunset. |
| `variants["1"].leadSuffix` | Text after the computed margin ("views ahead") |
| `timing.in` | Entrance time |
| `timing.count` | When every counter starts |
| `timing.land` | When every counter lands (all together). This is the payoff: pop, sheen or gradient sweep, then the pill or chip. |
| `timing.ease` | The one shared count ease (`power3.out`). Every value is `total × ease((t − count) / (land − count))`, so the ranking is true on every frame. |
| `timing.sheen` | v1 only: `[start, duration]` of the slow sunset sheen across the winning numeral during the hold (`[3.0, 1.2]`) |
| `timing.out` | Exit start (0.35 s fade) |
| `timing.end` | Composition end. If you change it, also change `data-duration` on `#root`, the videos and `#ov`. |
| `maxBlur` | Maximum vertical motion blur in px on a fast-rolling digit (6). It is scaled down for small numerals. |

Bar widths are true to the data (value / max × track width). Both margins are computed: v0 from the top two items, v1 as |a − b|. If you change the numbers, the odometer slots and the leading-digit openings recompute. Because every counter shares one clock, the ranking stays true on every frame for any data.

notes.eyebrow: Shared content (real numbers: Rockstar Games YouTube channel, checked 2026-11-18 — see research/gta6/FACTS.md) v0 header: [bright part, dim part] joined by " · " (v1 shows both)
notes.timing: in: entrance · count/land: ONE shared clock for every counter, value_i(t) = total_i * ease((t - count) / (land - count)), so the ranking and the bar ratios are true on every frame; land = the payoff · out: exit starts (0.35 s fade) · end: composition end sheen: v1's slow sunset sheen across the winning numeral during the hold [start, duration]

components.name: Stat count-up
components.job: A huge number rolls up to a real stat (305,372,086 views on Trailer 1) with its label; or a record badge (90M+ views in 24 hours).
components.summary: A huge real number rolls into place on a slot-style odometer, so a short can land a fact like "305,372,086 views on Trailer 1" or "90M+ views in 24 hours". Each digit is clipped to the number's cap line. Fast columns whir with vertical motion blur, and slow ones tick crisply into place, then the number lands with a punch. 1080×1920, 30 fps, 7 s. It is an overlay: use it over the sample footage, or export it with a transparent background and drop it on your own clip.
components.configDocs:
`CONFIG.variants["0" | "1"]`:

| Field | Variant | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `plate` | both | Sample clip under the overlay when `bg = "plate"` |
| `value` | both | The number as text. Digits roll; commas and dots stay fixed (`"305,372,086"`, `"90"`, `"1.5"`) |
| `from` | both | What the counter shows before it rolls, in the same shape as `value` (`"000,000,000"`, `"60"`) |
| `suffix` | both | Static text after the number (`"M+"`, `"%"`, `""`) |
| `numSize` / `maxWidth` | both | Numeral size in px; it shrinks to fit `maxWidth` automatically |
| `kicker` | 0 | Wide-tracked label above the number |
| `sub` | both | The label under the number ("views on YouTube", "views in 24 hours") |
| `meta` | 0 | The source and date line under the label |
| `scrim` | 0 | `"always"` (default: the smoke ships in the transparent export too, so it holds on bright clips), `"plate"` (only over the sample footage) or `"off"` |
| `chip` | 1 | Wide-tracked caps at the top of the card (Rockstar date style, magenta offset) |
| `footL` / `footR` | 1 | The footer line of the card (centred, with a hairline divider) |
| `gradient` | 1 | Three colours for the numeral fill (Leonida sunset by default), one sweep across the whole word |
| `stamp` | 1 | `{ scale, frames, shake }`: the land slam (1.12 → 1 over 3 frames) and the footage shake in px (6). With `bg: "none"` the card jolts instead |

`CONFIG.roll["0" | "1"]`:
- `start`: when the columns start rolling.
- `firstLand` / `lastLand`: when the first and the last column land.
- `order`: `"ltr"` (the leftmost lands first, a slot-reel settle) or `"rtl"`.
- `ease`: `"expo"` (fast start, long settle: count-ups), `"out3"` (power3.out) or `"in"` (accelerates into the land: stamps).
- `spinsMin` / `spinsMax`: extra full turns for the early-landing and late-landing halves of the columns. Keep the leading half at 0 so the number only counts up.
- `minCells`: the minimum travel per column (0 lets a column that already shows its digit stay put).
- `tickFrac` (optional): the longest tick as a fraction of a digit's time slot (default 0.38; v1 uses 0.7 so every 60 → 90 tick slides).

`CONFIG.odo`: `pitch` (reel cell spacing × digit height, 1.22), `pad` (window bleed past the cap box, 0.035), `fade` (edge mask while moving, 0.3), `tick` (the longest digit tick, 0.1 s = 3 frames) and `blur` (max motion blur × digit height, 0.05).
`CONFIG.timing`: `in` (entrance start per variant), `out` (exit start, 6.42 s), `end` (7.0 s).

**Tips:**
- Ticks are whole frames on the 30 fps grid, so a still never catches a half-and-half digit. Render at 30 fps.
- For a longer number, widen `lastLand − firstLand` so the columns settle one after another.
- For a stamp, use a short `from` → `value` jump with `ease: "in"`.

notes.roll: odometer: each digit column rolls from its `from` digit to its `value` digit like a ratchet: the digit rests crisp in its cell and ticks to the next one (quint-out, ≤ odo.tick s, vertical motion blur while it moves). ease: "expo" (fast start, long settle) | "out3" (power3.out) | "in" (accelerates into the land, for a stamp). order "ltr": leftmost column lands first at firstLand, rightmost last at lastLand (slot-reel settle); order "rtl": rightmost lands first. Columns in the later-landing half take `spinsMax` extra full turns, the rest `spinsMin`, so the magnitude only ever counts UP and never overshoots the real value.
notes.odo: pitch: cell spacing × digit height; pad: window bleed beyond the cap box (× digit height); fade: edge mask while moving (fraction of the window); tick: longest digit tick (s); blur: max motion blur (× digit height)
notes.timing: in: entrance start per variant (s)

components.name: Top 3 podium
components.job: Three.js podium for a top-3 reveal: third, second, first rise with labels, camera settles on the winner.
components.summary:
A Three.js podium for the top-3 payoff of a GTA 6 ranking short ("Top 3 moments", "most-viewed trailers", "best cars"...).
- It's one stepped podium in glossy ink-navy on a dusky sunset sky (Rockstar's `#9C7AA8 → #FFC88F` feature-card sky, graded over the blurred clip). The step heights are 1.00 / 0.70 / 0.50, and the winner's step is 1.15x wider.
- Third, second and first grow straight up out of the floor in that order. They are always solid, never see-through. Each step carries an extruded 3D rank numeral and has its clip standing on top as a card, seated with a contact shadow.
  - The "2" and "3" are a near-matched white pair (about 185 / 170 px on screen), with lit top edges so they read as extruded.
- The "1" slams in with a sunset sweep, and a thin sunset rim lights up along the winner's top edge. The winner is the only warm accent on the podium.

When to use it:
- At the end of a countdown compilation, as the "here's the final top 3" recap before the outro.
- As a 6-second hook that teases the winner before the full ranking plays.

1080×1920, 30 fps, 6.0 s. It's a full-frame component, so it always shows footage.

It loops cleanly. From 5.6 s the cards fold back and fade, then the steps sink into the floor, and the last frame shows only the backdrop. The house light is the same on the first and last frames, so the loop point never flashes.
components.configDocs:
- `variants["0"|"1"].style`: `"podium"` or `"spotlight"` (the camera and light behaviour).
- `.backdrop`: `{ src, in, rate }` for the clip used as the blurred full-frame backdrop. Use your #1 clip, and pick a stretch of it that keeps one colour.
- `.kicker`: small wide-tracked line above the title (e.g. `"GTA 6 · Trailer 2"`).
- `.title`: the hook title (uppercased, balanced over at most two lines).
- `.entries[0..2]`: **rank 1, 2, 3** in that order, each with:
  - `name`: the card title in caps, fitted to at most two lines and never below 44 px on screen. Side cards are about 250 px wide, so keep names short (two short lines).
  - `meta` (optional): a short line under the name, e.g. your own timestamp or note. Leave it `""` to hide it, so the name sits on the card's bottom edge.
  - `count` + `unit`: instead of `meta`, a number that rolls up as the card lands (e.g. `305.4` + `"M views"`).
  - `clip`: `{ src, in, rate, pos? }`.
    - `in` is the in-point in seconds and `rate` the playback speed. Pick them so the card stays on **one shot that matches its label** for its whole time on screen.
    - For slow motion, don't use a live `rate` below 1: it holds frames and judders. Pre-slow the clip with frame blending, play it at `in: 0, rate: 1`, and give the matching `<video>` the same `src`. The demo clips in `assets/clips/card-*.mp4` were made this way:
      `ffmpeg -ss <in> -t <span> -i clip.mp4 -vf "setpts=PTS/<rate>,minterpolate=fps=30:mi_mode=blend" -an out.mp4`
    - `pos` (optional) is the card's crop as a CSS `object-position`, e.g. `"50% 88%"` to drop the crop below a car's sun visor.
      - A vertical (9:16) clip in these cards can only be re-cropped up or down: a higher y% shows more of the bottom of the source, so content moves up in the card.
      - To re-frame left or right, use a horizontal clip. The demo's Jason card uses `p03-jason-door-h.mp4` at `"30% 50%"` to keep him in frame.
  - `chip` (optional, on #1): a smoked-glass pill centred on the top of the winner's card (e.g. `"90M+ in 24h"`). It shrinks to fit, never below 26 px, so keep it under about 12 characters.
- `type`: on-screen type sizes at the settled framing: `name` 52, `small` 32, plus the card radius. The script converts these through the camera, so they hold on screen.
- `timing`:
  - `rise[3|2|1]`: when each place starts to rise. Keep each card `<video>`'s `data-start` equal to it.
  - `riseDur` / `riseDur1`: how long the steps take to rise.
  - `slam`: the "1" hit. The v0 camera push starts here, and the winner's rim lights up.
  - `push`: how long the v0 push-in takes (1.2 s).
  - `spotlight`: when the v1 beam fires. The v1 camera settles from here.
  - `dimMore`: when v1 dims the runners-up further. Their dimmer goes 0.25 → 0.35, on top of a `saturate(.65) brightness(.8)` grade that eases in with the beam.
  - `out` / `end`: when the fade-out starts and when the component ends.

variants.kindEvidence: Full-frame component: it always shows footage

notes.type: on-screen type sizes (px) at the settled framing: three sizes per frame (title 108, names, small)
notes.timing: seconds. rise[r] = when place r starts rising (the clip <video> data-start matches it). The build is done by 1.6 s. push = the "Podium" camera push-in after the slam; dimMore = when the spotlight variant dims the runners-up further.

components.name: Clip carousel
components.job: Three.js ring of 5 clip cards (top-5 intro) that rotates and lands on the next item, the chosen card plays.
components.summary:
A top-5 intro for GTA 6 compilation shorts. Five clip cards (your own footage, playing live as WebGL textures) turn on a 3D ring or cycle through a deck. The playing card is 864 px wide (x 72–936, the full safe-zone width) on a clean ink field (#0B0B0E) that carries only a faint glow of the same clip behind the cards, so the clip is the one lit object in the frame. The carousel lands on the next item, and that card comes forward and plays with a play bar under it. A "now playing" label shows the rank numeral, a small caps line and the name. In the last 0.7 s the camera pushes into the chosen card until its clip fills the 9:16 frame, which hands off to the clip itself. The push ends on the part of the clip you choose with `focusX`, so the subject stays in frame.

**Use it** as the opening of a "Top 5 …" short, or between entries to show what is coming next. For a full countdown, render it once per entry and change `items[0]` and `items[1]` each time.

| Variant | Name | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | **Ring** | Five cards on a turning ring, seen from a low three-quarter angle. The ring fades in as one layer while it scales up and spins, lands on #5 (the label reads by 0.75 s), then turns one step to #4. The far row shows only ~110 px above the playing card, with its own clips on the card backs at low brightness, and the side cards dissolve before the frame edge, so nothing is cut by it or sits under the like/share column. |
| `1` | **Stack flip** | A deck of five cards rises in from below the frame, card by card and fully opaque, with #5 in front. Each card behind shows a ~40 px lip with a 1 px top hairline, stepping darker toward the back, so five clips read in the stack at phone size. The front card hinges on its top edge and flips up toward you, uncovering #4. It then goes over the top of the deck and drops in behind it as the darkest back lip, while #4 comes forward. The deck and its label sit 90 px higher than Ring's (front card y ≈ 667–1143). |

`bg`: `"plate"` fills the frame with a blurred copy of the playing clip at 0.18 gain and saturate 0.8. Its exposure is matched so every clip gives a similar level. A vertical ink grade (#0B0B0E at 55% top, 25% at 45% height, 75% bottom) and a radial ink field (as `radial-gradient(120% 70% at 50% 48%, transparent 0%, #0B0B0E 78%)`) keep the upper third and the edges clean ink, so only a faint glow of the clip's colour sits behind the cards. It crossfades when the carousel turns. `"none"` leaves the area around the cards transparent. The cards always show footage.

notes.timing: seconds. land = the carousel settles on #5; travel = "5" flies from the title into the lockup; out0 = #5's name leaves; turn = ring turn / deck flip starts; push = camera starts flying into #4; hit = arrival + payoff (a cut to #4's full-bleed shot); roll = numeral 5 -> 4 (lands on the hit); name1 = #4's name; cut2 = the next cut on rhythm; exit = type blurs out.

components.name: This or that
components.job: A this-or-that poll card ('Jason or Lucia?') with a tap and fill animation, ending on 'Comment A or B'.
components.summary:
A this-or-that poll for GTA 6 shorts. The two options land, a tap picks one, the result runs in, and the clip ends on **"Comment [A] or [B]"**. It turns the viewer's opinion into a comment, and comments drive the algorithm. Put it in the last 5 s of a comparison or character segment ("Jason or Lucia?", "Vice City or the Keys?").

Craft v2: 4K graded trailer shots cut on the beat, the Look finishing layer (grain, vignette, exposure hit), and type set at title scale on the image. There is no card.
components.configDocs:
- `variants["0"|"1"]`
  - `style`: `"bars"` or `"split"`.
  - `kicker` (Bars) / `question` (Split tap): the line above the options. In Split tap the ask replaces the question in the same slot.
  - `options`: two `{ key, label, pct }`. `key` is the letter on the key and in the ask. `label` is the option (keep it to about 9 characters: names are 104 px / 96 px wide caps). `pct` is **your own poll result** (e.g. a YouTube community poll or a story sticker). The two should add up to 100. The demo numbers are placeholders.
  - `pick`: the option the tap lands on (0 or 1). It gets the sunset accent and the hit. Make it the winner.
  - `layout` (Bars): `kicker`, `rows` (the tops of the two 128 px rows; the bars are the rows) and `cta`, in px. Keep the winner's `pct` under ~75: above that the beam reaches the percentage on the right.
  - `seam` (Split tap): `top` / `bottom` of the range the seam maps onto (the safe zone, 230–1480) and `gap` (the type's distance from the seam). The seam lands at `top + (bottom − top) × pct of A`.
  - `frame`: how each sample shot sits in the frame, `{ x, y, s }` (offset in px and scale, from the top-left).
  - `timing` (s): `rows` (when each option lands), `press` (the tap), `fill` (bars / seam and count), `hit` (the payoff, on a cut), `sheen`, `cta` (the ask), `keys` (A and B press once, this long after the ask), `out` (exit), `end`.
- `cta.pre` / `cta.or`: the words of the ask ("Comment", "or").
- `look`: grain, vignette and the exposure peak of the hit (per variant).

variants.kindEvidence: transparent overlay: no footage, grain, vignette or exposure hits

notes.look: exposure peak of the payoff hit, per variant

components.name: Facecam split
components.job: Reaction layout: facecam (assets/plates/facecam-sample.mp4, a stand-in talking head) plus gameplay, with a clean seam and label.
components.summary:
A reaction layout for GTA 6 shorts. Your facecam and the footage you're reacting to share the frame, joined by a seam of light and labelled with a title lockup that says who is reacting and to what. It is edited like a top reaction short: the game cuts on rhythm, your face is the held second camera, and on the big moment the face **punches in** while the footage takes an exposure hit. Use it for trailer reactions, first-look breakdowns, and any compilation where your face and voice carry the clip.

- **Variant 0, Top/bottom.**
  - GTA 6 footage on top (1080×980), cut on rhythm from 16:9 shots, and your facecam below (1080×940), framed big and slightly right of centre.
  - The seam at y 980 is a 2 px line of warm light with bloom, sitting in a valley of shadow. It draws in with a glint, flares on the payoff, and glints again on every cut.
  - The lockup hugs the seam from above: `@EVERESTCHRIS6 REACTS` (Archivo wide, tracked) over a 207 px wide **GTA 6**, with the "6" in the Leonida sunset and a sheen on the hit.
  - The payoff is at 1.3 s, on the cut to the explosion.
- **Variant 1, Corner bubble.**
  - Full-bleed vertical GTA 6 shots, cut on rhythm.
  - Your facecam is a 380 px circle docked in the top-left corner. Its 3 px white rim draws on, its warm rim light breathes while you talk, and it has a contact shadow.
  - Beside it sits the lockup `@EVERESTCHRIS6` over **Vice / City** (Inter display, 190 px, "City" in sunset), in the sky band of the shots.
  - The payoff is at 1.35 s, on the cut to the skydive: an exposure hit, the face punches in inside the bubble, the bubble pulses and the rim flares.
  - The lockup blurs out at 4.55 s, and the bubble stays docked to the end.

1080×1920, 30 fps, 6 s. All type sits inside the safe zone (x 72–936, y 230–1480). The finishing layer (grain, vignette, exposure hit) comes from `assets/kit/look`.
components.configDocs:
| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| `duration` | Length in seconds (also set `data-duration` on `#root` and the facecam `<video>`s). |
| `handle` | Reference only: the handle shown on screen lives in each variant's `kicker`. |
| `sunset` | The accent gradient used on the hero's second word. |
| `facecam.clip` | Your facecam clip (sample: `assets/cam/facecam-sample.mp4`, re-encoded with a keyframe every second). |
| `facecam.srcW / srcH` | Pixel size of the facecam source (16:9 webcam: 1920 × 1080). |
| `facecam.eyes.{x,y}` | Where your eyes sit in the source (0–1). This anchors the framing and the punch-in. |
| `voice.rate / seed` | v1's rim light "speaking" envelope: updates per second (syllable rate) and its deterministic seed. |
| `variants[n].shots[]` | The footage cut list: `{src, at, dur, in, pos}` = clip, start on the timeline, duration, in-point in the clip, and `object-position` (v0 crops 16:9 shots into the top panel, so pick the subject with `pos`). **Mirror any change on the matching static `<video>` tag** (`a0`–`a4` for v0, `b0`–`b3` for v1). Never let `in + dur` run past a clip's end. |
| `variants[n].kicker` | The small tracked line above the hero. |
| `variants[n].hero` | `[first, second]`: the hero words. The second carries the sunset fill. |
| `variants[n].hit` | The payoff time (put it on a cut): exposure hit, shake, face punch-in, seam or rim flare, sheen. |
| `variants[n].punchOut` | The cut where the face jumps back out of the punch-in. |
| `variants[n].punch` | Punch-in scale (v0 1.2, v1 1.18). |
| `variants[n].expose` | Exposure peak of the hit (v0 1.85; v1 1.5, because bright skies blow out). |
| `variants[n].face` | `{scale, bx, by}`: facecam scale of the source, and where the eyes land in the panel or bubble (0–1). It always covers its box. |
| `variants[n].camIn` | Facecam in-point (s). |
| `variants[n].out` | When the lockup blurs out. |
| `variants["0"].seamY` | Seam height in px (default 980): gameplay above, facecam below. |
| `variants["0"].heroWidth` | Ink width the hero is fitted to (default 720 px; never below 180 px type). |
| `variants["1"].bubble` | `{size, left, top}` of the facecam circle (default `{380, 72, 256}`). |

components.name: Clip grid
components.job: Several clips at once with numbered labels ('4 details in 4 seconds').
components.configDocs:
- `duration`: seconds (5). If you change it, also change `data-duration` on `#root`.
- `variants["0"|"1"]`:
  - `layout`: `"grid"` (4 cells) or `"stack"` (3 bands).
  - `kicker`: the small tracked line, e.g. `"4 scenes in 4 seconds"`. Grid: bottom-left of cell 3. Stack: top-left (it ends up in the black above the letterbox). Keep it to about 22 characters.
  - `cells`: one entry per clip, in number order (grid: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right; stack: top to bottom).
    - `label`: one or two words, all labels the same kind of thing (scenes, places, characters) so they match the kicker. Grid right-column labels have about 320 px (13 characters).
    - `clip`: the clip's path. Grid cells use **vertical 9:16** clips (1080×1920); stack bands use **16:9** clips (1920×1080).
    - `in`: the in-point, in seconds.
    - `grade` (optional): a CSS filter for that clip only, e.g. `"contrast(1.14) saturate(1.14)"` to lift a flat shot.
    - `zoom` / `origin` (grid) or `zoom` / `focus` (stack), optional: scale the clip inside its cell and choose the point it scales from. Use it to frame a subject or push a HUD element out of the cell.
- `timing.grid`: `first` (when cell 1 starts docking, 0.45), `step` (time between docks, 0.5), `dock` (dock length, 0.36), `take` / `takeDur` (when and how fast the last cell takes the frame back, 3.75 / 0.5). The payoff lands at `first + 3 × step + dock`.
- `timing.stack`: `step` (time between bands, 0.4), `wipe` (0.5), `payoff` (1.22, when band 3 has landed), `out` (3.42, when the outer bands leave).

components.name: Cinematic bars
components.job: Letterbox bars slide in with a place/time stamp, or a CCTV-style stamp, for cinematic or 'caught on camera' moments.
components.summary:
Letterbox bars that turn a GTA 6 clip into a *moment*. The vertical clip plays full-bleed, the bars close, and the picture opens up into a widescreen band, with the type set in the black above and below it. It runs 5.6 s and is clear by about 5.0 s, so it loops or cuts cleanly. It's an overlay: render it with `bg: "none"` for a transparent WebM.

| Variant | Use it for | Look |
|---|---|---|
| `0` Letterbox + time | A cinematic shot, a story beat, "first night in Vice City", a sunset montage | A 16:9 film gate (band y 656–1264, bars 656 px each). The bars glide in over 0.72 s, carrying `VICE CITY` in Archivo wide 800 at 120 px, centred, with a warm bloom. On the hit (0.9 s) the picture cuts to the wide shot with an impact punch and an exposure hit, and the title's bloom swells with the light. `NOVEMBER 19 · 5:24 PM` then rises under the picture in Rockstar's date style (white wide-tracked Archivo caps with a magenta kiss). Type masks out from 3.92 s and the gate opens at 4.4 s. |
| `1` CCTV stamp | "Caught on camera": a police stop, a getaway, an NPC doing something wild, any clip that could be security footage | A 4:3 security feed (band y 555–1365, bars 555 px each) that snaps shut over the clip. Above the feed is Rockstar's own two-line CCTV on-screen display from Trailer 2 (`FRONT DOOR / 09:58:47`), at poster scale: the camera name over a ticking clock, in JetBrains Mono 600 at 128 px, flush left on its ink. Under the feed is `CAM 06 · THU 11-19-2026`. The feed has fine scanlines, a barrel falloff and a slow roll bar. Every cut is a camera switch: the name and CAM id cut with the picture, the OSD drops for one frame, and the camera's auto-iris pulses. The payoff (2.9 s) is the switch to STREET as the police car turns in: an exposure blowout, a punch zoom, a 4 px chroma tick on the clock, then a slow PTZ push. The monitor snaps open at 4.9 s. |

All type sits in the letterbox black, never on the picture, so it stays legible on any clip and never covers a face.
components.configDocs:
- `duration`: the total length (5.6 s).
- `variants["0"]` (letterbox):
  - `aspect`: the band shape. `16/9` gives a 1080×608 picture and 656 px bars. With `2.39` the bars are thicker and the picture becomes a thin strip.
  - `shots`: the ids of the sample `<video>` tags this variant shows.
  - `place`: the hero line, set in uppercase. `placeSize` (120) shrinks by 1 px at a time, down to 110, only if the line would be wider than `placeMaxWidth` (790, centred, so it stays inside x 145–935). `placeTracking` is in em.
  - `placeGap` / `timeGap`: px from the picture's top edge to the bottom of the title, and from its bottom edge to the time line.
  - `time`: the line under the picture, at `timeSize` px. Match it to the light in your clip.
  - `bloom`: the title's two bloom colours (inner, outer).
  - `t`: when the bars start closing (`barsIn`) and how long they take (`barsDur`); when the title starts (`hero`); the payoff cut (`hit`); when the time line starts (`time`); when the type starts to mask out (`out`); and when the bars open (`barsOut`, `barsOutDur`).
  - `pushes`: `[element, start, duration, scale]` slow pushes on the footage, one per shot (plate only).
- `variants["1"]` (CCTV):
  - `aspect`: `4/3` (the classic CCTV frame).
  - `cams`: one entry per camera switch, `{ at, name, id, payoff }`. `name` is the first OSD line and `id` is the CAM number under the feed. Keep `at` equal to the `data-start` of the matching `<video>`. Name each camera after what the clip shows: a fixed-camera name over handheld footage reads as fake.
  - `clock`: `HH:MM:SS` at the first cut. It ticks once a second. Match it to the light (14:07 for daylight).
  - `date`: the date under the feed.
  - `osdSize` / `osdGap` / `metaGap`: the OSD size and its distances from the feed's edges.
  - `grade`: a CSS filter for the sample feed (plate only). `null` keeps full colour.
  - `t`: `barsIn`/`barsDur` (the snap shut), `live` (the cut to the feed), `out` (the OSD powers off and the bars snap open), `barsOutDur`.
  - `pushes`: as above. The payoff shot gets the PTZ push.

components.name: Social video frame
components.job: A clip presented as an in-world social video post: avatar, fictional handle, Follow pill, caption, like count.
components.configDocs:
- `fill`: `blur`, `brightness`, `saturate`, `zoom` and `drift` for the blurred background copy.
- `variants["0" | "1"]`:
  - `clip`: video path. It must match the `src` of that variant's two `<video>` tags (`#fill0`/`#card0` or `#fill1`/`#card1`).
  - `card`: `{ width, aspect, top, focus }`, the card geometry in px. `focus` is the clip's `object-position` inside the card, e.g. `"50% 34%"`.
  - `scrim`: `{ height, mid, midAt, max }`, the bottom fade. `height` is a share of the card (Reel 0.32, Live 0.50); the fade runs from clear to `mid` opacity at `midAt`% and to `max` at the bottom. Keep it low on Reel so the footage stays bright; Live needs more for the chat.
  - `avatar`: `{ emblem, from, to }`, a badge disc. `emblem` is a key of the `EMBLEMS` map below CONFIG (`palm`, `shades`, `user`); `from`/`to` is the disc gradient (default: the Leonida core `#F84FA4` → `#FE8E4E`).
  - `handle`: the account name (keep it fictional or your own).
  - `caption`: the caption text. It wraps balanced inside 700 px; `\n` forces a break.
  - Reel only:
    - `likes: { from, steps, at, every }`: starts at `from` and adds `steps[i]` at `at + i·every` seconds, each with a short digit roll. Keep every value at the same number of digits.
    - `comments`: the comment count, as text.
    - `age`: the post age label, e.g. "2h".
    - `likeAt`: when the double-tap heart fires, in seconds (it is gone 0.5 s later).
    - `followAt`: when Follow is tapped, in seconds.
  - Live only:
    - `viewers: { from, steps, at, every }`: same as `likes`, for "watching".
    - `followAt`: when Follow is tapped, in seconds.
    - `chat`: a list of `{ u, m }` (user, message).
    - `chatStart`: when the first comment arrives, in seconds.
    - `chatEvery`: the gap between comments, in seconds.
- `chatOldest`: the opacity of the oldest of the three visible live comments (default .75).
- `timing`: `in`, `out` (when the UI starts to leave) and `end`.

`EMBLEMS` (just below CONFIG) holds the avatar glyphs as white SVG paths in a 24×24 box. To add your own, add a key with your paths and point `avatar.emblem` at it. Every chat commenter uses the neutral `user` silhouette.

The accent colour is the `--gold` CSS variable (used only on the Follow pill), and the type shadow is `--shadow-type`.

components.name: Time skip card
components.job: '3 HOURS LATER' or a date card between scenes.
components.summary:
A full-frame bridge for a jump in time in a GTA 6 short ("3 hours later", "the next day", or stamping a real date such as the GTA 6 launch, Thursday, November 19, 2026). The time skip is carried by the edit itself:

- In **Time skip**, the hours pass through the light, cut by cut.
- In **Date card**, the calendar turns on the cut from night to morning.

Use it in story edits and compilations between two scenes, or as a chapter beat.

1080×1920, 30 fps, 5.8 s. Craft v2: 4K-sourced graded shots at 1.0×, the Look finishing kit (grain, vignette, exposure-pulse hit), with no cards and no tints.
components.configDocs:
- `duration`: 5.8. If you change it, also change `data-duration` on `#root` and `#ov`.
- `sunset`: the gradient used for the landing numeral.
- `variants["0"]` (Time skip)
  - `count`: the numerals shown on each cut (`["1","2","3"]`). The last one is the payoff and lands in sunset.
  - `unit`, `plural`, `later`: the words ("Hour", "s", "Later"). Try "Day" / "s" or "Minute" / "s".
  - `place`: the label's place ("Vice City").
  - `clock`: the time before the skip, then one entry per cut. Only the hour's last digit may change, because that digit is the odometer.
  - `cuts`: the cut times [hour 1, hour 2, payoff]. Keep them on whole frames (multiples of 1/30 s) and equal to the `data-start` of the matching `<video>`.
  - `shotStarts`: the start of every shot (documentation, and the per-shot push).
  - `out`: when the lockup exits.
- `variants["1"]` (Date card)
  - `day`: `[before, after]`. Digits that change roll; digits that stay the same cross-fade into sunset.
  - `weekday`: `[before, after]`.
  - `month`, `year`.
  - `roll`: the cut, roll and hit time. It must equal the `data-start` of `<video id="v1b">`.
  - `nudge`: an optical centring offset for the day numeral in px (−6 for "19", because Archivo's "1" has a wide left bearing).
  - `shotStarts`, `out`.
