components.name: Sunset wipe
components.job: Transition between two clips: diagonal bands in the Leonida sunset gradient sweep across.
components.summary:
A full-frame transition between two clips. Diagonal bands (or a single iris ring) in the Leonida sunset sweep across the frame and leave the next clip behind them.

Each band is a printed panel, not a flat gradient:
- solid sunset gradient on its leading 40%, then ink-navy halftone dots that grow toward its trailing edge (the comic-print tonal ramp);
- a 4 px ink keyline on both edges;
- a 1 px highlight on the leading edge;
- on the bands, solid ink gutters between neighbouring bands, so the group reads as one keylined object with no footage slivers between the bands.

The cut from clip A to clip B is hidden under the widest band, so you never see a hard edge. The incoming clip lands on a beat: a 2-frame scale punch plus a short shake on the first frame where the cut has cleared.

1080×1920, 30 fps, 5.0 s. The timeline (bands; the iris is within a few frames):
- 0–0.1 s: the end of the return wipe (B → A) leaves the frame. The loop seam sits inside this wipe.
- To 1.57 s: clip A plays.
- 1.57–2.07 s: the A → B wipe runs. Clip B lands at 1.9 s (frame 57, both variants).
- To 4.73 s: clip B plays clean.
- 4.73 s to the end: the same wipe runs in reverse and is mid-frame on the last frame, then carries on from frame 0.

The demo loops with no visible seam. Both clips run continuously through it, and the seam is covered by a moving wipe.
components.configDocs:
| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| `variants[*].palette` | The sunset colours. Bands: from the leading edge (meets the outgoing clip) to the trailing edge (reveals the incoming clip). Iris: from the amber side to the blue side of the ring. |
| `variants[*].clipA / clipB` | The outgoing and incoming clips. They must match the `src` of that variant's `<video>` tags: `v0a` and `v0r` (A), and `v0b` and `v0w` (B). For the iris, use `v1a`, `v1r`, `v1b` and `v1w`. |
| `variants["0"].angle` | Band tilt from vertical, in degrees. 30 sweeps from top-left to bottom-right. |
| `variants["0"].bands` | The bands as `[from, to]` px, measured back from the leading edge. Default: lead line `[0,36]`, panels `[46,340]` and `[350,600]`, trailing line `[610,634]`, each 10 px apart. |
| `variants["0"].gutter` | The colour that fills the gaps between bands (default `#0B0B0E`). `null` lets the footage show through the gaps. |
| `variants["1"].rings` | The iris ring as `[from, to]` px back from the leading (outer) edge. Default: `[[0,96]]`, one 96 px ring. It stays a solid sun disc until its hole is 24 px wide, and clip B only shows once the hole has opened. |
| `variants["1"].sweep` | The direction of the colour sweep round the ring, as a CSS gradient angle pointing from amber toward blue. The default, 300, puts blue at the top left and amber at the bottom right, the same axis as the bands. |
| `variants[*].cut` | Where the A/B cut sits, in px back from the leading edge. Keep it inside the widest band. |
| `variants[*].ink` | `{ width, color }`: the keyline on both edges of every band. `null` switches it off. |
| `variants[*].highlight` | `{ width, color }`: the thin line just inside each band's leading keyline. `null` switches it off. |
| `variants[*].print` | The halftone inside each band: `{ pitch, clear, max, alpha, color, minBand }`. There are no dots on the leading `clear` share of each band (0.4, clean gradient). The ink coverage then grows to `max` (0.32) at its trailing edge. `pitch` is the dot spacing (22 px), and `alpha` and `color` style the dots (0.6, `#1F202B`). Bands narrower than `minBand` px stay solid (on the bands that is the lead and trailing lines). Add `footage: { light, dark, blur }` to scale the dots by the incoming clip's smoothed tones instead of `max`. `null` gives flat gradient bands. |
| `variants[*].halftone` | `{ size, maxR, depth }`: the dot fringe trailing the last band (dot pitch, largest dot radius, how far it trails). `null` switches it off (the iris default). |
| `variants["1"].fade` | `[opening, closing]`: the iris fades while its outer radius is under this many px (default `[50, 120]`). The sun disc is solid from its second frame, and the close never ends on a lone dot. |
| `variants["0"].pushA / pushB / scaleA / scaleB` | How far the outgoing clip is shoved along the sweep (and its zoom), and how far the incoming clip travels in (and the scale it starts from). Whenever a shift (or the impact shake) would uncover the frame edge, the scale is raised automatically, so the clip underneath never shows through. |
| `variants["1"].center` | Where the iris opens, in px. Default `[620, 700]`, which keeps the ring whole inside the frame up to a 460 px radius while the face in p05 still lands inside the hole. Point it near the next clip's subject and keep it inside x 72–936, y 230–1480. |
| `variants["1"].scaleA / scaleB` | The outgoing clip pushes in to `scaleA`. The incoming clip lands from `scaleB`. |
| `variants[*].timing` | `{ wipeIn, wipeOut, wipeDur, lag, ease }`. `wipeIn` and `wipeOut` are when the A → B wipe and the return B → A wipe start. `wipeDur` is how long each wipe runs. `lag` is how long after a wipe starts the incoming clip starts travelling in. `ease` is `"power3.inOut"` for the bands. For the iris it is `"expo"`: a constant zoom rate from `r0` px on the open, down to `r1` px on the close. |
| `impact` | `{ scale, shake, frames }`: the landing on the first frame after the cut clears. The default is a 1.035 → 1 punch over 2 frames plus a 6 px decaying shake along the sweep (vertical for the iris). |
| `timing` | `{ end, fps, loop }`: the composition length and frame rate (the impact frame is snapped to the frame grid). With `loop: true`, the return wipe runs on past `end` and wraps to frame 0, so the loop seam is hidden inside it. With `false`, frame 0 starts on clean clip A. |

components.name: Punch zoom transition
components.job: Fast punch-in zoom blur (or whip pan) from one clip into the next, with a light flash.
components.summary:
A full-frame transition for GTA 6 compilation shorts (TikTok, Shorts, Reels). Clip A plays, then the camera either **punches in** with a radial zoom blur or **whips sideways** with a horizontal motion blur, and clip B lands. Near the end the same transition runs back into clip A, so the demo loops with no jump cut.

There's no text, so it fits between any two clips in a "top 10" or "details you missed" compilation without clashing with your captions.

1080×1920, 30 fps, 6.0 s. One HyperFrames project, two variants:

| Variant | Name | Sample clips | Use it for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0` | Punch zoom | police SUV charging (p09) → man at the truck (p05) → back to the SUV | Hard-hitting beats: the next rank, a reveal, a drop on the music. Clip A accelerates into your subject (`focusA`) over about 7 frames, keeping its contrast. On the cut frame the exposure burns: highlights clip while B's silhouette shows through. B then arrives still streaked from 1.25× and settles in 0.3 s. |
| `1` | Whip pan | Lucia at the gate (p06) → drive-by past the mural (p04) → back to Lucia | Moving between locations or characters. A whips out to the left with a full-frame horizontal smear, and the switch to B happens at peak blur, inside the shutter, so there's never an A/B edge on screen. B whips in and decelerates. A soft amber lift marks the peak. |

**Hero frame:** t = 1.66 s (frame 50). Both effects are clearly underway and the subject is still readable: the SUV punching in (v0) and Lucia starting to whip out (v1).
components.configDocs:
Shared:
- `duration`: total seconds. Keep it equal to `#root data-duration`.

Punch zoom (`variants["0"]`):
- `clipA.src` / `clipA.in`: the outgoing clip and its media in-point in seconds. `clipB.src` / `clipB.in`: the same for the incoming clip.
- `cut`: the flash frame where A becomes B.
- `returnCut`: where B punches back into A for the loop. Set it to `null` to end on B.
- `focusA` / `focusB`: the punch centres as `[x, y]` fractions of the frame. Put each one on its clip's subject.
- `punchIn`: seconds of accelerating zoom before the cut. `land`: seconds for the incoming clip to settle.
- `zoomA`: scale at the cut (2.3). `zoomB`: the scale the incoming clip lands from, down to 1.0.
- `landStreak`: the radial streak the incoming clip arrives with, as a fraction of `maxSpread`. It decays to 0 over `land`.
- `shutter`: blur length = zoom speed × shutter. `maxSpread`: the cap on streak length. `prefilter`: source pre-blur per pixel of streak.
- `vignette`: edge darkening while blurred. `drift`: the slow push on each held clip.
- `flash`: cut-frame flash strength (0.75 is a burn; 1 is near-white). `preFlash`: the exposure lift on the 2 frames before the cut. `flashDecay`: how fast it falls back. `exposure`: the multiplicative burn. `lift`: the additive shadow lift, scaled by flash².

Whip pan (`variants["1"]`):
- `clipA`, `clipB`: as above.
- `start`: when the whip begins. The switch is at `start + whip/2`. `returnStart`: when it whips back into A, or `null` to end on B. `whip`: how long each whip lasts (power4 in-out).
- `travel`: how far each clip slides, as a fraction of frame width. `direction`: `"left"` (picture travels left, B enters from the right) or `"right"`.
- `shutter`: blur length = speed × shutter (centred, tapered). `maxBlur`: the cap in px. `prefilter`: source pre-blur per pixel of streak.
- `camPunch`: camera scale bump at mid-whip. `drift`: the slow push.
- `leak` / `leakWidth`: strength and half-width of the soft #FE8E4E glow at the switch (`0` turns it off). `flash`: the amber exposure lift at peak speed.

variants.label: Punch zoom / Whip pan
variants.kindEvidence: Full-frame transition: it always shows footage

components.name: Chapter card
components.job: Interstitial between segments: 'DETAIL 04' + title, over a sunset card or the blurred footage.
components.summary: A full-frame interstitial between two segments of a compilation short: the outgoing clip plays, then the chapter (`DETAIL 04` + a title + a sub line + a "4 of 10" progress row), then the incoming clip. Use it in "10 details you missed", "every new feature" or ranked-list GTA 6 shorts, wherever you cut from one detail to the next. 1080x1920, 30 fps, 5.2 s.
components.configDocs:
- `variants["0" | "1"]`
  - `style`: `"card"` (sunset card) or `"blur"` (blurred footage).
  - `kicker`, `num`, `of`: the label and number (`"Detail"`, `4` gives `DETAIL 04`) and the length of the progress row (`of: 0` hides the row).
  - `title`: the chapter title. `\n` forces a line break; lines auto-fit to `layout.titleMaxWidth`.
  - `sub`: the sub line (`""` hides it).
  - `clipOut` / `clipIn`: `{ src, from }` for the segment that ends and the one that starts. `from` is the source second the clip starts at. v0's `clipIn` also has `rate` (playback rate; the sample uses 0.62 to stay inside p06's clean window, so use 1 for a long clip).
  - `window` (v0 only): the hero window, `{ w, h, top, radius, focusY }` (sample: 750×422 at top 1006, r28, x 165–915 to match the title). `focusY` sets which part of the 9:16 clip shows in the window: `0` = the top (keeps a face in frame), `1` = the bottom. The window is a clip-path over the full-frame clip, which is scaled down into it and grows back to 1:1 on exit, so the video never has to be resized.
  - `hold` (v1 only): `{ src, from, rate, at }`, the clip that plays under the full blur, crossfaded in at `at` seconds. The sample p02 is clean only for 0–1.35 s, so the hold is that window reversed (`assets/custom/p02-blue-club-rev-v.mp4`, from 0.15 = source 1.15 s, at 0.4×). It continues from where `v1out` is, as a slow push. With a long clean clip, use `{ src: clipOut.src, from: clipOut.from + at, rate: 1, at }`, or `null` to drop the hold layer and let `v1out` run on.
- `layout`: `centerY` (lockup centre per style), `titleMaxWidth` (740, which keeps glyphs inside the safe zone), `titleSize` (min/max px per style; v1 is Barlow Condensed 800, up to 150 px), `blurTracking` (v1 title tracking in em, 0.06).
- `blur`: the v1 defocus at full strength: `px` (scaled by the push, so 9 at zoom 1.38 is ≈ 12 px on screen), `brightness` (.74), `saturate`, `dip` (brightness at the clip swap; .72 is only a slight dip, so the crossfade never turns muddy), `zoom` and `origin` (centre of the push; aim it at the brightest part of your clip).
- `timing`: `card` (`in`, `move`, `out` = when the window starts to grow; the lockup leaves 0.15 s before it, `grow`), `blur` (`in`, `ramp`, `textOut`, `swap`, `dipDur`, `focusDur`; the focus pull starts at `swap + dipDur`) and `end`. If you change `end`, also change `data-duration` on `#root` and `#ov`.

components.name: X post card
components.job: An X post card (by @everestchris6) with one phrase highlighted and counts rolling.
components.summary:
**The post becomes the headline.** An X post from your own account (@everestchris6) lands as a full-width, faithful post card over a cut montage of GTA 6 shots. Its key phrase is highlighted, and then the phrase lifts off the card and flies up into the headline slot in one move (a FLIP), landing on a hard cut with a light hit, a shake and a small RGB split. The card keeps a gap where the words were until they settle back after the hit. The big type is the hook; the card underneath is the receipt.

After the hit the post gets its own second beat: it gets liked, X-style (the heart fills pink and pops with a ring and a dot burst, and the like count rolls up). The other counts tick up digit by digit, the views keep ticking like a live post, and the card drifts slowly through the hold. 6.5 s, 1080×1920, 30 fps.

**When to use it in a GTA 6 short:** for the fact or take you're about to talk over, as the hook at the top of a short or the "source" beat before a reaction. Examples: "pre-load is live", "Trailer 1 did 90M views in 24 hours", or a hot take. Use it for your own posts or a fan-made voice; never fake a post from Rockstar or a real person.
components.configDocs:
- `author`:
  - `name`, `handle`: the display name and @handle.
  - `avatar`: a square image path; the sample is `assets/img/avatar-everest.jpg`.
  - `initials`: shown instead when `avatar` is `""`.
- `layout`:
  - `left`, `width`: the card and headline column, `72 / 864` (the full safe width).
  - `titleTop`: the headline's top in px.
  - `gap`: the space between the headline and the card.
  - `maxBottom`: the lowest the card may reach.
- `variants["0" | "1"]`:
  - `style`: `"light"` or `"dark"`.
  - `highlight`: `"marker"` (a sunset highlighter sweep; the ink flips exactly at the edge) or `"light"` (the phrase goes pure white while the rest dims to `dim`).
  - `text`: the post. Wrap the **one** phrase in `[[double brackets]]` and keep it to one line (up to about 34 characters). In marker mode with a `flip`, mark exactly the headline's words (v0: `[[Pre-load is live]] right now.`). It reads best leading the post, followed by `\n`. Keep the post to about 4 lines in total (about 110 characters). Use ` ` to keep words together and `‑` for a hyphen that must not break.
  - `time`, `date`: the meta line.
  - `counts`: `{ views, replies, reposts, likes, saves }` as raw numbers, shown X-style (`862`, `1.2K`, `24K`, `486.2K Views`).
  - `title`: the headline.
    - `kicker`: the small tracked label above it.
    - `lines`: an array of lines, set in Archivo wide caps.
    - `fill`: `"white"` or `"sunset"`.
    - `maxSize`: px.
    - `fit`: the share of the safe width the widest line fills, e.g. `0.90`.
    - `unit`: the label under it, e.g. `"Views in 24 hours"`.
    - `bloom` (optional, white fill): `{ color, strength }`, a soft glow around the headline.
    - `count` (optional): `{ line, from, to, suffix, roll }` makes that line a number (`to` + `suffix`). With `roll: false` (v1) it is static: it flies out of the post and lands reading the same value on every frame. With `roll: true` and no `flip`, it rolls `from` → `to` as it lands (keep both the same digit count). A number that flies out of the post never rolls.
    - `slam` (optional): the headline lands on the payoff cut this many times too big and settles to 1 in 0.4 s (v0: 1.08, v1: 1.14).
    - `stretch` (optional, marker flip): `{ dur }`. Each line lands at its chip's width on Archivo's width axis (measured, 62–125 %) and stretches out to the wide face in `dur` s (v0: 0.5).
  - `flip`: the words in `text` that lift off the card on the payoff. If the headline has a `count`, the number itself flies out of these words (v1: `"90M+"`). Otherwise the highlighted words split into one chip per headline line (by word count of each line in `title.lines`) and each chip lands on its own line: text edge on x 72, baseline on the line's baseline, cap height on the headline's (v0: `"Pre-load is live"` → "Pre-load" | "is live"). Use `""` to turn it off.
  - `highlightAt`, `lift`, `flipLead`, `flipBlur` (optional, per variant): override `timing.highlight`, `timing.lift`, `timing.flipLead` and `timing.flipBlur` (v0: 0.6, 1.17, 0.32 (the whole flight, so it arrives on the cut), 9).
  - `chroma` (optional): `{ px, dur }`, the RGB split on the landing headline (v0: 5 px for 0.18 s; default 14 px for 0.36 s).
  - `expose` (optional, plate only): `{ peak }`, an exposure pulse on the footage at the payoff (`Look.expose`; v0: 1.3). Use it with `flash: 0`.
  - `tokenFill` (count flip only): `true` settles the flip word back into the post in the sunset fill after the number lands, so the highlight still reads at rest.
  - `bodySize` (optional): the post's body size in px (default 50; v1 uses 46 for three even lines). Keep each line of `text` inside the 768 px measure at that size.
  - `shots`: the ids of the `<video>` elements this variant shows.
  - `reframe` (optional): `{ videoId: { from: {…}, to: {…}, ease } }`, any GSAP-settable props on a shot (`scale`, `x`, `y`, `objectPosition`, `filter`), optionally pushed to `to` across the shot. A `transformOrigin` in `from` sets the pivot. Use it to move a shot's subject out from under the card (v1's `b3` scales the night drive 1.25 from its top edge so the skyline fills the headline band and the passenger stays below the card; `b4` shows the right side of the horizontal pier master so the couple never enters the frame), to give one shot its own push (v0's `a1` drops 170 px and scales 1.06 from its bottom edge; v0's `a3` goes 1.0 → 1.05), or to grade one shot (v0's `a2` gets `contrast(1.22) saturate(1.15) brightness(.95)`; v1's `b3` gets an extra `blur(4px) brightness(1.3)` for real bokeh).
  - `shotScrim` (optional, plate only): `{ videoId: strength }`, an extra copy of the headline scrim that cuts in and out with that shot, for a bright sky behind the headline (v0: `a3` 1, `a4` 0.35; v1: `b4` 0.4, `b5` 0.55). A shot that runs past the exit fades it out with the graphic. `shotScrimCss` (optional) gives it its own gradient (v0 uses the firmer r07 scrim there); it defaults to `scrimCss`.
  - `flash`: the white overlay flash on the payoff cut (v0: 0, it uses `expose`; v1: 0.5).
  - `payoff`: when the headline hits, in seconds. Put it on a cut.
  - `out`: this variant's exit time (falls back to `timing.out`).
  - `sheen`: `true` sends a warm light band across the card on the hit.
  - `dim` (light highlight): the alpha of the white post text that isn't the phrase (v1: 0.60, so the white line and the sunset token stand out).
  - `scrim`: 0–1, the strength of the soft top darkening behind the headline. `scrimCss` is its gradient.
  - `scrimBottom` (plate only): the strength of the kit's `.lk-scrim-bottom` under the card (v1: 0.35).
  - `rack`: px of focus blur on the footage behind the card (0 = sharp; v1: 5).
  - `rackGrade`: the filter added in the racked state (v1: `contrast(1.2) saturate(1.15) brightness(1.08)`, so lights bloom into bokeh).
  - `glow`: `[[time, "rgba(...)"], …]`, the light behind the card per shot, or `null`. On the dark card the same colour tints the top rim and a soft wash across its top.
  - `smoke`: the full-frame wash used only with `bg: "none"`.
- `rollFrom`: the counts start from this fraction of their value (0.93), so they tick (452.2K → 486.2K) and never start from 0.
- `likeFrom`: the like count rolls up from this fraction of its value on the like beat (0.9: 22K → 24K).
- `tickAt`: the moments (s) when the views tick up by one more unit during the hold.
- `timing`, all in seconds:
  - `cardIn`, `highlight`, `highlightDur`.
  - `countsAfter`: the time from the payoff to the count roll.
  - `rollDur`, `digitStagger`.
  - `flip`, `flipLead`, `flipBlur`: the flight's duration, how long before the payoff it leaves the card, and its vertical motion blur in px.
  - `lift` (count flip only): when the post's number turns sunset and peels off its line, before the flight.
  - `likeAfter`, `likeDur`: when the like lands after the payoff, and how long the heart pop and the like roll take.
  - `drift`, `driftTilt`: px the card rises and degrees it tilts back across the hold (linear, payoff → exit).
  - `out`: the default exit.
  - `end`: the composition length (6.5; keep the root's `data-duration` in step).

Use one sunset element per frame: the marker *or* a sunset headline, not both (v1's sunset token in the post is the same number as the headline, so it reads as one accent). The pink of the liked heart is X's own like state (`#F91880`), not the sunset accent.

notes.author: the account posting: use your own
notes.layout: the card and the headline hang on the x 72 safe line; the card sits `gap` px under the headline
notes.rollFrom: counts roll up from this fraction of their value as a short tick (452K → 486K), never from 0
notes.likeFrom: the like (the post's second beat, `likeAfter` s after the payoff): the heart fills X pink and pops, a ring and 6 dots burst, and the like count rolls up from this fraction (22K → 24K) in the same 0.35 s
notes.tickAt: after the roll, the views tick up by one unit at these moments (seconds): live, but mostly settled
notes.timing: flip: the phrase-to-headline flight (seconds); it leaves the card `flipLead` s before the payoff cut, so the cut, the flash and the chroma land as it arrives; flipBlur = px of vertical motion blur on the flight lift (v1): when the post's "90M+" turns sunset and peels off its line, before the flight drift: px the card rises (and deg it tilts back) across the hold, linear from the payoff to the exit

components.name: Headline card
components.job: A news headline card with one phrase highlighted, using real reported headlines (publication-neutral).
components.configDocs:
- `variants["0"]`
  - `plate`: the sample background clip, for preview only.
  - `top`: the card's top edge in px.
  - `tilt`: the resting angle in degrees (`0`, straight). The card lands from 2.5× this angle. Keep it within ±1, or the card leaves the safe zone during the hold push.
  - `vignette`: the stage vignette's peak opacity with `bg: "plate"`, 0–1 (`1`).
  - `maxLines`: the headline auto-fits. It starts at 76 px and steps down until it fits this many lines.
  - `keepPhrase`: `true` keeps the highlighted phrase on one line, so the marker is one bar. The headline steps down (to at most 90%) to make the phrase fit. If it still can't fit, the phrase wraps and the marker flows across the wrap.
  - `card`
    - `tag`, `source`, `date`: the meta row under the headline. Keep these publication-neutral.
    - `headline`: the exact reported headline.
    - `highlight`: an exact whole-word substring of `headline` that gets the marker. It may wrap across lines; each line then gets its own full pink→amber marker.
    - `dek`: one line under the meta row, 28 px (the same size as the meta row and credit). It steps down to 26 px to stay on one line, and wraps only if it is still too long.
      - The sample, "Out Thursday, Nov 19, on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.", is a fact, not a quote.
      - Paste the article's real dek if you have it, and never invent one in an outlet's voice.
      - Set it to `""` to drop it.
  - `thumb`: `{ src, credit }`, the 2:1 lead image (a 16:9 source is cropped to fit).
    - `src` is a `.jpg`/`.png` still. This is recommended, and the sample is `assets/stills/p05-truck-yard.jpg`. It can also be an `.mp4` that has a matching `<video class="clip thumb-src">` in the HTML (`#thumbA`).
    - `credit` is the muted line under the image. Set it to `""` to hide it.
    - Set `thumb: null` to drop the image.
- `variants["1"]`
  - `plate`: the stack's sample clip (p01, The Keys sign → marina → teal car, which stays in colour behind the stack).
  - `label`: the paper section tag on the first card.
  - `top`: the first card's top edge.
  - `gap`: the spacing between cards.
  - `maxLines`: the auto-fit limit for each card's headline (54 px, stepping down).
  - `dim`: `{ opacity, scale }`, how the earlier cards recede as each new card lands (`0.72` / `1`). `opacity` applies to the card's text (meta and headline), not the glass, so a receded card never turns see-through. Keep `scale: 1` so the receded cards stay on the same edges and text column as the payoff card and the tag. Use `{ opacity: 1, scale: 1 }` to turn it off.
  - `vignette`: the stage vignette's peak opacity with `bg: "plate"` (`0.55`, lighter than the single card's, so the footage keeps its colour behind three cards).
  - `cards[]`: up to three `{ source, date, headline, highlight, paper }` objects.
    - `highlight: ""` leaves a card unlit. The sample lights only the payoff card (cards 1 and 2 are `""`), so the stack has one rule: glass cards are context, the paper card is the point. If you light an earlier card, its marker wipes off left to right as the next card lands, so only one phrase is ever lit.
    - `paper: true` makes a card paper with ink instead of glass. Use it on the payoff card only, so the stack ends on one bright object.
    - The stack's marker covers ascenders and descenders, so a phrase with g, p or y reads cleanly on glass and on paper.
    - Add a `tag` to a card to give it a chip, but on the stack fewer repeats read cleaner. Use one date format on every card, and vary the source words ("Video report", "News video") rather than repeating one.
- `colors`: `ink`, `paper`, and `sunset` (the three gradient stops for the marker).
- `marker`
  - `pad`: the space between the glyph ink and the marker's edge in em (`0.08`), the same on both sides. It is measured from the actual ink, so a "1" or a "T" at the edge gets no extra gap.
  - `gap`: when a neighbouring word sits on the same line, the most of the ink-to-ink gap the marker may cover (`0.3`), so the word space before or after the phrase always stays visible.
- `timing`
  - `in`: when the first card starts to show (0.133 s; the single card's headline lines start rising at 0, so they are set on its first frame).
  - `reveal`: single card: how long the paper takes to grow from headline-only to full height (0.45 s).
  - `sweep`: when the single card's marker starts.
  - `every`: stack interval (0.75 s).
  - `sweepSpeed`: marker speed in px/s.
  - `wipe`: how long the previous marker takes to wipe off on the stack.
  - `hold`: peak hold push. 1.01 keeps the card and the stack inside x 72–936.
  - `out`: exit start.
  - `end`: 7.0 s.

notes.marker: marker: pad = space between the glyph ink and the marker edge, in em, the same on both sides. gap = the most of a neighbouring word space the marker may cover (share of the ink-to-ink gap), so the space stays visible. Every line of a wrapped phrase gets the full pink→amber gradient (like box-decoration-break: clone).

components.job: Reply-to-comment sticker ('Reply to @user: is the water real?') that opens a video answering it.
components.summary:
A reply-to-comment overlay for GTA 6 shorts. A viewer's question ("is the water real?") pops in within the first few frames over a lightly dimmed, blurred hold. The hold eases in over 0.18 s, so the loop is seamless. Then the hold clears and the sticker docks while your clip plays as the answer. Use it to open a "you asked, here's the answer" short, a Q&A follow-up, or any clip that settles a debate from the comments.

- **Variant 0 · Reply sticker**: a white speech-bubble sticker ("Reply to @user" + the comment in big type). It pops out of its tail at full white, then lifts into the hook zone (top third) with a slight hand-placed tilt.
- **Variant 1 · Comment stack**: three smoked-glass comments of one shared width load in as a single list. One gets picked: the others dim and soften. Its Reply pill is tapped (press and flash), fills with the sunset gradient and becomes "▶ Video reply" in ink type on that tap. As the result, the others clear and the pick grows to the full safe width (comment at about 54 px) as it drops just above the caption zone.

1080×1920, 30 fps, 6.5 s. Everything stays inside the 9:16 safe zone (x 72–936, y 230–1480).

components.name: Pre-load progress
components.job: Diegetic hook: a download bar for 'Grand Theft Auto VI' ticking 98% → 100% → 'Ready to play'. Our own neutral UI, no console or store branding.
components.summary:
A diegetic hook for GTA 6 release shorts. It shows a neutral, unbranded launcher-style download card for **Grand Theft Auto VI**.

What happens:
1. The card opens already at **97%** and ticks **98 → 99**, then holds on 99 for a beat before **100**. The holds stay live: a highlight sweeps along the fill (or a comet runs along the ring) every 0.9 s.
2. At 2.75 s the **100** slams (1.12 → 1 in 3 frames), one light sweep crosses the bar or laps the ring, and the card lands on **"Ready to play"**. The date line turns to **"Available now"** (and in Bar the kicker turns from PRE-LOAD to **INSTALLED**).
3. **Play** gets a controller-style press at 4.36 s: it scales 1 → 0.96 → 1 with an inner highlight flash. There's no mouse cursor, because GTA 6 launches on PS5 and Xbox Series only.
4. The card drops away (scale 0.97, expo.in) from 4.55 s.

Use it in the first 2–3 seconds of a release-day or pre-load short ("after 13 years of waiting…"), then cut to gameplay on the press. It's our own UI, with no console, store or Rockstar branding and no GTA VI logo.

1080×1920, 30 fps, 5.0 s. Overlay component: it works over the sample plate or as a transparent overlay.
components.configDocs:
- `game.title`: the game name on the card (`"Grand Theft Auto VI"`).
- `game.tile`: the text on the square tile (`"GTA 6"`, in our own type on the soft sunset backdrop).
- `progress`: the percent states. The card enters showing the first value, and each later value ticks in at `timing.ticks[i]`. The default is `[97, 98, 99, 100]`. Keep one more value than there are ticks.
- `variants["0"|"1"]`:
  - `plate`: the sample clip used when `bg` is `"plate"`. It must match the `src` of a `<video class="plate">`.
  - `kicker` and `kickerDone` (Bar only): the small caps label above the title while installing (`"Pre-load"`) and at 100% (`"Installed"`). A hyphen in it keeps tight spacing.
  - `sub`: the date line under the title (Bar `"Unlocks Nov 19, 2026"`, Ring `"Launches November 19, 2026"`).
  - `subDone`: what the date line turns into at 100% (`"Available now"`), so it never contradicts the Play button.
  - `status` and `done`: the label while installing (`"Installing"` / `"Downloading"`) and the label at 100% (`"Ready to play"`). Ring shows its status as "Downloading · 0:03 left".
  - `cta`: the Play button label.
  - `speedMBs` (Bar only): the demo speed in the meta row.
  - `etaStart` (both): the seconds left shown on entrance. The ETA counts down to 0:00 as the last tick lands (Bar: in the meta row; Ring: in the status line).
  - `cursor`: an optional mouse arrow, **off by default** (`show: false`) because the game is console-only at launch. If you set `show: true` (for example, for a future PC version), it waits at `rest`, glides during `timing.move` and clicks at `click`. Both are in card pixels from the card's top-left.
- `timing`:
  - `in`: card entrance.
  - `ticks`: when each later percent rolls in.
  - `step`: the fill ease per tick.
  - `live`: the cycle of the live highlight while downloading (0.9 s).
  - `done`: the 100% beat (slam, light sweep, status swap, Play state).
  - `glint`: the one ready sheen or glint.
  - `click`: the press.
  - `move`: the optional cursor's glide (only used when `cursor.show` is true).
  - `out`: when the card starts to drop away.
  - `end`: clip end. If you change `end`, also change `data-duration` on `#root`, `#plateA` and `#ov`.

notes.game: the game on the card; written in our own type, no logo, no store or console branding
notes.progress: percent states: the card enters already showing the first value, then each later value ticks in at timing.ticks[i]
notes.timing: in: card entrance · ticks: when 98 / 99 / 100 roll in · step: fill ease per tick · live: highlight cycle while downloading done: 100% lands (numeral slam, light sweep, status swap, Play state) · glint: one ready sheen across Play / the ring click: Play is pressed (scale 1 -> .96 -> 1 + inner flash) · move: optional cursor glide · out: card drops away · end: clip end

components.name: Phone message
components.job: In-game style phone: a text from Lucia slides in as a notification or a short thread.
components.summary:
An in-game-style phone moment: a text from Lucia lands on screen. Use it when a short needs a story beat between clips, for example "Lucia when the pre-load finishes", a release-eve hook, a "who's texting Jason" meme cut, or a setup line before a mission clip. 1080×1920, 30 fps, 7 s, and it loops clean (in at 0.08 s, out by 6.9 s). The first words are readable by about 0.3 s (v0) and 0.65 s (v1).

| Variant | What it shows | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| `0` Notification | Each text drops in as its own smoked-glass banner with a haptic nudge (0.08 s, 2.0 s, 3.8 s). Older banners step back into a visible stack under the newest one. | A quick hook over any clip. It sits in the upper third and leaves the footage clear. |
| `1` Thread | A handset rises into frame. Lucia types ("…" dots), you type a reply in the composer and send it (a sunset bubble plus "Delivered"), she answers, and then she starts typing again until the exit. | A 5–7 s story beat. The phone carries the frame. |
components.configDocs:
- `contact.name`, `contact.subtitle`: the name on the banner or header, and the line under it in the thread header ("Vice City").
- `contact.avatar`: a square image (default `assets/avatar/lucia.jpg`, a still from the sample trailer plate). Set it to `""` for a sunset monogram that uses `contact.initial`.
- `contact.carrier`: the fictional in-world network tag (default "Leonida", shown in wide-tracked caps). It appears as "LEONIDA · NOW" on the banner and after the clock in the thread's status bar. Set it to `""` to hide it.
- `variants["0"].messages`: one to four strings, one banner each. The first lands at `timing.in`, the second at `timing.second`, and each later one `timing.next` seconds after that. Keep each to about 40 characters (two lines). `time` is the label after the carrier tag ("now").
- `variants["1"].messages`: an array of `{ from: "them" | "me", text }`. Her texts get a typing indicator for `timing.typing` seconds. Yours are typed into the composer at `timing.cps` characters per second, then sent. Four messages fit the 7 s timeline. Keep each to one line (about 24 characters).
- `variants["1"].statusTime`, `stamp`, `placeholder`, `delivered`: the status-bar clock, the date chip above the thread, the empty-composer text, and the receipt under your last text.
- `variants["1"].typingAfter`: `true` shows her typing again after the last message, so the final hold stays alive.
- `variants[*].plate`: the sample footage path (used only when `bg` is `"plate"`).
- `timing` (seconds unless noted): `in` is the first motion; `second` and `next` time the Notification banners; `typingAt`, `typing` and `read` set when the first typing bubble appears, how long the dots show and the pause after each of her texts; `cps` is your typing speed in characters per second; `out` is when the exit starts; `end` is the end of the clip.

messages: Pre-load's done. You ready for tomorrow?
Nov 19. Vice City. Just you and me.
I'm outside. Don't keep me waiting.

components.name: Minimap route
components.job: A rounded translucent minimap (abstract roads) where a GPS route draws to the destination blip.
components.summary: A rounded, translucent minimap with abstract roads. A GPS route in the Leonida sunset gradient draws from the player arrow to a destination blip. It is 1080×1920, 30 fps and 7 s, and works as a transparent overlay.

components.name: Mission objective
components.job: Mission objective text ('Go to the Vice City Marina.') with the keyword accented; or a mission title card.
components.summary:
The GTA "what to do next" beat for a GTA 6 short. Use it when a clip needs a goal on screen: the start of a challenge ("Go to the Vice City Marina."), a "mission" framing for a story edit, or a chapter break styled like the game's own mission title.

- **Variant 0 · Objective line:** the in-game objective box at the top left. It is a square-cornered (8 px), warm frosted HUD panel holding:
  - a wide-tracked "LEONIDA" label;
  - a distance readout;
  - a hollow diamond bullet before the objective line.

  The keyword is filled with the Leonida sunset gradient. The distance counts down ("1.4 MI" → "0.0 MI"). At `timing.arrive` (5.05 s) it swaps to **ARRIVED** at full white. The diamond fills with a quick pop and the panel's hairline catches one sheen: the "you're there" payoff. On exit the panel fades and slides out to the left.
- **Variant 1 · Mission title:** a centred lockup in the upper third (y 380–660). A wide-tracked "LEONIDA" label sits over a big condensed "VICE CITY" title. The sunset sweeps across the title at ~0.8–1.2 s, and the first objective sits right under it in plain white.
  - At `timing.handoff` (3.7 s) the title drains back to white and clears, as the game does.
  - While it fades, the objective glides up under the label, its diamond draws, and it grows to 72 px. The keyword sweep then lands as the payoff (~4.5 s).
  - The card resolves into "LEONIDA / ◇ Go to the Vice City Marina." A light vignette sits behind it in both background modes, so the type holds on bright footage.
  - Only one thing carries the sunset at a time: the title, then the keyword.

1080×1920, 30 fps, 7 s. Clears by 6.7 s so it loops.
components.configDocs:
| Field | Variant | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `plate` | both | Sample footage shown when `bg` is `"plate"`. |
| `layout` | both | `"card"` (objective HUD panel, top left) or `"title"` (mission title lockup, upper third). |
| `mission` | 0 | Wide-tracked label above the objective (same style as variant 1's `label`). `""` hides it. |
| `objective` | both | The objective sentence. Wrap the keyword in `[brackets]`; it gets the sunset fill. Long lines wrap inside the card. In variant 1, `""` hides the row (and there is no handoff). |
| `distance` | 0 | `{ from, to, unit }`: the readout counts from `from` to `to`, reaching it 0.3 s before `timing.arrive`. It shows in caps, e.g. "1.2 MI" (use `"km"` for metric). `null` hides it; the diamond still fills at arrival. |
| `arrived` | 0 | Word the readout swaps to at `timing.arrive`, e.g. "Arrived". `""` keeps the final number. |
| `label` | 1 | White wide-tracked label above the title, e.g. a region, "Mission 1" or "Chapter 3". |
| `title` | 1 | Mission title. Carries the sunset until the handoff. Starts at 150 px and auto-fits down to `titleMaxWidth` (792 px). |
| `handoffMaxPx` | 1 | Largest font size the objective grows to at the handoff (72). |
| `accent` | both | The three sunset stops: on the keyword (v0), on the title and then the keyword (v1). |
| `timing` | both | `in`: entrance start. `arrive` (v0): the readout swaps to `arrived` and the diamond fills. `handoff` (v1): the title drains and clears, and the objective takes its place and its keyword sweeps; `null` keeps the full lockup with the accent on the title. `out`: exit start. `end`: clip length. |

notes.accent: Leonida sunset core: one thing per frame (v0 keyword; v1 title, then keyword)
notes.titleMaxWidth: px; keeps the centred title inside x 144–936
notes.handoffMaxPx: v1: the objective grows to at most this font size at the handoff
notes.timing: in: entrance · arrive (v0): readout swaps to "Arrived", diamond fills · handoff (v1): title drains to white and clears, the objective takes its place and its keyword sweeps (null keeps the full lockup) · out: exit · end: clip length

components.name: Cash payout
components.job: Money rolls up (+$1,250,000) for heist/payout moments.
components.summary:
Money rolls up for the payoff of a heist, a big sale or any "how much did that make" moment in a GTA 6 short. The count rushes from the first frame: the low digits flicker, the top digits tick up into place, and the total stops dead on an exact frame. That frame gets the hit (flash and punch), never before it.

- **Variant 0, HUD corner.** A game-HUD wallet in the top-right corner: the balance in white condensed numerals, a teal `+$1,250,000` line under it with a bold "HEIST PAYOUT" label, then the balance rolls up and flashes teal on the frame it is credited (2.0 s). Use it over gameplay or trailer footage when you want the "real game" feel.
- **Variant 1, Centre card.** A smoked-glass payout card in the upper half: caps label and place, a big numeral that grows from a centred `$0`, a Leonida-sunset progress rule that fills in sync, a punch and sheen on the landing frame (2.1 s), and a crew split row (Jason / Lucia) that the card expands to reveal. Use it as the headline beat of a "biggest heist payout" or "how much money" short.

Both work as transparent overlays (`bg: "none"`). Length 5.5 s; everything clears by 5.1 s so it loops cleanly.
components.configDocs:
| Field | Variant | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `currency` | both | Currency symbol, default `"$"` |
| `variants["0"].plate` | 0 | Sample footage under the HUD (only with `bg: "plate"`) |
| `variants["0"].balanceFrom` | 0 | Wallet balance before the payout (12500) |
| `variants["0"].payout` | 0 | Amount credited; shown as `+$1,250,000` and added to the balance |
| `variants["0"].label` | 0 | Small caps label beside the `+$` line; `""` hides it |
| `variants["0"].accent` | 0 | Colour of the `+$` line and the credited flash (Vice teal `#2EC4B6`) |
| `variants["1"].plate` | 1 | Sample footage under the card |
| `variants["1"].payout` | 1 | The number the card rolls up to (from a centred `$0`) |
| `variants["1"].label` / `place` | 1 | Top-left label and top-right place; `place: ""` hides it |
| `variants["1"].split` | 1 | `[{ name, amount }, ...]` crew split revealed on landing; `[]` hides the row |
| `timing.*` | both | `in`, `delta`, `count` + `countDur` (V0), `cardCount` + `cardCountDur` (V1), `deltaOut`, `out`, `end` |
| `timing.rush` | both | Roll ease strength (normalised exponential ease-out, default 9). Higher means the top digits settle earlier. It always stops dead on the total. |

The hit fires at `count + countDur` (V0) and `cardCount + cardCountDur` (V1). Keep those sums on the 1/30 s grid (e.g. 0.5 + 1.5) so the flash lands on the same frame as the final value.

The numeral auto-fits the card, so 6- to 8-digit payouts all fit. Digit counts and commas come from the numbers themselves.

notes.timing: keep count + countDur on the 1/30 s frame grid so the hit lands on a real frame

components.name: Race HUD
components.job: Racing overlay in Rockstar's sparse style: LAP 1/2, position 3/8, a ticking timer; or a speedometer.
components.summary:
A racing overlay in the style of Rockstar's own GTA 6 race HUD: sparse white condensed numerals with the official thin dark edge, ink-navy chips, one Leonida-pink accent. The race stack sits in the bottom-right corner of the safe zone, where the game puts it. The speedometer sits low and just left of centre, so that on the sample chase its ring clears the game's own aim reticle (you can move it, see `layout` below).

**When to use it in a GTA 6 short:**
- Over race, chase or driving clips to make edited footage read as "in-game".
- For "street race in Vice City" moments, overtake clips, top-speed runs and car reviews.
- As a transparent overlay (`bg: "none"`) on your own gameplay or live-action clips, for the "real-life GTA" format.
components.configDocs:
- `variants["0"]` (Race stack)
  - `lap.label`, `lap.total`: the LAP row (`LAP 1/2`).
  - `lap.steps`: the laps shown in order, e.g. `[1, 2]`. `lap.at`: the time (s) of each lap change, one fewer entry than `steps` (default `[4.2]`). Use `steps: [1]` and `at: []` for no lap change.
  - `position.total`: field size (`/8`).
  - `position.steps`: the positions shown in order, e.g. `[5, 4, 3]`.
  - `position.at`: the time (s) of each overtake; one fewer entry than `steps`.
  - `timer.startSec`: what the timer reads when it appears (46.20 → `00:46.20`); it then ticks in real time.
  - `timer.from`: the second the timer starts ticking.
- `variants["1"]` (Speedometer)
  - `layout`: this variant's own position, which overrides the shared `layout` (default `{ right: 366, bottom: 450 }`: gauge centre x 460, y 1216, so the ring clears the sample chase's aim reticle). On your own clip, `{ right: 144, bottom: 480 }` puts it in the bottom-right corner like the race stack.
  - `unit`: `"MPH"` (or `"KM/H"`), `max`: the top of the dial (140), `tickEvery`: tick spacing (20, which gives 8 ticks).
  - `speed`: `[time, speed]` keyframes (default 24 → 138 mph). Each short dip is a gear change. Eased per segment. The unit label and the numeral are centred in the ring as one row. The numeral always uses 3 digit cells, and a leading zero is ghosted, so the row never shifts when the speed passes 100. The arc's colour runs pink → orange → amber up to the highest speed in this list, so the tip always ends warm. Match the numbers to your footage: a crawl shouldn't read 140.
  - `gears`: `[time, gear]` pairs (default 2 → 6, shifts at 1.25 / 2.5 / 3.95 / 5.6 s). At each time the chip rolls and flashes pink. Put each shift inside a speed dip.
  - `gearLabel`: `"GEAR"`.
- `variants[...].plates`: ids of the sample-footage clips shown under that variant.
- `accent`: the single accent colour (Leonida pink `#F84FA4`). It's used for the keyline, the overtake / lap / gear-shift flash and the start of the speed arc.
- `flashHold`, `finalHold`: how many frames the pink event fill holds before it wipes out (2), and the hold for the last event of the run (3: the final-lap flip or the last gear shift).
- `flash`: wipe-in and wipe-out time (s) of the overtake and lap flash (0.16 / 0.16). `gearFlash`: the quicker gear-shift flash (0.07 / 0.09, about 0.25 s of pink in all).
- `layout.right`, `layout.bottom`: distance of the HUD from the right and bottom edges (default 144 / 480, so the race stack's corner sits at x 936, y 1440). `layout.scale`: scales the whole HUD. A variant's own `layout` (the speedometer has one) overrides these.
- `scrim`: strength of the soft dark corner shade behind the HUD over the sample footage (0.45; 0 turns it off). `scrimNone`: the shade in the transparent export (0 by default, because the dark type edge already holds the HUD on bright footage; raise it to about 0.3 if your clip is very bright).
- `timing.in`, `timing.out`, `timing.outDur`, `timing.end`: entrance start (0.08 s, so the full HUD reads by about 0.45 s), exit start, exit length, total length (6.5 s).

notes.flashHold: frames the pink event fill holds before it wipes out; the last event (final lap / 5 -> 6 shift) holds 3
notes.flash: pink wipe-in / wipe-out (s) for the overtake and lap flash
notes.gearFlash: the gear-shift flash is quicker (about 0.25 s in all), so the pink chip and the sunset arc barely overlap
notes.accent: Leonida pink: the keylines, the event wipe, the start of the speed arc
notes.layout: right/bottom edge in px (x 936, y 1440), whole HUD scale; a variant's own layout overrides it
notes.scrim: corner shade behind the HUD over the sample footage, 0 = off
notes.scrimNone: transparent (bg "none") export: no shade, the dark type edge carries legibility

components.name: Character intro
components.job: Freeze-frame character intro: 'LUCIA CAMINOS' with a role line; or a character switch wheel.
components.summary:
A full-frame character intro for GTA 6 shorts, 1080×1920, 5.5 s, built in HyperFrames. It always shows footage, taken from the clip paths in CONFIG.

- **Variant 0, "Freeze + name":** the clip plays, then freezes hard on the character: a warm 2-frame flash, a 4-frame shake, a punch-in and a 2-frame grade snap. A big two-line name lands: LUCIA in white and CAMINOS in the Leonida sunset gradient, with one sheen pass, an index row (`01 / 02`) and a role line (`PROTAGONIST · LEONIDA`). The still keeps pushing in (1.06 to 1.14) for a 2.8 s hold, then the name leaves and the footage resumes before the loop.
- **Variant 1, "Switch wheel":**
  - A smoked-glass switch wheel opens over the current character, reading **PLAYING AS / JASON / DUVAL**, and the footage drops to slow motion.
  - The sunset selection arc travels over the top of the wheel to LUCIA, and the centre rolls to **SWITCH TO / LUCIA / CAMINOS**.
  - On confirm, the plate punches 1 to 1.6 into a blur and hard-cuts on a warm 2-frame flash to the new character, who lands 1.25 to 1.
  - The selected portrait then flies up into a **PLAYING AS / LUCIA CAMINOS** HUD chip.

**When to use it:** the first time a character appears in a compilation ("meet Lucia"), at a segment change between the two protagonists, or in "who would you play first" and character-explainer shorts.
components.configDocs:
`CONFIG` is defined in a `<script>` in `<head>`.

- `duration`: total length in seconds (5.5). It must match `data-duration` on `#root` and `#ov`.
- `freeze.clip`: the clip path for variant 0. It must match every `<video data-cfg="freeze">` src; the script re-applies it.
- `freeze.clipStart`: the second in the clip where playback starts (`data-media-start` of `#v0play`).
- `freeze.freezeAt`: the composition second the picture freezes. The frozen source frame is `clipStart + freezeAt`, which must equal `data-media-start` on the hold and resume tags.
- `freeze.resumeAt` (3.9): when the footage plays again; the overlay is gone by `resumeAt + 0.45`.
  - The hold chain (`#v0hold00..09`: 0.3 s clips, then a final 0.1 s one) must cover `freezeAt` to `resumeAt` exactly.
  - `#v0resume` starts at `resumeAt`.
- `freeze.index`, `freeze.first`, `freeze.last`, `freeze.role`: the text. `last` carries the gradient.
- `freeze.nameSize` (236): the name size. It auto-shrinks so the name fits within `maxWidth` (864, x 72–936).
- `freeze.top`: the y of the index row.
- `freeze.pushOrigin`: where the punch-in aims (the face).
- `wheel.open`, `wheel.select`, `wheel.confirm`, `wheel.out`: the beat times (0.3 / 1.1 / 2.6 / 5.05).
  - The hard cut lands at `confirm + 0.3`; keep it on a frame boundary (2.9 s = frame 87).
  - `#v1lu` should start about 0.1 s before the cut.
- `wheel.playing` ("PLAYING AS"): the kicker while the current character is selected, and the HUD chip label after the switch.
- `wheel.kicker` ("SWITCH TO"): the kicker once the selector reaches the new character.
- `wheel.from` and `wheel.to`: each has `first`, `last`, `plate` (the main footage) and `portrait`:
  - `portrait.clip`;
  - `fx`, `fy`: the face centre in source pixels of a 1080×1920 clip;
  - `span`: how many source pixels fit across the 220 px portrait.

components.name: Follow CTA
components.job: End-of-short CTA: 'Follow for Part 2' with a follow button press, or a next-part card.
components.summary:
The last 5–7 seconds of a GTA 6 short: ask the viewer to follow for Part 2, or hand them straight to the next part. It is a clean overlay, centred on the frame and inside the 9:16 safe zone (x 144–936, y 300–1340), so it drops onto any end clip.

- **Variant 0 · Follow button.** "THANKS FOR WATCHING / FOLLOW FOR PART 2" (Part 2 in the sunset gradient) over a smoked-glass profile card: an avatar monogram with a TikTok-style "+" follow badge, your handle, a one-line pitch and a full-width white **Follow** pill. At 1.5 s a touch indicator presses the button (to the right of the label). On release, the app's grey-glass **✓ Following** state wipes out from the tap point as one opaque circle, with no crossfade, and only the check and the avatar badge turn teal. At 2.6 s the pitch line changes to "Part 2 drops on my page". At 3.2 s a white underline sweeps under your handle and a ↓ arrow under the card starts bobbing toward your handle in the app UI. Use it when Part 2 isn't posted yet.
- **Variant 1 · Next part card.** "END OF PART 1 / PART 2 IS UP NEXT" over an ink-navy (#1F202B) end tile. The tile holds a 16:9 preview clip of the next part with a "NEXT" chip and a glass play button, your handle, an "ON MY PAGE ↓" route line, the next video's title and a 12 px sunset progress bar, which is the only countdown. When the bar fills, the chip wipes to a white **OUT NOW**, the play button pulses once (it keeps the play icon: nothing pretends to autoplay), the preview brightens slightly, and your handle and the route light up from 62% to 100% white while the arrow bobs twice. Use it when Part 2 is already live on your page.

Timing: entrance 0.15–1.2 s. v0 presses at 1.5 s, changes the pitch line at 2.6 s, and starts the handle underline and arrow at 3.2 s. v1 counts down 0.9–4.9 s and holds OUT NOW 4.9–6.55 s. Clean exit 6.55–6.9 s, 7.0 s total, so it loops.
components.configDocs:
| Field | Variant | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `handle` | both | Channel handle shown on the card (`@everestchris6`). |
| `plate` | both | Sample footage under the overlay; must match a `<video class="plate">` src. |
| `kicker` | both | Small wide-tracked line above the headline. |
| `headline` | both | Two headline lines. In v0, line 2 carries the sunset gradient. |
| `avatar` | 0 | Monogram inside the avatar circle (2 letters). |
| `sub` | 0 | One-line pitch under the handle (before the press). |
| `subDone` / `subDoneAt` | 0 | The line that replaces `sub` after the follow lands ("Part 2 drops on my page") and when (s). |
| `routeAt` | 0 | When the handle underline sweeps and the ↓ arrow under the card starts bobbing (s). |
| `button` / `buttonDone` | 0 | Button label before and after the press. |
| `tap.x` / `tap.at` | 0 | Tap point across the button (0–1; keep it right of the label, default 0.84) and press time in seconds. The Following wipe grows from this point. |
| `thumb` | 1 | Preview clip of the next part. The script sets it on `#thumbClip` at load, so CONFIG is the only place to change it. |
| `chip` / `chipDone` | 1 | Thumbnail chip label during ("Next") and after ("Out now", white chip) the countdown. |
| `route` | 1 | Where Part 2 lives ("On my page"), shown with a down arrow that points at your handle in the app UI. |
| `title` | 1 | Next video's title (2 lines max at 44 px). |
| `countFrom` / `countStart` | 1 | Countdown length (s) for the sunset bar, and its start time. |
| `timing.in/out/end` | both | Entrance start, exit start, composition end. |

components.name: End card
components.job: Closing card in Rockstar's end-tile language: ink-navy tile, wide-tracked date line, channel name.
components.summary:
The closing card of a GTA 6 short, in Rockstar's end-tile language. Your last shot stays full-width, and nothing is boxed. One solid tile slides over it, and every line of type sits on that clean tile. The release date tracks in as wide-tracked caps, and your channel name rises in, paired with a small fan-edit line like the legal line on Rockstar's own end tiles. Each frame has one accent. In v0 it is Rockstar's crisp right-side magenta offset on the two-line date. In v1 it is the sunset sky itself.

**When to use it in a GTA 6 short:** as the last 2–4 seconds of any GTA 6 short (a trailer breakdown, a "things you missed", a countdown, a compilation). It turns your final clip into a branded sign-off with the date viewers care about.
- Use variant 0 for night, moody or neon edits, or any time you want the closest match to Rockstar's own ink end tile.
- Use variant 1 for warm, golden-hour or "hype" edits.

Type starts at 0.38 s in v0 and at 0.32 s in v1, so the first line arrives as the tile lands, and the channel name has landed by about 1.2 s. At 6.3 s the type clears and the tile slides away, so the last frame is your clip at full frame and the card loops cleanly.

- 1080x1920, 30 fps, 7 s. Footage always shows, because this is a full-frame component.
- Variables:
  - `variant`: `"0"` Ink tile + date, `"1"` Sunset card.
  - `bg`: kept for library consistency. This component always shows its CONFIG clip.

| Variant | Tile | Type (3 sizes per frame) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 Ink tile + date | A flat ink-navy `#1F202B` tile rises from the bottom. The footage is clear above y 860, and a 120 px seam makes the ink solid by y 980 | Two tight pairs, centred in the ink between y 980 and 1480. First, Rockstar's two-line date card: the date is Inter 700, 58 px caps tracked 0.21em, with a crisp 3px/2px `#EE08F2` magenta offset and a faint bloom, so it is the heaviest thing on screen. Under it, "SEE YOU IN LEONIDA" is Inter 600, 40 px, tracked 0.24em, with the same offset. Then the sign-off: the channel name (Inter 600, 40 px) over the 28 px fine print |
| 1 Sunset card | The tile is the sunset: plum `#2C1446` to `#6B2A6E` to rose `#C9566F` to peach `#F08A62`, falling from the top. It ends in a hard horizon at y 760: a 2 px peach hairline on its last rows, with clear footage straight below | Two groups. First, "SEE YOU IN" (28 px tracked) over "VICE CITY" (Inter 700, 136 px, tracked 0.10em, about 73% of the frame width, with a soft plum shadow and no magenta) over the tracked date (28 px). Then, after about 100 px of air, the channel name (40 px) and the fine print (28 px, 82% white so it holds on the rose part of the sky) |
components.configDocs:
| Field | What it does |
|---|---|
| `channel` | Channel name that signs off the card (both variants), e.g. `@everestchris6` |
| `finePrint` | Small legal-style line. `""` hides it |
| `variants["N"].style` | `"ink"` (navy tile) or `"sunset"` (the sunset-sky tile) |
| `variants["N"].clip` | Path of the clip the card plays over |
| `variants["0"].date`, `.line2` | Date line and the second line under it (typed in normal case; both shown as tracked caps with the magenta offset) |
| `variants["1"].eyebrow`, `.title`, `.date` | Small tracked line, big title, and tracked date line |
| `variants["N"].veil.from` | `"bottom"` (tile rises, footage on top) or `"top"` (tile falls, footage below) |
| `variants["N"].veil.edge`, `.fade` | `edge`: the y (px) where clear footage starts. `fade`: how long the soft seam into the tile is. v0 uses a 120 px seam. v1 uses `0`, a hard edge, which is its horizon. In v1 the 2 px horizon hairline is drawn automatically on the tile's last two solid rows (`edge - fade - 2`). Keep the type off any seam |
| `variants["N"].shot.focus` | `[x, y]` point of your clip (0–1), e.g. a face, that should sit in the clear footage |
| `variants["N"].shot.to` | The y (px) where that point settles once the tile is in. The move is clamped so the clip's edge always stays under the tile. Keep it a little below the clamp (v1 uses 1110, which leaves a 72 px margin) so the clip's top rows stay hidden |
| `variants["N"].shot.push` | Slow push-in while the card holds (`0.05` = 5%) |
| `variants["N"].layout` | Top (px) of each text line. Keep text between y 230 and 1480, and on solid tile (above `edge - fade` in v1, below `edge + fade` in v0) |
| `variants["N"].timing` | Optional per-variant overrides of any `timing` field. v1 sets `{ type: 0.32 }`, so its title rises while the tile lands |
| `timing.tile`, `.tileDur` | When the tile starts sliding over the footage, and how long it takes |
| `timing.shot`, `.shotDur` | When the footage starts settling, and how long it takes. Keep it starting after `tile` |
| `timing.type`, `.step` | When the first text line lands (0.38 s), and the gap between lines (one line leads at a time) |
| `timing.out`, `.reopen`, `.end` | When the type clears, when the tile slides away again, and the total length |

Colours are CSS tokens at the top of the `<style>` block: `--ink-navy`, `--magenta`, `--sunset-sky` (the v1 tile gradient) and `--sunset-horizon` (the v1 horizon hairline). Type sizes, the magenta offset shadows (v0 date and line 2) and the v1 title's soft shadow are in the CSS rules below them. If you change the v0 date's shadow, also change `BLOOM_ON` in the script, which is the value it ramps to. The v1 title is at the largest size that keeps its ink inside the x 936 safe edge, so if you type a longer title, lower its `font-size`.

variants.label: Ink tile + date / Sunset card
variants.kindEvidence: Full-frame component: it always shows footage

notes.channel: the channel that signs off the short (both variants)
notes.finePrint: small legal-style line, like the fine print on Rockstar's end tiles. "" hides it.
notes.timing: tile = tile starts sliding over the footage; shot = footage settles; type = first line; step = gap between lines out = type clears; reopen = tile slides away again; end = total
